Cursor
std:sql.documentation:
An owned row cursor borrowing its Pool. Obtain it with await db.cursor(sql, parameters); await cursor.next() yields one owned Row or undefined at EOF. Close or drop it to release its pending result stream. This is client-side row streaming, not a named server cursor or a transaction snapshot.

```tsrust
const cursor = await db.cursor('SELECT 1 AS value');
const row = await cursor.next(); // Row with value 1
cursor.close();
```

Ownership: cannot clone or outlive its pool. Each pending next() exclusively borrows the cursor.

SqlPool.name: migrate

parameters.label: directory: string
parameters.documentation: Trusted migration directory, relative to the process working directory or absolute. Ship these files with your service. Direct .sql files must have unique positive signed-64-bit VERSION_description.sql names.

SqlPool.documentation:
Applies pending forward migrations in version order and checks applied SQL checksums. Returns void when complete; repeating the same directory is a no-op. Uses the _sqlx_migrations ledger, PostgreSQL/MySQL advisory locks and SQLite per-migration transactions. Use one deployment migration owner. Read the directory when awaited. Non-.sql entries are ignored; nested directories are not traversed. Empty SQL, duplicate/nonpositive versions, reversible .up/.down files and -- no-transaction files reject with migration-source. In-memory and temporary SQLite databases are unsupported. Missing or changed applied SQL throws migration-drift; unfinished MySQL migrations throw migration-dirty; database execution throws migration-failed. Other connection errors retain their ordinary SqlError codes. PostgreSQL/SQLite roll back each failed migration; MySQL DDL may persist partially and requires operator recovery. Cancellation closes the migration connection through tracked cleanup. Do not run migrations during request serving.

```tsrust
await pool.migrate('examples/sql-migrations/migrations');
await pool.migrate('examples/sql-migrations/migrations'); // already applied
```

Checksums detect migration history changes, not out-of-band schema edits. Verify required columns with a startup query. Files are trusted deployment code, may contain multiple statements, and are not automatically packaged. No down migration, automatic repair, or cross-driver SQL translation is provided. Trusted scripts must not issue transaction/session control or modify the migration ledger.

Ownership: borrows the pool until completion or cancellation; no SQL row or resource escapes the migration connection.

SqlPool.documentation:
Opens a cursor without collecting all result rows. Uses the same prepared parameter checks and driver-specific SQL as query(). Parameters default to []. Creation validates SQL and parameter metadata; next() starts the result stream and acquires its connection. Metadata preparation and streaming may use different connections from the same pool. Rows are yielded in database result order. Use ORDER BY when order matters. Database/parameter errors throw SqlError; errors during execution can appear at next(). Driver buffering remains in effect; application code retains only rows it chooses to keep. SQL may perform writes with RETURNING; closing or dropping a cursor does not roll them back. ```

Ownership: the returned cursor borrows the pool until close/drop. SQL text and parameter values are retained as owned query data; no caller parameter loan escapes.

parameters.documentation: One SQL statement with positional placeholders; no raw transaction control.

SqliteConnection.documentation:
Prepares exactly one SQL statement without executing it. sql is UTF-8 SQL; bind data with ?1, ?2 placeholders. Rejects syntax errors, multiple statements and SQL transaction/savepoint commands. Returns Result with SqliteError on failure; unwrap propagates the error to try/catch.


Ownership: the statement borrows this handle until finalized or its scope ends. It prevents closing the connection or finishing the transaction.


Ownership: consumes the connection. Cannot close while statements or a transaction borrow it; scope exit also closes automatically.

SqliteTransaction.name: commit
SqliteTransaction.documentation:
Commits all changes in this transaction. Deferred constraint or lock failures return SqliteError and trigger rollback. If SQLite already aborted the transaction, returns transaction-ended. No arguments or success value.

```tsrust
unwrap(tx.commit());
```

Ownership: consumes the transaction and releases its exclusive connection borrow. All its statements must be released first.

SqliteTransaction.name: rollback
SqliteTransaction.documentation:
Discards all changes in this transaction; succeeds if SQLite already rolled it back. Rollback failure returns SqliteError and prevents further connection operations except close. No arguments or success value.

```tsrust

```

Ownership: consumes the transaction. All statements must be released first. Scope exit and errors also roll back automatically.

std:futures.name: delay

parameters.label: milliseconds: int
parameters.documentation: Creates a lazy timer. Awaiting waits without blocking a worker thread. milliseconds is an integer from 0 through 31536000000; zero imposes no positive delay. Invalid values throw AsyncError code range when awaited. No receiver mutation.

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a lazy timer. Awaiting waits without blocking a worker thread. milliseconds is an integer from 0 through 31536000000; zero imposes no positive delay. Invalid values throw AsyncError code range when awaited. No receiver mutation.

```tsrust
await delay(10); // waits at least 10 ms
```

Ownership: uniquely owned task; await once or transfer it.

examples.source: import {delay} from 'std:futures'; async function main():Task<void>{await delay(1); console.log('ready');}

std:futures.name: yield
std:futures.documentation:
Gives the scheduler a chance to run other ready tasks when awaited. Resumes without a fixed delay; another task is not guaranteed to run first. Acts on the task executing await; it cannot pause another job or choose which task runs next. Calling yield() alone does nothing until awaited. Usually unnecessary when already awaiting timers or channel operations. Takes no arguments and returns no value. No receiver mutation or ordinary failures.

```tsrust
await yield(); // resume after yielding to the scheduler
```

Ownership: consumes the task once.

std:futures.name: race

parameters.label: inputs: (Task<T> | Job<T, E>)[]
parameters.documentation: Creates a lazy race over an owned array. Lazy inputs begin together when awaited; started jobs continue running. First completion, including failure, wins. Ready ties prefer input order. Cancels remaining work and waits for cleanup before returning. Empty input throws AsyncError code empty. Every input must have the same result type. Worker failures retain their typed cause. No input array mutation is visible after transfer.

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a lazy race over an owned array. Lazy inputs begin together when awaited; started jobs continue running. First completion, including failure, wins. Ready ties prefer input order. Cancels remaining work and waits for cleanup before returning. Empty input throws AsyncError code empty. Every input must have the same result type. Mix tasks and jobs in an array literal at the call; stored arrays hold one input type. Worker failures retain their typed cause. No input array mutation is visible after transfer.

```tsrust
const result = await race([slow(), fast().start()]);
```

Ownership: consumes the array and every input. Started-job settlement obligations remain active inside the returned task. Cancelling a parent drains its children.

examples.source: import {race,allSettled} from 'std:futures';async function value(n:int):Task<int>{return n;}async function main():Task<void>{console.log(await race([value(1),value(2)]));const results=await allSettled([value(3),value(4).start()]);for(const result of results){console.log(unwrap(clone(result)));}}

parameters.label: inputs: (Task<T> | Job<T, E>)[]
parameters.documentation: Creates a lazy group that waits for every outcome, including failures, in input order. Lazy inputs begin together when awaited; started jobs continue running. Empty input returns an empty array. All inputs need the same result type. A failure does not cancel siblings. Errors carry code and optional typed cause.

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a lazy group that waits for every outcome, including failures, in input order. Lazy inputs begin together when awaited; started jobs continue running. Empty input returns an empty array. All inputs need the same result type. Mix tasks and jobs in an array literal at the call; stored arrays hold one input type. A failure does not cancel siblings. std:futures.name: Channel

parameters.label: capacity: int
parameters.documentation: Creates a bounded async channel. capacity is the maximum number of queued messages, 1..1000000; invalid capacity throws RangeError. A full channel makes send wait without blocking a worker. receive waits for a message. close rejects further sends while allowing queued messages to drain. Each message moves to one receiver.

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a bounded async channel. capacity is the maximum number of queued messages, 1..1000000; invalid capacity throws RangeError. A full channel makes send wait without blocking a worker. receive waits for a message. close rejects further sends while allowing queued messages to drain. Each message moves to one receiver.

```tsrust
const queue = new Channel<int>(2); await queue.send(42); console.log(await queue.receive()); // 42
```

Ownership: unique channel owner; sender() creates an owned sending endpoint. Messages must be owned transferable data without endpoints or jobs.

TaskMethods.name: start
TaskMethods.documentation:
Schedules this task on the async runtime and immediately returns its unique job handle. Takes no arguments. The task may execute before start returns. Inputs and completion must own transferable data; caller borrows cannot cross scheduling. Call inside an async function.

```tsrust

```

Ownership: consumes this task. The returned job must be settled; no implicit detach.

Completed work wins if ready when polled.

Job.name: cancel
Job.documentation:
Requests cancellation of this job. Returns true only for the first request that wins before completion; repeated requests or completed work return false. Cancellation is observed at a scheduling point, so synchronous blocking code is not forcibly interrupted. No arguments or defaults.


AsyncChannel.name: close

std:threads.name: spawnScoped
std:threads.signature: spawnScoped(callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>): Result<ScopedThread<T, E>, SpawnError>
std:threads.inferredSignature: function spawnScoped(callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>): Result<ScopedThread<T, E>, SpawnError>

parameters.label: callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>
parameters.documentation: Starts one OS thread immediately and registers fallback joining with the returned owner. The callback runs once with zero arguments or one TaskContext; T is its return type and E its inferred thrown payload, or undefined. Returns Ok with a scoped handle or Err with code spawn and an OS message. Failed creation disposes the callback. No options or defaults. Leaving the owning scope waits for an unsettled worker, including on return or error. Moving the handle transfers cleanup responsibility. Fallback cleanup discards completion values and failures; use join to observe them. Cleanup never replaces a pending caller error, and can wait indefinitely for a worker that never finishes.

examples.source: import {spawnScoped,join} from 'std:threads';import {unwrap} from 'std:result';function main(){const first=unwrap(spawnScoped(():int=>20));const second=unwrap(spawnScoped(():int=>22));const a=unwrap(join(first));const b=unwrap(join(second));console.log(a+b);}

std:threads.name: ScopedThread
std:threads.documentation:
Compatibility spelling. Prefer Thread: both handle types join during owner cleanup.

An opaque, uniquely owned worker handle with fallback joining at the end of its owning scope. No fields, constructors or arguments. Obtain it from spawnScoped. Use join to collect its result or detach to explicitly stop waiting. Moving it transfers cleanup responsibility. Fallback cleanup waits and discards the completion, including failures, without replacing a pending error. It can block indefinitely.

Ownership: cannot be cloned, inspected, placed in containers or transferred into worker callbacks.

```tsrust
import {spawnScoped,join} from 'std:threads';import {unwrap} from 'std:result';function main(){const first=unwrap(spawnScoped(():int=>20));const second=unwrap(spawnScoped(():int=>22));const a=unwrap(join(first));const b=unwrap(join(second));console.log(a+b);}
```

Expected output: 42.

std:threads.signature: spawn(callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>): Result<Thread<T, E>, SpawnError>
std:threads.inferredSignature: function spawn(callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>): Result<Thread<T, E>, SpawnError>

parameters.label: callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>
parameters.documentation: Starts one native OS thread immediately. The callback runs once with zero arguments or one TaskContext. T is its returned type; E is its inferred thrown payload type, or undefined when it cannot throw. Returns Ok with a uniquely owned handle, or Err with code spawn and an OS error message. A failed spawn disposes the callback and its captures. Worker throws are retained for join; they do not throw in the spawning caller. No pool, serialization, cancellation or stack-size option is provided. Captures, returned values and thrown payloads must be owned transferable data. Caller loans, program-state borrows and stored callbacks are rejected.

std:threads.signature: join(worker: Thread<T, E> | ScopedThread<T, E>): Result<T, ThreadError<E>>

parameters.label: worker: Thread<T, E> | ScopedThread<T, E>
parameters.documentation: Waits for the worker to finish and returns its owned result. Returns Err with code worker and the original typed error payload when the callback throws; code panic has no error payload and reports a backend panic. The handle is consumed on success and failure. The caller blocks until completion; there is no timeout or forced cancellation.

std:threads.documentation:
Waits for the worker to finish and returns its owned result. Returns Err with code worker and the original typed error payload when the callback throws; code panic has no error payload and reports a backend panic. Code cancelled has no error payload and reports a cancellation request that won before completion was published. The handle is consumed on success and failure. The caller waits until completion; a pool worker helps execute queued work during nested joins. There is no timeout or forced interruption. Blocking dependency cycles are unsupported.

Ownership: consumes the handle and moves the returned value or thrown payload without cloning. A second join or detach is rejected.

```tsrust
import {spawn,join} from 'std:threads';function main(){match(spawn(():int=>42)){Ok(worker)=>{match(join(worker)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);}}},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);}}}
```

Expected output: 42.

workers.documentation: Configured reusable worker count; nested helping can make running tasks exceed this count. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().workers is 2. Ownership: copies the integer.

capacity.documentation: Configured maximum outstanding tasks, including completed results still retained. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().capacity is 16. Ownership: copies the integer.

queued.documentation: Admitted tasks not yet started, including cancelled tasks awaiting disposal. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().queued is 0. Ownership: copies the integer.

running.documentation: Started tasks not yet completed, including parents helping nested tasks. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().running is 0. Ownership: copies the integer.

completed.documentation: Published task results still waiting for collection; joining or cleanup releases their slots. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().completed is 0. Ownership: copies the integer.

outstanding.documentation: Total admitted tasks whose slots remain retained; equals queued + running + completed. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().outstanding is 0. Ownership: copies the integer.

std:threads.name: ThreadPoolOptions
std:threads.signature: type ThreadPoolOptions = { workers: int; capacity: int }
std:threads.documentation:
Explicit limits for new ThreadPool(options). Both fields are required when options are supplied: workers is 1..256 and capacity is 1..1000000 outstanding tasks. Invalid ranges throw SpawnError. Omit the constructor argument entirely to use system-based defaults. Construction does not mutate options; the record can be reused for independent pools.

```tsrust
import {ThreadPool,ThreadPoolOptions} from 'std:threads';
```

capacity.documentation: Required outstanding task limit, 1..1000000. Includes queued, running and completed uncollected tasks. Construction throw SpawnError code range outside that interval. Read as int; reading does not change options. Ownership: copies the integer. Example: options = {workers: 2, capacity: 16}; options.capacity is 16.

ValidationContext.name: addIssue
ValidationContext.signature: addIssue(options: { path?: Path<T>; message: string }): void

parameters.label: options: { path?: Path<T>; message: string }
parameters.documentation: Required message and optional literal path. Omitted or empty path identifies the current value. Fields and nonnegative integer array indices must match T.

ValidationContext.documentation:
Reports a refinement-failed validation issue. Adds the containing schema path before the supplied relative path. Does not throw or stop the callback; any reported issue rejects validation, including issues discarded by retention limits. Invalid paths are checker errors.

Example: ctx.addIssue({ path: ['confirm'], message: 'Passwords differ' }) reports at the confirm field.

Ownership: mutably borrows the temporary context and consumes the message. The context cannot escape its callback.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.int().superRefine((value,ctx)=>{if(value<1){ctx.addIssue({message:'Must be positive'});}});const result=schema.safeParse(0);if(result.success){const value=result.data;throw 'Expected rejection';}else{const error=result.error;console.log(error.issues[0].message);}}
```

Expected output:
```text
Must be positive
```

SchemaPipeline.name: toJsonSchema
SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Exports the reusable schema as an owned JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 document. Takes no arguments and leaves the receiver unchanged. Strict object properties, required fields, scalar bounds, literals, enums, arrays, string-keyed records and recursive references are preserved. Overlapping union branches use anyOf. Optional object properties may be absent; undefined elsewhere has no JSON representation.

Throws SchemaExportError with code, path and reason for callbacks, default factories, native Map/Set schemas and output transformations such as strip or retain. path is a JSON Pointer into the schema; an empty string identifies the root. Export never invokes callbacks or returns a partial document. Custom validation messages do not change exported acceptance rules.

Numeric types and bounds are exported, but native checked conversion still applies: an external validator can accept an exact integer that native number conversion rejects for precision loss. Integer bounds remain exact.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.boolean();console.log(JSON.stringify(schema.toJsonSchema()));}
```

Expected document: {"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","type":"boolean"}.

Ownership: borrows the schema and allocates an independently owned JsonValue. Export does not clone the plan.

SchemaPipeline.name: superRefine
SchemaPipeline.signature: superRefine(callback: (value: ReadOnly<Output>, ctx: Mutable<ValidationContext<Output>>) => void): Schema<Output>

parameters.label: callback: (value: ReadOnly<Output>, ctx: Mutable<ValidationContext<Output>>) => void
parameters.documentation: Reusable callback. Read the validated value and report zero or more issues with ctx.addIssue. Return void; thrown exceptions propagate.

SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Checks a validated value and can report multiple issues without changing its output type. Zero issues accepts the value; any issue rejects it. Later stages do not run after rejection. The callback continues after addIssue, even after the retention limit is reached. Validation retains at most 64 issues with 32 path segments and 1024 path bytes each; truncated reports discarded information. Paths are relative to this value and checked against its fields and array elements. Input and captures cannot be mutated or consumed.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.int().superRefine((value,ctx)=>{if(value<1){ctx.addIssue({message:'Must be positive'});}});const result=schema.safeParse(0);if(result.success){const value=result.data;throw 'Expected rejection';}else{const error=result.error;console.log(error.issues[0].message);}}
```

Expected output: Must be positive.

Ownership: consumes the receiving schema; validation borrows the reusable callback. The callback temporarily borrows its value and context. The context cannot be cloned, consumed or retained.

examples.source: import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.int().superRefine((value,ctx)=>{if(value<1){ctx.addIssue({message:'Must be positive'});}});const result=schema.safeParse(0);if(result.success){const value=result.data;throw 'Expected rejection';}else{const error=result.error;console.log(error.issues[0].message);}}

SchemaPipeline.name: safeParseJson
SchemaPipeline.signature: safeParseJson(text: ReadOnly<string>): SafeParseSuccess<Output> | SafeParseError<{ kind: 'json'; error: JsonError } | { kind: 'validation'; error: ValidationError }>

parameters.label: text: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Borrowed UTF-8 JSON text. The complete document is checked before any default factory or callback runs.

SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Decodes JSON text directly into the inferred schema output, applying the reusable rules, defaults and callbacks. Returns { success: true, data: output }, or { success: false, error } with kind json for malformed JSON/resource limits and kind validation for data that violates the rules. Narrow kind to access JsonError code/message/byte offset or ValidationError issues/property-index paths. Callback exceptions propagate. Limits are 16 MiB of UTF-8 input, depth 64, one million entries per container and one million value nodes; validation retains at most 64 issues with 32 path segments and 1024 path bytes each. Unknown object fields reject by default; strip discards them and retain returns owned extras. Last duplicate key wins before callbacks. Exact integer-to-number conversion remains checked. Entire syntax and resource validation precedes callbacks, including discarded fields. Union branches retry only before a consuming transform/coercion commits. The receiver is unchanged.

Ownership: borrows text and schema; output owns its data and outlives text. Typed fields do not construct an intermediate JsonValue tree. Explicit retained extras or JsonValue coercion arguments request owned dynamic values.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.object({count:s.int()});const result=schema.safeParseJson('{"count":7}');if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value.count);}else{const error=result.error;console.log(error.kind);}}
```

Expected output: 7.

SchemaPipeline.name: refine
SchemaPipeline.signature: refine(predicate: (value: ReadOnly<Output>) => boolean, options?: { path?: Path<Output>; message?: string }): Schema<Output>

parameters.label: predicate: (value: ReadOnly<Output>) => boolean
parameters.documentation: Reusable predicate. Reads the validated value and returns true to accept or false to report refinement-failed. Exceptions propagate.

parameters.label: options?: { path?: Path<Output>; message?: string }
parameters.documentation: Optional diagnostic location and message. Path is a literal array checked against the value received by the predicate: declared field names and nonnegative integer array indices. Empty or omitted path reports at the current value. Invalid paths are compiler errors.

SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Checks a validated value without changing its output type. False returns a validation issue; a thrown exception propagates. Later pipeline stages do not run after either failure. Predicates may log or allocate but cannot mutate or consume input or captures.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.int().refine(value=>value>0);const result=schema.safeParse(3);if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value);}else{const error=result.error;console.log('rejected');}}
```

Expected output: 3.

Consumes the receiving schema and returns a reusable immutable plan. Validation consumes owned input; the predicate only borrows its typed value.

Options may supply a custom message and a relative path, for example { path: ['confirm'], message: 'Passwords must match' }. Nested schemas prepend their containing path. The path does not read or mutate the value. Constructor messages supply a fallback; a child custom message takes precedence.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.object({password:s.string(),confirm:s.string()}).refine(value=>value.password===value.confirm,{path:['confirm'],message:'Passwords must match'});const result2=schema.safeParseJson('{"password":"one","confirm":"two"}');if(result2.success){const value=result2.data;throw 'Expected rejection';}else{const error=result2.error;if(error.kind==='validation'){console.log(error.error.issues[0].message);}else{throw 'Unexpected JSON failure';}}}
```

Expected output: Passwords must match.

examples.source: import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.object({password:s.string(),confirm:s.string()}).refine(value=>value.password===value.confirm,{path:['confirm'],message:'Passwords must match'});const result=schema.safeParseJson('{"password":"one","confirm":"two"}');if(result.success){const value=result.data;throw 'Expected rejection';}else{const error=result.error;if(error.kind==='validation'){console.log(error.error.issues[0].message);}else{throw 'Unexpected JSON failure';}}}

SchemaPipeline.name: transform

parameters.label: convert: (value: Owned<Output>) => Next
parameters.documentation: Reusable conversion callback. May mutate or consume its owned value and returns the next output. Captured state remains readonly.

SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Converts a successfully validated value and infers the next output type. The callback runs only after earlier validation succeeds. It may mutate its owned input. Exceptions propagate and skip later stages. Within a union, the first consuming stage commits the branch; later failure does not retry another branch.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.array(s.int()).transform(values=>values.length);const result=schema.safeParse([2,4]);if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value);}else{const error=result.error;console.log('rejected');}}
```

Expected output: 2.

Consumes the receiving schema. The returned plan retains its original accepted input type and uniquely owns a reusable callback with readonly captures.

SchemaPipeline.name: coerce

parameters.label: convert: (input: Owned<Raw>) => Input
parameters.documentation: Conversion before receiving-schema validation. Annotate raw input to define the accepted type; return a value that the receiving schema accepts.

SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Explicitly converts raw input before validating it with this schema. The callback parameter defines the accepted raw input type. Invalid converted data produces validation issues; conversion exceptions propagate. No implicit string, number or boolean conversion occurs. A consuming coercion inside a union commits that branch before conversion.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.int().min(2).coerce((values:int[]):int=>values.length);const result=schema.safeParse([3,5]);if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value);}else{const error=result.error;console.log('rejected');}}
```

Expected output: 2.

Consumes the receiving schema and raw input. The callback may mutate owned input; captures remain readonly and reusable.

SchemaPipeline.name: parse

parameters.label: input: Input
parameters.documentation: Owned input accepted by this chain. Earlier conversions determine its type; later transformations determine the successful output.

SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Validates input and returns the inferred output directly. Throws ValidationError on invalid input; inspect its issues array for code, message, expected, observed and field/index path segments. The truncated flag reports omitted issues. Callback exceptions propagate unchanged. Uses the same accepted inputs, conversion rules and validation limits as safeParse. The reusable schema is unchanged.

Ownership: borrows the schema; owned input is consumed on success and failure, exactly as with safeParse. No implicit cloning.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.string().min(1);console.log(schema.parse('Hello'));try{schema.parse('');}catch(error){console.log(error.issues.length);}}
```

Expected output: Hello, then 1.

SchemaPipeline.name: safeParse

parameters.label: input: Input
parameters.documentation: Owned input accepted by this chain. Earlier conversions determine its type; later transformations determine the successful output.

SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Validates through each stage in order. Returns { success: true, data } with the final typed output or { success: false, error } with bounded validation issues. Callback exceptions propagate rather than becoming validation issues. Failure skips later stages.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.array(s.int()).transform(values=>values.length);const result=schema.safeParse([1,2,3]);if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value);}else{const error=result.error;console.log('rejected');}}
```

Expected output: 3.

Borrows the reusable schema and consumes input on success or failure. No hidden clone preserves input.

SchemaPipeline.name: optional
SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Accepts undefined without invoking inner pipeline callbacks. Other supplied values retain the original input contract and produce the transformed output. For missing object fields, an inner default still runs and is validated; otherwise the field becomes undefined. Failed defaults and factory exceptions are not suppressed.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.string().transform(value=>value.length).optional();const result=schema.safeParse(undefined);if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value);}else{const error=result.error;console.log('rejected');}}
```

Expected output: undefined.

Consumes the receiving schema and returns a reusable immutable plan. No payloads are cloned.

SchemaPipeline.name: nullable
SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Accepts null without invoking inner pipeline callbacks. Other supplied values retain the original input contract and produce the transformed output. Missing object fields are distinct from null and still require an optional rule or default.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.string().transform(value=>value.length).nullable();const result=schema.safeParse(null);if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value);}else{const error=result.error;console.log('rejected');}}
```

Expected output: null.

Consumes the receiving schema and returns a reusable immutable plan. No payloads are cloned.

SchemaPipeline.name: default

parameters.label: factory: () => RawInput
parameters.documentation: Reusable zero-argument factory producing input for the receiving pipeline. Runs only for a missing object field. Captures remain readonly.

SchemaPipeline.documentation:
Supplies input when an object field is missing, then validates it through the receiving pipeline. The factory produces the original accepted input type; transformations determine the final output type. Supplied null, undefined and invalid values do not trigger the factory. Factories run once per missing field per attempted branch. Invalid generated data returns schema issues; exceptions propagate. An outer optional rule does not hide a failing default.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.object({count:s.string().transform(value=>value.length).default(()=> 'hello')});const result=schema.safeParse(JSON.parse('{}'));if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value.count);}else{const error=result.error;console.log('rejected');}}
```

Expected output: 5.

Consumes the schema and uniquely owns a reusable factory. Fresh owned arrays or records need no hidden clone.

string.name: isWellFormed
string.documentation:
Tests whether text contains a valid Unicode representation. Takes no arguments; every native UTF-8 string returns true.

```tsrust
console.log("é😊".isWellFormed()); // prints "true"
```

Lone surrogate strings cannot be constructed in Tsrust. Receiver is borrowed and unchanged.

string.name: toWellFormed
string.documentation:
Returns unchanged string content. Takes no arguments and leaves the receiver reusable.

```tsrust
console.log("Hello".toWellFormed()); // prints "Hello"
```

Native strings are always valid UTF-8 and cannot contain lone surrogates. No surrogate replacement is needed. Static text can remain borrowed; owned text receives an independent copy.

string.name: trim
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from both ends, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trim()); // prints "Hello"
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy.

string.name: trimStart
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from the beginning, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trimStart()); // prints "Hello  "
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy.

string.name: trimEnd
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from the end, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trimEnd()); // prints "  Hello"
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy.

string.name: trimLeft
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from the beginning, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trimLeft()); // prints "Hello  "
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy. Alias of trimStart().

string.name: trimRight
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from the end, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trimRight()); // prints "  Hello"
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy. Alias of trimEnd().

string.name: toLowerCase
string.documentation:
Converts text to lowercase using Unicode case mappings. Takes no arguments and leaves the original unchanged.

```tsrust
console.log("ÉCOLE".toLowerCase()); // prints "école"
```

Locale-independent conversion may expand characters and change byte length. The receiver is borrowed; the result owns its text.

string.name: toUpperCase
string.documentation:
Converts text to uppercase using Unicode case mappings. Takes no arguments and leaves the original unchanged.

```tsrust
console.log("Straße".toUpperCase()); // prints "STRASSE"
```

Locale-independent conversion may expand characters and change byte length. The receiver is borrowed; the result owns its text.

string.name: toLocaleLowerCase
string.documentation:
Returns the string converted to lowercase. The result is the same as `toLowerCase()`.

Takes no arguments. A locale argument such as `"tr"` is an `unsupported` error, because locale-specific rules are not provided; the conversion always uses the general Unicode mapping, whatever the system language is.

@returns A new string. A character can change length: `"İ"` becomes `i` followed by a combining dot.

```tsrust
console.log("ÉCOLE Straße".toLocaleLowerCase()); // prints "école straße"
```

Text in Turkish, Azerbaijani or Lithuanian can need rules that this conversion does not apply, for example dotted and dotless i.

The receiver is only read. The result is a new owned string.

string.name: toLocaleUpperCase
string.documentation:
Returns the string converted to uppercase. The result is the same as `toUpperCase()`.

Takes no arguments. A locale argument such as `"tr"` is an `unsupported` error, because locale-specific rules are not provided; the conversion always uses the general Unicode mapping, whatever the system language is.

@returns A new string. A character can change length: `"ß"` becomes `"SS"`.

```tsrust
console.log("école straße".toLocaleUpperCase()); // prints "ÉCOLE STRASSE"
```

Text in Turkish, Azerbaijani or Lithuanian can need rules that this conversion does not apply, for example dotted and dotless i.

The receiver is only read. The result is a new owned string.

string.name: includes
string.signature: includes(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, position?: int): boolean
string.documentation:
Tests whether search text occurs anywhere in the receiver. Optional position clamps to [0, byte length], default zero (start of the searched suffix). The search argument is a string; the receiver remains unchanged.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param position - UTF-8 byte boundary, clamped to the string bounds; defaults to zero.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".includes("ell")); // prints "true"
```

Search coordinates use UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 units. Explicit search boundaries must be valid scalar boundaries. String operands are borrowed.

A StringView supports this read directly. A JsonValue or JsonView proven to contain a string by a stable typeof guard also supports this read without copying or consuming its text. The search argument may also be a JSON value proven to contain a string. The source owner stays borrowed for the complete operation; later arguments cannot invalidate it.

string.name: startsWith
string.signature: startsWith(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, position?: int): boolean
string.documentation:
Tests whether the receiver begins with search text. Optional position clamps to [0, byte length], default zero (start of the searched suffix). The search argument is a string; the receiver remains unchanged.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param position - UTF-8 byte boundary, clamped to the string bounds; defaults to zero.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".startsWith("he")); // prints "true"
```

Search coordinates use UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 units. Explicit search boundaries must be valid scalar boundaries. String operands are borrowed.

A StringView supports this read directly. A JsonValue or JsonView proven to contain a string by a stable typeof guard also supports this read without copying or consuming its text. The search argument may also be a JSON value proven to contain a string. The source owner stays borrowed for the complete operation; later arguments cannot invalidate it.

string.name: endsWith
string.signature: endsWith(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, position?: int): boolean
string.documentation:
Tests whether the receiver ends with search text. Optional position clamps to [0, byte length], default byte length (end of the searched prefix). The search argument is a string; the receiver remains unchanged.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param position - UTF-8 byte boundary, clamped to the string bounds; defaults to byte length.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".endsWith("lo")); // prints "true"
```

Search coordinates use UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 units. Explicit search boundaries must be valid scalar boundaries. String operands are borrowed.

A StringView supports this read directly. A JsonValue or JsonView proven to contain a string by a stable typeof guard also supports this read without copying or consuming its text. The search argument may also be a JSON value proven to contain a string. The source owner stays borrowed for the complete operation; later arguments cannot invalidate it.

string.name: indexOf
string.signature: indexOf(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, fromIndex?: int): int
string.documentation:
Returns the first matching byte offset, or -1 when absent. The search argument is a string; the receiver remains unchanged.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param fromIndex - Byte offset; negative values clamp to zero, large values clamp to byte length. Defaults to zero.

```tsrust
console.log("éclair".indexOf("c")); // prints "2"
```

fromIndex defaults to zero. Search coordinates use UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 units. Explicit search boundaries must be valid scalar boundaries. String operands are borrowed.

A StringView supports this read directly. A JsonValue or JsonView proven to contain a string by a stable typeof guard also supports this read without copying or consuming its text. The search argument may also be a JSON value proven to contain a string. The source owner stays borrowed for the complete operation; later arguments cannot invalidate it.

string.name: lastIndexOf
string.signature: lastIndexOf(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, fromIndex?: int): int
string.documentation:
Returns the last matching byte offset, or -1 when absent. The search argument is a string; the receiver remains unchanged.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param fromIndex - Byte offset; negative values clamp to zero, large values clamp to byte length. Defaults to the end for backward search.

```tsrust
console.log("banana".lastIndexOf("a")); // prints "5"
```

fromIndex defaults to the last available position. Search coordinates use UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 units. Explicit search boundaries must be valid scalar boundaries. String operands are borrowed.

A StringView supports this read directly. A JsonValue or JsonView proven to contain a string by a stable typeof guard also supports this read without copying or consuming its text. The search argument may also be a JSON value proven to contain a string. The source owner stays borrowed for the complete operation; later arguments cannot invalidate it.

string.name: slice
string.documentation:
Returns the portion between start (inclusive) and end (exclusive). Both are optional integer byte offsets; defaults are zero and byte length. Negative offsets count from the end; bounds clamp to the string. Reversed bounds return empty text.

@param start - UTF-8 byte start offset. Negative values count from the end; bounds clamp. Defaults to zero.
@param end - Exclusive UTF-8 byte bound, default byte length. Negative values count from the end and bounds clamp.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".slice(1, 4)); // prints "ell"
```

Nonempty endpoints must be UTF-8 scalar boundaries. The receiver is borrowed; static slices may stay borrowed, owned slices copy.

string.name: substring
string.documentation:
Returns text between two clamped byte offsets. start is required; end defaults to byte length. Negative offsets clamp to zero and reversed bounds swap.

@param start - UTF-8 byte start offset. Required; negative bounds clamp to zero. Required.
@param end - Exclusive UTF-8 byte bound, default byte length. Reversed bounds swap; negative bounds clamp to zero.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".substring(4, 1)); // prints "ell"
```

Nonempty endpoints must be UTF-8 scalar boundaries; empty ranges skip boundary checks. Static slices can stay borrowed; owned results copy.

string.name: substr
string.documentation:
Returns up to length bytes of text beginning at start, without changing the receiver. Both arguments are optional ints. start defaults to zero; a negative start counts from the end, then clamps to [0, byte length]. length defaults to the remaining bytes. A length <= 0 returns empty text, and a positive length is capped at the remaining bytes without overflowing. All signed 64-bit int values are accepted for these bounds. More than two arguments or arguments of other types are errors; no coercion is performed. The receiver and supplied arguments are evaluated once, left to right, even for an empty or full result.

@param start - Optional signed int UTF-8 byte start, default zero. Negative values count from the end; the resulting offset clamps to the string bounds.
@param length - Optional int byte count, default remaining bytes. Values <= 0 give empty text; positive values cap at the remaining bytes without overflow.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".substr(1, 3)); // prints "ell"
console.log("hello".substr(-3, 2)); // prints "ll"
console.log("é😀x".substr(2, 4)); // prints "😀"
console.log("é".substr(1, 0)); // prints empty text
```

Bounds count UTF-8 bytes, unlike the legacy JavaScript substr method's UTF-16 code units. Both endpoints of a nonempty result must be Unicode scalar boundaries; otherwise execution fails with a source-located boundary diagnostic. For example, "é".substr(1, 1) fails because byte 1 is inside é, and "😀".substr(0, 1) fails because the end is inside the astral scalar. Empty ranges skip these checks. On "hello", start -9223372036854775808 clamps to zero, start 9223372036854775807 gives empty text, and length 9223372036854775807 returns only the remaining bytes.

The receiver is borrowed through argument evaluation and remains reusable; later arguments cannot move or mutate that borrowed input. Empty results use static empty text. A full nonempty range uses Cow cloning: static text can be shared, while owned text is independently copied. Partial static text can borrow a static slice; partial owned text is independently copied.

examples.source: const text = "hello".repeat(1); const piece = text.substr(1, 3); console.log(piece); console.log(text);

string.name: charAt
string.documentation:
Returns the Unicode scalar at an integer index, default zero. Negative or out-of-range indices return empty text.

@param index - Unicode scalar index, default zero; outside the string returns empty text.

```tsrust
console.log("é😊".charAt(1)); // prints "😊"
```

Counts Unicode scalars, unlike byte-indexed slice and JavaScript UTF-16 charAt. Receiver is borrowed; a selected scalar produces owned text.

string.name: concat
string.documentation:
Appends zero or more string arguments in order and returns the combined text. No coercion is performed; the receiver is unchanged.

@param values - Strings appended in order, without coercion.

```tsrust
console.log("Hello".concat(" ", "world")); // prints "Hello world"
```

Operands are borrowed. Changed text owns an independent buffer; zero/all-empty arguments clone the receiver with static sharing or an owned copy.

Spread arguments may come from strings, arrays or Sets whose elements are strings. String sources construct Unicode scalar character values and stay usable.

```tsrust
console.log("a".concat(..."bc"));
// prints abc
```

string.name: padStart
string.documentation:
Pads the beginning until the integer target byte length is reached. Optional filler defaults to a space and repeats as needed. Short/negative targets or empty filler leave text unchanged.

@param target - Destination byte length of the padded string; short or negative targets leave it unchanged.
@param filler - String repeated to fill missing bytes; defaults to one space, empty text disables padding.

```tsrust
console.log("7".padStart(3, "0")); // prints "007"
```

Targets count UTF-8 bytes, not JavaScript UTF-16 units. A truncated filler must end at a scalar boundary or fail. Receiver stays reusable; changed results own their storage, no-ops use Cow cloning.

string.name: padEnd
string.documentation:
Pads the end until the integer target byte length is reached. Optional filler defaults to a space and repeats as needed. Short/negative targets or empty filler leave text unchanged.

@param target - Destination byte length of the padded string; short or negative targets leave it unchanged.
@param filler - String repeated to fill missing bytes; defaults to one space, empty text disables padding.

```tsrust
console.log("7".padEnd(3, "0")); // prints "700"
```

Targets count UTF-8 bytes, not JavaScript UTF-16 units. A truncated filler must end at a scalar boundary or fail. Receiver stays reusable; changed results own their storage, no-ops use Cow cloning.

string.name: repeat
string.documentation:
Repeats the receiver count times, returning new text. count is a required nonnegative integer; zero produces empty text. Negative counts and excessive lengths fail.

@param count - Nonnegative integer repetition count; zero returns empty text.

```tsrust
console.log("ha".repeat(3)); // prints "hahaha"
```

Receiver is borrowed; output has independent storage.

string.name: replace
string.documentation:
Replaces the first occurrence of string search with replacement text. The original remains unchanged. Regular expressions are unsupported.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param replacement - Replacement text; supports $$, $&, $` and $' templates.

```tsrust
console.log("banana".replace("a", "o")); // prints "bonana"
```

Replacement templates support $$ (literal dollar), $& (match), $` (prefix) and $' (suffix); capture references have no regex groups. Operands are borrowed; output owns its text.

string.name: replaceAll
string.documentation:
Replaces every non-overlapping occurrence of string search with replacement text. The original remains unchanged. Regular expressions are unsupported.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param replacement - Replacement text; supports $$, $&, $` and $' templates.

```tsrust
console.log("banana".replaceAll("a", "o")); // prints "bonono"
```

Replacement templates support $$ (literal dollar), $& (match), $` (prefix) and $' (suffix); capture references have no regex groups. Operands are borrowed; output owns its text.

string.name: split
string.documentation:
Returns a string array by splitting the receiver at a literal string separator. The receiver is unchanged. The optional separator must be a string; when omitted, the result contains the whole receiver as one element, including an empty receiver. The optional limit must be an int. It is converted modulo 2^32 to an unsigned count from 0 through 4294967295; omission defaults to 4294967295. A converted count of zero returns an empty array. Other counts keep only the first pieces and discard the rest; the remainder is not joined into the last piece. More than two arguments or other argument types are errors. Receiver and supplied arguments are evaluated once, left to right, even when the converted limit is zero.

@param separator - Optional literal string separator. Omission returns the whole text as one element. Empty text splits Unicode scalar values, without artificial leading or trailing empty pieces.
@param limit - Optional int converted modulo 2^32 to the maximum number of returned pieces. Defaults to 4294967295; -1 converts to that same count, 4294967296 converts to zero, and 4294967297 converts to one. Pieces beyond the converted cap are discarded.

```tsrust
const parts = "a,b,c".split(",", 2);
console.log(parts.length); // prints "2"
console.log(parts[1]); // prints "b", not "b,c"
console.log("😀é".split("").length); // prints "2"
console.log("".split("").length); // prints "0"
console.log("".split().length); // prints "1"
console.log("a,b".split(",", -1).length); // prints "2"
console.log("a,b".split(",", 4294967296).length); // prints "0"
```

Nonempty separators match literally and do not overlap. Leading, adjacent and trailing separators retain empty pieces: "a,,".split(",") has three elements. Empty separators split Unicode scalars, including separate combining marks, rather than JavaScript UTF-16 code units. Limit wrapping preserves the existing unsigned 32-bit count contract: -1 permits up to 4294967295 pieces, while 4294967296 permits none. All signed int limit values are accepted; no implicit numeric or string coercion is performed. Regular expressions, omitted-argument placeholders and argument coercion are unsupported.

The receiver and separator are borrowed through argument evaluation; later arguments cannot move or mutate an earlier borrowed operand. The returned array is independent. Pieces from static text may borrow static slices; pieces from owned input have independent copied storage. An omitted separator uses the ordinary Cow clone of the receiver.

examples.source: const parts = "😀é".split(""); console.log(parts.length); console.log(parts[0]); console.log(parts[1]); console.log("e\u0301".split("").length);

console.log("".split("").length); console.log("".split().length); console.log("a,b".split(",", -1).length); console.log("a,b".split(",", 0).length); console.log("a,b".split(",", 4294967296).length); console.log("a,b".split(",", 4294967297).length);
const text = "a,b".repeat(1); const parts = text.split(); console.log(parts[0]); console.log(text);

string.name: anchor
string.documentation: Returns the receiver text inside and tags. Requires exactly one string argument, name, used as the name attribute. Only ASCII double quotes in that attribute are replaced with "; ampersands, angle brackets and single quotes are unchanged. Missing, extra or non-string arguments are errors. No implicit coercion or default "undefined" attribute is supplied. The receiver remains unchanged. The raw receiver content is inserted without escaping; this method is not an HTML sanitizer. @param name - Required string anchor name; only ASCII double quotes become ". No value validation or coercion is performed. ```tsrust console.log("hello".anchor("section")); // prints "hello" ``` For a quote-containing attribute, "é😀".anchor("a\"&<>'") returns "'\">é😀". This is a legacy, deprecated JavaScript HTML-wrapper method. Native strings are valid UTF-8; Unicode text is preserved exactly. Strict string types replace JavaScript argument coercion. No DOM operation, rendering, URL validation or HTML sanitization occurs. The receiver and attribute are borrowed and evaluated once, left to right, remaining reusable. Later arguments cannot move or mutate the borrowed receiver. Every result is a fresh, independently owned string, including an empty receiver.

string.name: big
string.documentation:
Returns the receiver text inside <big> and </big> tags. Takes no arguments; supplying an argument is an error. The receiver remains unchanged. The raw receiver content is inserted without escaping; this method is not an HTML sanitizer.

```tsrust
console.log("é😀".big()); // prints "<big>é😀</big>"
```

This is a legacy, deprecated JavaScript HTML-wrapper method. Native strings are valid UTF-8; Unicode text is preserved exactly. Strict string types replace JavaScript argument coercion. No DOM operation, rendering, URL validation or HTML sanitization occurs.

The receiver is borrowed and evaluated once, remaining reusable. Every result is a fresh, independently owned string, including an empty receiver.

string.name: blink
string.documentation:
Returns the receiver text inside <blink> and </blink> tags. Takes no arguments; supplying an argument is an error. The receiver remains unchanged. The raw receiver content is inserted without escaping; this method is not an HTML sanitizer.

```tsrust
console.log("é😀".blink()); // prints "<blink>é😀</blink>"
```

This is a legacy, deprecated JavaScript HTML-wrapper method. Native strings are valid UTF-8; Unicode text is preserved exactly. Strict string types replace JavaScript argument coercion. No DOM operation, rendering, URL validation or HTML sanitization occurs.

The receiver is borrowed and evaluated once, remaining reusable. Every result is a fresh, independently owned string, including an empty receiver.

string.name: bold
string.documentation: Returns the receiver text inside and tags. Takes no arguments; supplying an argument is an error. The receiver remains unchanged. The raw receiver content is inserted without escaping; this method is not an HTML sanitizer. ```tsrust console.log("é😀".bold()); // prints "é😀" ``` This is a legacy, deprecated JavaScript HTML-wrapper method. Native strings are valid UTF-8; Unicode text is preserved exactly. Strict string types replace JavaScript argument coercion. No DOM operation, rendering, URL validation or HTML sanitization occurs. The receiver is borrowed and evaluated once, remaining reusable. Every result is a fresh, independently owned string, including an empty receiver.

examples.source: const text = "hello".repeat(1); const wrapped = text.bold(); console.log(wrapped); console.log(text);

string.name: fixed
string.documentation:
Returns the receiver text inside <tt> and </tt> tags. Takes no arguments; supplying an argument is an error. The receiver remains unchanged. The raw receiver content is inserted without escaping; this method is not an HTML sanitizer.

```tsrust
console.log("é😀".fixed()); // prints "<tt>é😀</tt>"
```

This is a legacy, deprecated JavaScript HTML-wrapper method. Native strings are valid UTF-8; Unicode text is preserved exactly. Strict string types replace JavaScript argument coercion. No DOM operation, rendering, URL validation or HTML sanitization occurs.

The receiver is borrowed and evaluated once, remaining reusable. Every result is a fresh, independently owned string, including an empty receiver.

string.name: fontcolor
string.documentation:
Returns the receiver text inside <font color="…"> and </font> tags. Requires exactly one string argument, color, used as the color attribute. Only ASCII double quotes in that attribute are replaced with "; ampersands, angle brackets and single quotes are unchanged. Missing, extra or non-string arguments are errors. No implicit coercion or default "undefined" attribute is supplied. The receiver remains unchanged. The raw receiver content is inserted without escaping; this method is not an HTML sanitizer.

@param color - Required string font color text; only ASCII double quotes become ". No value validation or coercion is performed.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".fontcolor("red")); // prints "<font color=\"red\">hello</font>"
```

For a quote-containing attribute, "é😀".fontcolor("a\"&<>'") returns "<font color=\"a"&<>'\">é😀</font>".

This is a legacy, deprecated JavaScript HTML-wrapper method. Native strings are valid UTF-8; Unicode text is preserved exactly. Strict string types replace JavaScript argument coercion. No DOM operation, rendering, URL validation or HTML sanitization occurs.

The receiver and attribute are borrowed and evaluated once, left to right, remaining reusable. Later arguments cannot move or mutate the borrowed receiver. Every result is a fresh, independently owned string, including an empty receiver.

string.name: length
string.documentation:
Returns the number of bytes in the UTF-8 representation. This read-only property does not change the receiver.

```tsrust
console.log("é😊".length); // prints "6"
```

This is neither a Unicode scalar count nor JavaScript UTF-16 length. Observation borrows text and allocates nothing.

A StringView supports this read directly. A JsonValue or JsonView proven to contain a string by a stable typeof guard also supports this read without copying or consuming its text. The source owner stays borrowed for the complete operation; later arguments cannot invalidate it.

string.name: valueOf
string.documentation:

```tsrust
console.log("Hello".valueOf()); // prints "Hello"
```

Native strings are always valid UTF-8 and cannot contain lone surrogates. Static text can remain borrowed; owned text receives an independent copy.

string.name: at
string.documentation:
Returns the character at a position counted from the start, or from the end when the position is negative.

@param index - Required int position. `0` is the first character and `-1` is the last. Positions count whole Unicode characters, so an accented letter or an emoji is one position.

Returns the character as a one-character string, or `undefined` when the position is outside the string. The result type is `string | undefined`; use `??` for a fallback or compare with `undefined` before using it as a string.

```tsrust
const text="aé😀b";console.log(String(text.at(0)),String(text.at(-1)),String(text.at(2))); // prints "a b 😀"
```

```tsrust
const text="ab";console.log(String(text.at(2)),text.at(5)??"none"); // prints "undefined none"
```

Calling it with no argument or more than one is an `arity` error; a number or string index is a `type` error. Unlike `charAt`, which returns an empty string for a missing position, `at` returns `undefined` and accepts negative positions.

Positions count Unicode characters, not UTF-16 code units: `"😀".at(0)` is the whole emoji.

Receiver is borrowed and unchanged; the returned character is a new string owned by the caller.

if (code !== undefined) { console.log(code + 1, String.fromCodePoint(code + 1)); }

string.name: normalize
string.documentation:
Returns Unicode-normalized text so equivalent character spellings can have the same sequence of characters. The receiver is unchanged.

@param form - Optional string: `"NFC"`, `"NFD"`, `"NFKC"` or `"NFKD"`, case-sensitive. Omission or undefined selects `"NFC"`. NFC uses canonical decomposition followed by composition; NFD keeps the canonical decomposed form. NFKC and NFKD also replace compatibility characters, such as ligatures and circled digits, with their ordinary equivalents.

Returns a new string. Normalization can combine, split or reorder characters and can change byte length. It does not lowercase text, strip accents, remove punctuation or apply language-specific spelling rules. Empty text stays empty.

```tsrust
const text="é";
console.log(text.normalize(),"é".normalize("NFD")); // prints é é
```

```tsrust
console.log("ﬁ①가".normalize("NFKC"),"가".normalize("NFD")); // prints fi1가 가
```

Canonical combining marks reorder stably; Hangul syllables compose and decompose. Equal combining classes keep their order, and composition observes blocking and composition exclusions. Characters without normalization mappings stay unchanged. Strings contain valid Unicode scalars; isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves are unavailable.

Any other form name, including lowercase `"nfc"` or `""`, stops the program with `normalize form must be NFC, NFD, NFKC or NFKD` and the call's source position. A non-string form other than undefined is a `type` error; more than one argument is an `arity` error. Receiver and form expressions evaluate once, in that order.

Ownership: the receiver and form are borrowed; both remain usable. The returned string owns independent text.

Array.name: toString
Array.documentation:
Returns array element text separated by commas, with the same result as join() without a separator. The array is unchanged. Takes no arguments; passing any argument, including undefined, is an error. An empty array returns an empty string.

Nested arrays contribute their own comma-separated text. Null and undefined slots contribute empty text but retain their positions; records contribute [object Object]. Booleans become true or false. Number negative zero becomes 0; NaN and infinities become NaN, Infinity and -Infinity.

```tsrust
const values:int[][]=[[1,2],[],[3]];
console.log(values.toString()); // prints "1,2,,3"
```

```tsrust
const values:null[]=[null,null];
console.log(values.toString()); // prints ","
```

Native arrays are dense and homogeneously typed; supported leaves include int, Number, boolean, string, null, undefined and records at supported array ranks. Valid UTF-8 text is preserved. Integers retain the full signed 64-bit domain. Finite Number magnitudes from 1e-6 inclusive to 1e21 exclusive use decimal notation; other finite magnitudes use scientific notation with signed exponents. Standard native digits may differ at rounding boundaries. Custom overrides, prototype hooks and boxed values are absent. This method belongs to arrays; Number.toString is unsupported.

The receiver is borrowed and evaluated once, remains reusable, and produces one independently owned string.

Array.name: join
Array.documentation:
Returns the array elements as one string, inserting a separator between adjacent elements. The array is unchanged. An omitted separator defaults to a comma; an empty separator inserts no text. An empty array returns an empty string.

@param separator - Optional string placed between outer array elements; defaults to ",". More than one argument, a non-string separator, or explicit undefined is an error. The separator is evaluated even when the array is empty.

Nested arrays use commas internally regardless of the outer separator. Null and undefined elements contribute empty text while retaining their positions. Records contribute [object Object]. Booleans become true or false. Number negative zero becomes 0; NaN and infinities become NaN, Infinity and -Infinity.

```tsrust
const values:int[][]=[[1,2],[],[3]];
console.log(values.join("|")); // prints "1,2||3"
```

```tsrust
const values:null[]=[null,null];
console.log(values.join("|")); // prints "|"
```

Arrays are dense and homogeneously typed, with supported integer, Number, boolean, string, null, undefined, record and nested-array elements. Native strings preserve valid UTF-8 text. Integers retain their full signed 64-bit decimal values; finite Number magnitudes from 1e-6 inclusive to 1e21 exclusive use ordinary decimal notation, with scientific notation outside that range and an explicit sign on the exponent. Digits follow standard native formatting and can differ at rounding boundaries. Separators are strict strings, without implicit coercion.

The receiver and separator are borrowed and evaluated once, left to right, so both remain reusable. Later arguments cannot move or mutate the borrowed receiver. The result is one independently owned string.

Array.name: some
Array.signature: some(callback: (value: Element, index: int, source: Element[]) => boolean): boolean
parameters: callback: (value: Element, index: int, source: Element[]) => boolean
Array.documentation:
Returns true as soon as a boolean predicate succeeds; returns false for an empty array. Visits elements from the beginning and stops on the first success.

@param callback - Reusable callback with optional element, index and source arguments; must return boolean.

```tsrust
let values:int[]=[1,2,3];console.log(values.some((x:int):boolean => { return x > 2; })); // prints "true"
```

The method supplies element, integer index and source array in those positions; the callback may declare fewer parameters. Data element/source arguments are read-only borrows. Callable element parameters use mutate borrowing and permit only an optional index parameter; once elements and an overlapping source-array parameter are rejected. A zero-parameter callback can observe a callable array without taking its environments; reusable and once elements stay available afterward. Stored reusable callable elements can be lent to an arrow visitor directly, through a local binding or from a factory. Use a mutate callable element parameter, followed by an optional int index. Once elements and a simultaneous source-array parameter are rejected.

Ownership: the receiver is borrowed for the iteration and is not cloned or consumed. The result does not copy receiver elements.

Invoking a borrowed callable can change its captured state; the changed environment stays in its original slot. Short-circuiting leaves unvisited environments untouched.

Ownership: a mutate callable element parameter uses exclusive receiver access and preserves each environment in the array. Overlapping receiver captures, mutation or moves are rejected during traversal. An arrow visitor can be supplied directly, held in a local binding or returned by a factory; forwarded function declarations and abstract visitor parameters are not yet supported.

For data-element callbacks, additional trailing optional or defaulted parameters receive undefined. A default initializer runs for each reached callback invocation when its supplied value is undefined; a present null does not trigger it. Empty input and unvisited short-circuit positions do not run callback defaults. Required fixed parameters beyond the supplied positions are rejected. Callable-element mutate visitors remain limited to element and optional index positions; extra parameters or an overlapping source-array parameter are rejected.

```tsrust
const values = [3,1,2];
console.log(values.some((value: int, index: int, source: ReadOnly<int[]>, extra: int = 2): boolean => { return value > extra; }));
// true
```

Ownership: the receiver stays borrowed through defaults and callback execution; element environments remain in their original slots.

A terminal homogeneous rest parameter collects only the remaining arguments actually supplied by this method, in order, into a fresh owning array. After the full documented fixed prefix it receives an empty array. Undefined padding for optional/defaulted fixed parameters does not become a tail element; an actually supplied undefined remains a value and must satisfy the rest element type. The supplied data tuple is element, index and source. Owned element and source-array arguments remain borrowed and cannot transfer into a rest pack. Mutate callable-element visitors retain their restricted element and optional index tuple; a lent environment cannot transfer into the pack.

```tsrust
const values:int[]=[2,3];console.log(values.some((value:int,index:int,source:int[],...tail:int[]):boolean=>{return value>2&&tail.length===0;}));
// true
```

Ownership: the rest pack is independent; Copy tail values are copied and eligible owned tail values transfer without hidden clones. Fixed-prefix borrowing, receiver loans and callback result ownership stay unchanged.

A checked callback error stops callback execution and propagates to the enclosing catch; applicable finally blocks run.

console.log(values.some((value: int, index: int, source: ReadOnly<int[]>, extra: int = 2): boolean => { return value > extra; }));

Array.name: pop
Array.documentation:
Removes and returns the last element of a supported dense homogeneous array. Takes no arguments; supplying any argument is an arity error. An empty array returns undefined and remains empty. Otherwise length decreases by one. Returns the element type or undefined; duplicate undefined alternatives collapse. The receiver remains available with its remaining elements.

```tsrust
let values:int[]=[1,2,3];const removed=values.pop();console.log(String(removed),values.length,values.join("|")); // 3 2 1|2
let empty:int[]=[];console.log(String(empty.pop()),empty.length);empty.push(7);console.log(String(empty.pop()),String(empty.pop()),empty.length);
// undefined 0
// 7 undefined 0
```

Supports existing homogeneous scalar, nested-array and record element types. Sparse arrays and prototype overrides are unsupported; mixed or nullable elements need a declared union element type such as `(int | string)[]`. Number results retain their original IEEE bits, including signed zero and NaN. An undefined[] element is indistinguishable from an empty removal result; the changed length distinguishes the cases. Nullable array receivers and returned payloads require a strict null/undefined guard before member access.

Requires mutable access to the receiver. Removed owned strings, arrays and records transfer into the result without cloning; no reference to the removed slot is returned. Remaining elements and the receiver keep their owners.

Use postfix `!` when an element must be present: `const users=["Pat"]; const user=users.pop()!; console.log(user.toUpperCase());` prints `PAT` and gives `user` type `string`. If the array is empty, the assertion fails at runtime with a non-null assertion message. Use `??` for a fallback instead.

Ownership: `!` does not clone or change transfer/borrow rules; the removed owned element remains an owned result.

For a fallback on any falsy result, use `||`: `const users=["Alice"]; const name=users.pop() || "Guest"; console.log(name);` prints `Alice` and gives `name` type `string`. An empty string also selects `"Guest"`. Use `??` to preserve an empty string and replace only null/undefined. Both operators evaluate the left operand once and skip the fallback when it is not needed.

Ownership: an owning logical result transfers selected owned values; readonly inspection borrows them. No implicit clone is added.

A standalone removal statement drops its result there. For a known dense local array, this releases captures belonging only to the removed callback. A discarded comma sequence containing direct removals and scalar operations also drops each removal result before its next operand; for example, `(handlers.pop(), second[0] = 9)` permits the assignment when only the removed element captured second. Nested discarded comma sequences preserve this order. A local declaration can retain a direct final removal: `const removed = (handlers.pop(), second[0] = 9, handlers.shift())` drops the discarded pop result before the assignment and transfers the final shift result into removed. Its captures stay protected until removed is disposed or replaced. A separately declared local `Holder | undefined` slot may start as `undefined` and later receive a concrete removal result; `Holder | null` slots similarly support `null`. Direct named reassignment of an existing concrete removal result can use the same final-removal form. The previous result stays alive while all RHS operands run and is dropped only after the new result has been evaluated; only then do its unshared captures become available. A removal result passed to another function remains protected during evaluation of the other arguments. Surviving elements and retained results keep their own captures protected. For a direct removal from a known dense local array, a local result owns only the removed element’s captures; leaving its lexical scope releases those captures. Direct result replacement in a normal lexical sequence evaluates the new value first, then drops the previous value and releases captures with no remaining owner. Replacements with a different captured environment inside branches or loops are not supported yet. Uncertain array contents retain conservative protection.

```tsrust
type Holder={run:ReadOnly<Function<int>>;};function main():void{const first=[3];const second=[5];const handlers:Holder[]=[{run:():int=>first[0]},{run:():int=>second[0]}];handlers.pop();second[0]=9;console.log(handlers[0].run(),second[0]);}
// 3 9
```
