Set.name: size
Set.documentation:
Returns the number of distinct keys. Readonly; assigning this property is rejected.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); console.log(values.size); // 2
```

Set.name: add
Set.documentation:
Inserts a key if absent. A duplicate leaves order unchanged. Returns void; chaining is unsupported. Deleting and adding a key again places it last. Ownership: owned keys transfer into the set; scalar keys copy.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); values.add(3); console.log(values.size); // 3
```

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); values.add(3); console.log(values.size);

Set.name: has
Set.documentation:
Reports whether a matching key exists. Receiver and argument are borrowed and unchanged.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); console.log(values.has(2)); // true
```

Set.name: delete
Set.documentation:
Removes a matching key and returns true, or returns false if absent. Surviving keys keep their order. Argument is borrowed; receiver mutates.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); console.log(values.delete(2), values.size); // true 1
```

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); console.log(values.delete(2), values.size);

Set.name: clear
Set.documentation:
Removes every key. Returns void. Receiver mutates.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); values.clear(); console.log(values.size); // 0
```

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); values.clear(); console.log(values.size);

Set.name: values
Set.documentation:
Returns an independent array of keys in insertion order. Takes no arguments. This is an array snapshot, not a live iterator. Receiver is borrowed; keys are explicitly copied.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); console.log(values.values().join(",")); // 2,1
```

Set.name: keys
Set.documentation:
Returns an independent array of keys in insertion order, like values(). Takes no arguments. Receiver is borrowed; keys are explicitly copied.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); console.log(values.keys().join(",")); // 2,1
```

Set.name: entries
Set.documentation:
Returns an independent array of key/key tuples in insertion order. Takes no arguments and does not mutate the receiver. Each tuple contains the same key in both positions. An empty Set returns an empty array. Replacement does not change order; deletion and reinsertion places a key last. Number keys use SameValueZero, including NaN and normalized zero. Wrong argument counts are static errors. This operation returns an array snapshot rather than a live iterator.

Example: `const values = new Set<string>(["b", "a", "b"]); const pairs = values.entries(); console.log(pairs[0][0], pairs[0][1]);` prints `b b`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<string>(["b", "a", "b"]); const pairs = values.entries(); console.log(pairs[0][0], pairs[0][1]);
// prints b b
```

Ownership: explicitly copies owned keys into both tuple positions. Later receiver mutation does not change the snapshot.

examples.source: const values = new Set<string>(["b", "a", "b"]); const pairs = values.entries(); console.log(pairs[0][0], pairs[0][1]);

Set.name: forEach
Set.signature: forEach(callback: (value: Element, key: Element, source: Set<Element>) => Result): void
parameters: callback: (value: Element, key: Element, source: Set<Element>) => Result
Set.documentation:
Calls a reusable callback once for each key in insertion order. The callback receives the value, the same key again, and the readonly source Set. Callbacks may use zero through three supplied positions; normal default and rest parameter rules apply. An empty Set does not call the callback. There is no thisArg argument. Wrong arity, incompatible parameter types/access, consuming callbacks, and receiver mutation or transfer during iteration are static errors.

Returns void and does not mutate the receiver. Callback results are evaluated and discarded after each call. Callback errors propagate and may be caught by surrounding try/catch. External mutable captures are allowed when they do not conflict with receiver borrows.

Example: `const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 3]); let total = 0; values.forEach((value) => { total = total + value; }); console.log(total);` prints `4`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 3]); let total = 0; values.forEach((value) => { total = total + value; }); console.log(total);
// prints 4
```

Ownership: scalar inputs copy; owned key arguments and the source Set borrow readonly. No owned callback input is implicitly cloned.

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 3]); let total = 0; values.forEach((value) => { total = total + value; }); console.log(total);

Set.name: isSubsetOf
Set.documentation:
Tests whether every receiver key occurs in another Set. Takes exactly one other Set, whose key type may differ from the receiver. Returns a boolean and does not mutate either input. An empty receiver returns true. Wrong arity, a non-Set argument, and conflicting mutation/transfer during argument evaluation are static errors. Set-like records are not accepted.

Keys follow existing native key equality: NaN equals NaN, negative zero equals zero, and compatible numeric alternatives can match. Distinct string/boolean/null/undefined alternatives do not match; enum keys retain their enum type identity. Large int-to-number comparisons can lose precision.

Example: `const values = new Set<int>([1, 2]); console.log(values.isSubsetOf(new Set<int>([1, 2, 3])));` prints `true`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([1, 2]); console.log(values.isSubsetOf(new Set<int>([1, 2, 3])));
// prints true
```

Ownership: both Sets and their owned keys borrow readonly. No keys are cloned or transferred.

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([1, 2]); console.log(values.isSubsetOf(new Set<int>([1, 2, 3])));

Set.name: isSupersetOf
Set.documentation:
Tests whether every key in another Set occurs in the receiver. Takes exactly one other Set, whose key type may differ from the receiver. Returns a boolean and does not mutate either input. An empty argument returns true. Wrong arity, a non-Set argument, and conflicting mutation/transfer during argument evaluation are static errors. Set-like records are not accepted.

Keys follow existing native key equality: NaN equals NaN, negative zero equals zero, and compatible numeric alternatives can match. Distinct string/boolean/null/undefined alternatives do not match; enum keys retain their enum type identity. Large int-to-number comparisons can lose precision.

Example: `const values = new Set<string>(["a", "b"]); console.log(values.isSupersetOf(new Set<string>(["b"])));` prints `true`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<string>(["a", "b"]); console.log(values.isSupersetOf(new Set<string>(["b"])));
// prints true
```

Ownership: both Sets and their owned keys borrow readonly. No keys are cloned or transferred.

examples.source: const values = new Set<string>(["a", "b"]); console.log(values.isSupersetOf(new Set<string>(["b"])));

Set.name: isDisjointFrom
Set.documentation:
Tests whether the receiver and another Set share no keys. Takes exactly one other Set, whose key type may differ from the receiver. Returns a boolean and does not mutate either input. If either Set is empty, returns true. Wrong arity, a non-Set argument, and conflicting mutation/transfer during argument evaluation are static errors. Set-like records are not accepted.

Keys follow existing native key equality: NaN equals NaN, negative zero equals zero, and compatible numeric alternatives can match. Distinct string/boolean/null/undefined alternatives do not match; enum keys retain their enum type identity. Large int-to-number comparisons can lose precision.

Example: `const values = new Set<int>([1, 2]); console.log(values.isDisjointFrom(new Set<string>(["1", "2"])));` prints `true`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([1, 2]); console.log(values.isDisjointFrom(new Set<string>(["1", "2"])));
// prints true
```

Ownership: both Sets and their owned keys borrow readonly. No keys are cloned or transferred.

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([1, 2]); console.log(values.isDisjointFrom(new Set<string>(["1", "2"])));

Set.name: union
Set.documentation:
Returns an independent Set containing keys from either input. Takes exactly one Set; its key type may differ. Neither input is mutated. Receiver keys come first, followed by new keys in other insertion order. Empty inputs follow these same rules. Wrong arity, non-Set arguments and conflicting receiver mutation/transfer during argument evaluation are static errors. Set-like records are not accepted.

Key comparisons retain existing native SameValueZero and enum identity rules. Large int/number overlap can lose precision. Union and symmetric difference infer a joined key type; intersection and difference keep the receiver key type.

Example: `const values = new Set<int>([3, 1]); const result = values.union(new Set<int>([1, 2])); console.log(result.values().join(","));` prints `3,1,2`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([3, 1]); const result = values.union(new Set<int>([1, 2])); console.log(result.values().join(","));
// prints 3,1,2
```

Ownership: both inputs borrow. This explicit result-producing operation copies selected keys, including owned text, into an independent Set. Binding or reading a Set never implicitly clones it.

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([3, 1]); const result = values.union(new Set<int>([1, 2])); console.log(result.values().join(","));

Set.name: intersection
Set.documentation:
Returns an independent Set containing receiver keys also present in other. Takes exactly one Set; its key type may differ. Neither input is mutated. Results follow the insertion order of the smaller Set; ties use receiver order. Matching receiver keys are copied so the receiver key type is preserved. When numeric precision loss lets one other key match multiple exact receiver keys, all those receiver keys are retained. Empty inputs follow these same rules. Wrong arity, non-Set arguments and conflicting receiver mutation/transfer during argument evaluation are static errors. Set-like records are not accepted.

Key comparisons retain existing native SameValueZero and enum identity rules. Large int/number overlap can lose precision. Union and symmetric difference infer a joined key type; intersection and difference keep the receiver key type.

Example: `const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.intersection(new Set<int>([2, 1])); console.log(result.values().join(","));` prints `2,1`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.intersection(new Set<int>([2, 1])); console.log(result.values().join(","));
// prints 2,1
```

Ownership: both inputs borrow. This explicit result-producing operation copies selected keys, including owned text, into an independent Set. Binding or reading a Set never implicitly clones it.

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.intersection(new Set<int>([2, 1])); console.log(result.values().join(","));

Set.name: difference
Set.documentation:
Returns an independent Set containing receiver keys absent from other. Takes exactly one Set; its key type may differ. Neither input is mutated. Results follow receiver insertion order and preserve its key type. Empty inputs follow these same rules. Wrong arity, non-Set arguments and conflicting receiver mutation/transfer during argument evaluation are static errors. Set-like records are not accepted.

Key comparisons retain existing native SameValueZero and enum identity rules. Large int/number overlap can lose precision. Union and symmetric difference infer a joined key type; intersection and difference keep the receiver key type.

Example: `const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.difference(new Set<int>([1, 2])); console.log(result.values().join(","));` prints `3`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.difference(new Set<int>([1, 2])); console.log(result.values().join(","));
// prints 3
```

Ownership: both inputs borrow. This explicit result-producing operation copies selected keys, including owned text, into an independent Set. Binding or reading a Set never implicitly clones it.

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.difference(new Set<int>([1, 2])); console.log(result.values().join(","));

Set.name: symmetricDifference
Set.documentation:
Returns an independent Set containing keys present in exactly one input. Takes exactly one Set; its key type may differ. Neither input is mutated. Unshared receiver keys come first, followed by unshared other keys in their insertion order. Empty inputs follow these same rules. Wrong arity, non-Set arguments and conflicting receiver mutation/transfer during argument evaluation are static errors. Set-like records are not accepted.

Key comparisons retain existing native SameValueZero and enum identity rules. Large int/number overlap can lose precision. Union and symmetric difference infer a joined key type; intersection and difference keep the receiver key type.

Example: `const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.symmetricDifference(new Set<int>([2, 4, 1])); console.log(result.values().join(","));` prints `3,4`.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.symmetricDifference(new Set<int>([2, 4, 1])); console.log(result.values().join(","));
// prints 3,4
```

Ownership: both inputs borrow. This explicit result-producing operation copies selected keys, including owned text, into an independent Set. Binding or reading a Set never implicitly clones it.

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([3, 1, 2]); const result = values.symmetricDifference(new Set<int>([2, 4, 1])); console.log(result.values().join(","));

Map.name: size
Map.documentation:
Returns the number of distinct keys. This property is readonly; assignment is rejected. It takes no arguments.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.size); // 1
```

Ownership: receiver is read and unchanged.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.size);

Map.name: set
Map.documentation:
Inserts a key and value, or replaces the value for an existing key. Replacement keeps the key’s original insertion position. Returns void; chaining is unsupported.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); values.set("a", 3); console.log(values.size, values.get("a") ?? 0); // 1 3
```

Ownership: owned keys and values transfer into the receiver; scalar inputs copy. Receiver mutates.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); values.set("a", 3); console.log(values.size, values.get("a") ?? 0);

Map.name: get
Map.documentation:
Reads the value for a key, or returns undefined when absent. Stored undefined remains distinguishable through has(). Receiver is unchanged.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.get("a") ?? 0, values.get("missing") ?? 0); // 1 0
```

Ownership: key is borrowed. Scalar values copy; owned values from a named receiver are readonly borrows and block mutation or transfer of that receiver while the borrow is in scope. A temporary receiver is consumed and its selected owned value moves out. Use clone() explicitly to own a copy of a borrowed value.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.get("a") ?? 0, values.get("missing") ?? 0);

Map.name: has
Map.documentation:
Reports whether a matching key exists, including when its stored value is undefined. Receiver is unchanged.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.has("a"), values.has("missing")); // true false
```

Ownership: receiver and key are borrowed.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.has("a"), values.has("missing"));

Map.name: delete
Map.documentation:
Removes a key and value and returns true, or returns false if absent. Remaining entries keep their order. Deleting and reinserting a key places it last.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.delete("a"), values.delete("a"), values.size); // true false 0
```

Ownership: key is borrowed; receiver mutates and the removed value is dropped.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.delete("a"), values.delete("a"), values.size);

Map.name: clear
Map.documentation:
Removes all entries and returns void. Takes no arguments.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); values.clear(); console.log(values.size); // 0
```

Ownership: receiver mutates; all keys and values are dropped.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); values.clear(); console.log(values.size);

Map.name: keys

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>([["b", 2], ["a", 1]]); console.log(values.keys().join(","));

Map.documentation:
Returns an independent array of keys in insertion order. Takes no arguments and does not mutate the receiver. An empty Map returns an empty array. Replacement preserves the key position; deletion and reinsertion places it last. Later receiver changes do not change the snapshot. This operation returns an array snapshot, not a live iterator.

Example: `const values = new Map<string, int>([["b", 2], ["a", 1]]); console.log(values.keys().join(","));` prints `b,a`.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>([["b", 2], ["a", 1]]); console.log(values.keys().join(","));
// prints b,a
```

Ownership: Explicitly copies owned keys; the receiver stays usable.

Map.name: values

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>([["a", 1], ["b", 2], ["a", 3]]); console.log(values.values().join(","));

Map.documentation:
Returns an independent array of values in key insertion order. Takes no arguments and does not mutate the receiver. An empty Map returns an empty array. Replacement preserves the key position; deletion and reinsertion places it last. Later receiver changes do not change the snapshot. This operation returns an array snapshot, not a live iterator.

Example: `const values = new Map<string, int>([["a", 1], ["b", 2], ["a", 3]]); console.log(values.values().join(","));` prints `3,2`.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>([["a", 1], ["b", 2], ["a", 3]]); console.log(values.values().join(","));
// prints 3,2
```

Ownership: Explicitly copies owned values, including nested owned storage. Values must support cloning; the receiver stays usable.

Map.name: entries

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>([["a", 3]]); const pairs = values.entries(); console.log(pairs[0][0], pairs[0][1]);

Map.documentation:
Returns an independent array of key/value tuples in insertion order. Takes no arguments and does not mutate the receiver. An empty Map returns an empty array. Replacement preserves the key position; deletion and reinsertion places it last. Later receiver changes do not change the snapshot. This operation returns an array snapshot, not a live iterator.

Example: `const values = new Map<string, int>([["a", 3]]); const pairs = values.entries(); console.log(pairs[0][0], pairs[0][1]);` prints `a 3`.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>([["a", 3]]); const pairs = values.entries(); console.log(pairs[0][0], pairs[0][1]);
// prints a 3
```

Ownership: Explicitly copies owned keys and values into owned tuples. Values must support cloning; the receiver stays usable.

Map.name: forEach
Map.signature: forEach(callback: (value: Value, key: Key, source: Map<Key, Value>) => Result): void
parameters: callback: (value: Value, key: Key, source: Map<Key, Value>) => Result
Map.documentation:
Calls a reusable callback once for each entry in insertion order. The callback receives the value, its key, and the readonly source Map. Replacing a key preserves its position; deletion and reinsertion places it last. An empty Map does not call the callback. Callbacks may use zero through three supplied positions; normal default and rest parameter rules apply. There is no thisArg argument. Wrong arity, incompatible parameter types/access, consuming callbacks, and receiver mutation or transfer during iteration are static errors.

Returns void and does not mutate the receiver. Each callback result is evaluated and discarded. A checked callback error stops iteration and propagates to surrounding catch/finally. External mutable captures are allowed when they do not conflict with receiver borrows.

Example: `const values = new Map<string, int>([["b", 2], ["a", 1]]); let text = ""; values.forEach((value, key) => { text = text + key + String(value) + "|"; }); console.log(text);` prints `b2|a1|`.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>([["b", 2], ["a", 1]]); let text = ""; values.forEach((value, key) => { text = text + key + String(value) + "|"; }); console.log(text);
// prints b2|a1|
```

Ownership: scalar keys and values copy; owned keys and values borrow readonly, as does the source Map. No owned callback input is implicitly cloned. Values need not support cloning.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>([["b", 2], ["a", 1]]); let text = ""; values.forEach((value, key) => { text = text + key + String(value) + "|"; }); console.log(text);

MapConstructor.name: groupBy
MapConstructor.signature: groupBy<Element, Key>(source: Element[] | string | Set<Element> | Map<unknown, unknown>, callback: (value: ReadOnly<Element>, index: int) => Key): Map<Key, Element[]>
parameters: source: Element[] | string | Set<Element> | Map<unknown, unknown>

Deque.name: size
Deque.documentation:
Returns the number of stored elements as int. This readonly property takes no arguments. Assignment is rejected. The receiver is unchanged. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1.

Ownership: The receiver is borrowed readonly.

Deque.name: pushFront
Deque.documentation:
Inserts one value before the current first element. Exactly one value of the declared element type is required. Returns void and increases size by one. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushFront(2);console.log(values.popFront()!);}
```

Expected output: 2.

Ownership: Owned values transfer into the queue; scalar values copy. Borrowed payloads retain their original owners. The receiver must allow mutation.

Deque.name: pushBack
Deque.documentation:
Inserts one value after the current last element. Exactly one value of the declared element type is required. Returns void and increases size by one. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.popBack()!);}
```

Expected output: 2.

Ownership: Owned values transfer into the queue; scalar values copy. Borrowed payloads retain their original owners. The receiver must allow mutation.

Deque.name: popFront
Deque.documentation:
Removes and returns the first element, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. A successful removal decreases size by one. An empty queue stays empty. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.popFront()!,values.size);}
```

Expected output: 4 1.

Ownership: The removed value transfers to the caller without cloning. Borrowed payloads retain their original owners. The receiver must allow mutation.

Deque.name: popBack
Deque.documentation:
Removes and returns the last element, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. A successful removal decreases size by one. An empty queue stays empty. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.popBack()!,values.size);}
```

Expected output: 2 1.

Ownership: The removed value transfers to the caller without cloning. Borrowed payloads retain their original owners. The receiver must allow mutation.

Deque.name: front
Deque.documentation:
Reads the first element, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. Returns Element | undefined and leaves the receiver unchanged. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.front()!,values.size);}
```

Expected output: 4 2.

Ownership: Scalar elements copy. Owned elements borrow readonly from a stored receiver and block its mutation or transfer while the borrow remains in scope. Temporary receivers cannot supply owned borrowed elements.

Deque.name: back
Deque.documentation:
Reads the last element, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. Returns Element | undefined and leaves the receiver unchanged. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.back()!,values.size);}
```

Expected output: 2 2.

Ownership: Scalar elements copy. Owned elements borrow readonly from a stored receiver and block its mutation or transfer while the borrow remains in scope. Temporary receivers cannot supply owned borrowed elements.

Deque.name: at
Deque.documentation:
Reads the element at a zero-based index counted from the front. Exactly one signed 64-bit int index is required. Negative indices and indices at or beyond size return undefined; negative indices do not count from the end. Returns Element | undefined and leaves the receiver unchanged. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.at(1)!,values.at(-1)===undefined);}
```

Expected output: 2 true.

Ownership: Scalar elements copy. Owned elements borrow readonly from a stored receiver and block its mutation or transfer while the borrow remains in scope. Temporary receivers cannot supply owned borrowed elements.

Deque.name: clear
Deque.documentation:
Removes every element and sets size to zero. Takes no arguments and returns void. Clearing an empty queue has no effect. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.clear();console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 0.

Ownership: Stored owned values are released. The receiver must allow mutation. Existing view-owner restrictions remain conservatively active until the queue binding leaves scope.

std:collections.name: OrderedMap
std:collections.documentation:
An owned map that visits entries in ascending key order. new OrderedMap<K, V>() creates empty independent storage, takes no arguments and requires explicit key and value types. Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors. for...of borrows [key, value] entries without removing them. Spread into readonly tuple parameters borrows entries and leaves the map usable. Array spread and owning rest arguments transfer entries in ascending key order, consuming the map without cloning payloads. Array.from(map, mapper) supplies borrowed entries and zero-based indices in ascending key order; the mapper cannot mutate the map. Array.from(map) creates an independent entry snapshot when keys and values support cloning. clone(map) creates independent storage when both types support cloning; views remain non-cloneable.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);for(const entry of values){console.log(entry[0],entry[1]);}}
```

Expected output: a 1
b 2.

Ownership: set transfers owned keys and values. Borrowed views and callbacks retain their owner lifetimes. Traversal prevents receiver mutation or transfer. Storage releases when its owner ends.

examples.source: import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);for(const entry of values){console.log(entry[0],entry[1]);}}

std:collections.name: OrderedSet
std:collections.documentation:
An owned set that visits unique values in ascending key order. new OrderedSet<T>() takes no arguments and requires an explicit int, number, boolean, string or enum element type. Numbers compare numerically; signed zeros share one positive-zero key and all NaNs share one key greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. for...of visits each stored value once in ascending order without removing it. Empty sets perform no iterations. clone(set) creates independent storage. Call and array spread follow ascending order; scalar elements copy, readonly call arguments borrow strings, and owning string arguments transfer the set. Mutable key arguments are rejected. Ownership: add transfers owned keys; iteration borrows strings and prevents receiver mutation or transfer. Storage releases when its owner ends.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(3);values.add(1);values.add(3);for(const value of values){console.log(value);}console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1
3
2.

examples.source: import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(3);values.add(1);values.add(3);for(const value of values){console.log(value);}console.log(values.size);}

std:collections.name: Deque
std:collections.documentation:
An owned double-ended queue of values of type T. Construct an empty queue with new Deque<T>(); the constructor takes no arguments and requires an explicit element type. Construction returns independent empty storage. Storage releases automatically when its owner ends. Record literals, comparison and inspection are currently unsupported. clone(queue) creates independent storage and deep-clones each element. It borrows the source without changing it. Cloning is rejected when any element contains a byte view, resource or callback that cannot be cloned. for...of visits elements from front to back without removing them. Scalar elements copy; owned elements borrow readonly for the iteration. Mutation or transfer of the queue during iteration is rejected. Empty queues perform no loop iterations. Call spread copies scalar elements, borrows owned elements for readonly parameters, or transfers the collection for owning parameters. Array spread copies scalars and transfers owned elements. Deque spread preserves front-to-back order; Heap spread order is unspecified. Mutable Heap element arguments are rejected to preserve heap ordering. Ownership: passing by value transfers the queue; borrowed element types retain their original owners.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections"; function accept(values:Deque<int>):void{} function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();accept(values);}
```

Expected output: none.

Records with readonly callbacks retain captured owners while stored or removed. A removed callback still borrows its captures.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";type Reader={read:ReadOnly<Function<int>>;};function main(){const text="hello";const values=new Deque<Reader>();values.pushBack({read:()=>text.length});for(const item of values){console.log(item.read());}}
```

Expected output: 5.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function sum(...values:int[]):int{let total=0;for(const value of values){total+=value;}return total;}function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(2);values.pushBack(3);console.log(sum(...values),values.size);}
```

Expected output: 5 2.

Nested readonly indexing borrows the stored array. It copies scalar elements and borrows owned elements; assignment through this view is rejected.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int[]>();values.pushBack([4,5]);console.log(values.front()![0],values.back()![1],values.size);}
```

Expected output: 4 5 1.

examples.source: import {Deque} from "std:collections"; function accept(values:Deque<int>):void{} function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();accept(values);}

import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(2);values.pushFront(1);let sum=0;for(const value of values){sum+=value;}console.log(sum,values.size);}

import {Deque} from "std:collections";type Reader={read:ReadOnly<Function<int>>;};function main(){const text="hello";const values=new Deque<Reader>();values.pushBack({read:()=>text.length});for(const item of values){console.log(item.read());}}

import {Deque} from "std:collections";function sum(...values:int[]):int{let total=0;for(const value of values){total+=value;}return total;}function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(2);values.pushBack(3);console.log(sum(...values),values.size);}

std:collections.name: Heap
std:collections.documentation:
An owned max heap: peek reads the greatest value and pop removes it. new Heap<T>() takes no arguments and requires an explicit int, number, boolean, string or enum element type. Numbers use numeric order, with all NaNs equal and greater than infinity; signed zeros are stored as positive zero. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order, without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place true above false. Enums use their backing values. Duplicate values remain separate entries. for...of borrows every stored element without removal in unspecified order. Scalar loop values copy; strings borrow readonly. Mutation or transfer during traversal is rejected. Repeated pop consumes values in descending order. clone(heap) deep-clones independent storage.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(2);values.push(9);console.log(values.pop()!,values.pop()!);}
```

Expected output: 9 2.

Call spread copies scalar elements, borrows owned elements for readonly parameters, or transfers the collection for owning parameters. Array spread copies scalars and transfers owned elements. Deque spread preserves front-to-back order; Heap spread order is unspecified. Mutable Heap element arguments are rejected to preserve heap ordering. Ownership: passing by value transfers the heap; storage releases automatically when its owner ends.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function sum(...values:int[]):int{let total=0;for(const value of values){total+=value;}return total;}function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(2);values.push(3);console.log(sum(...values),values.size);}
```

Expected output: 5 2.

examples.source: import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(2);values.push(9);let sum=0;for(const value of values){sum+=value;}console.log(sum,values.size);}

import {Heap} from "std:collections";function sum(...values:int[]):int{let total=0;for(const value of values){total+=value;}return total;}function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(2);values.push(3);console.log(sum(...values),values.size);}

std:fs.name: File
std:fs.documentation:
An owned open file with private storage. Use open for an existing read-only file, create for a new or truncated write-only file, read/write/writeAll for cursor operations, and close for explicit release. File literals, clone, comparison, hashing, console inspection and implicit sharing are unsupported. Unclosed files release automatically on scope exit. Explicit close consumes the handle even on failure; later use is rejected. No implicit flush or durability synchronization occurs. Ownership: passing by value transfers the handle; Mutable<File> borrows it for cursor-changing reads and writes.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {File} from "std:fs"; function inspect(file:ReadOnly<File>):void{} function main(){}
```

Expected output: none.

examples.source: import {File} from "std:fs"; function inspect(file:ReadOnly<File>):void{} function main(){}

std:fs.name: FsError
std:fs.signature: type FsError = { code: string; operation: string; message: string; osCode?: int; }
std:fs.documentation:
A file operation failure. code is a stable category: not-found, permission-denied, invalid-input, interrupted, is-directory, would-block, io, length-range, allocation, capacity-range or write-zero. operation names open, create, read, write, writeAll, readFile, writeFile, bufferReader, bufferWriter, flush or close. message explains the failure; its text is not stable. osCode preserves the platform error number when available, otherwise undefined. This record type takes no arguments and changes no file. Ownership: strings are owned; borrowing fields leaves the error reusable.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined.

code.documentation:
Stable failure category, as a string. Reading this field changes no file.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined. Ownership: string fields may be borrowed or explicitly cloned; osCode copies.

operation.documentation:
Operation that failed: open, create, read, write, writeAll, readFile, writeFile, bufferReader, bufferWriter, flush or close. Reading this field changes no file.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined. Ownership: string fields may be borrowed or explicitly cloned; osCode copies.

message.documentation:
Human-readable description. Text may vary by platform. Reading this field changes no file.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined. Ownership: string fields may be borrowed or explicitly cloned; osCode copies.

osCode.documentation:
Optional platform error number. Missing values read as undefined; range/allocation failures have no OS code. Reading this field changes no file.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined. Ownership: string fields may be borrowed or explicitly cloned; osCode copies.

std:fs.name: open

parameters.label: path: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required path to an existing file. Relative paths use the process working directory; no default. Borrowed without mutation.

std:fs.documentation:
Opens an existing path read-only at cursor zero. Does not create or truncate files. Returns Ok(File) or an open error; missing paths, permissions and embedded NUL are reported. Opening a directory may succeed, but reading it fails. Paths follow normal filesystem symlink resolution. The example assumes input.bin exists. Ownership: path is borrowed; success creates a unique file owner.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.


std:bytes.signature: append(bytes: Mutable<Bytes>, values: ReadOnly<int[]>): Result<void, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: Mutable<Bytes>
parameters.documentation: Buffer to extend through an exclusive borrow.

parameters.label: values: ReadOnly<int[]>
parameters.documentation: Integers in 0..255 to append in order. The array is borrowed and unchanged.

std:bytes.documentation:
Adds checked integer values to the end of a byte buffer in array order. Returns Ok() on success; an empty array succeeds without changing the buffer. Each value must be in 0..255. Checks the combined byte length first, then every input value, before reserving storage or changing contents. An invalid value returns byte-range with its index in the input array as offset. A combined length outside native storage returns length-range with an undefined offset. Failed reservation returns allocation with an undefined offset. Every failure preserves the original length and contents. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable. Byte values are copied explicitly from the array; no integer wrapping occurs.

```tsrust
import {fromArray,append,length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(fromArray([65])){Ok(bytes)=>{match(append(bytes,[0,255])){Ok(_)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: 3.

Ownership: borrows the buffer exclusively and the array readonly for the call. Neither input is consumed or implicitly cloned.

std:bytes.name: copy
std:bytes.signature: copy(bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>, start: int, end: int): Result<Bytes, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Source buffer, borrowed without mutation. Also accepts a ByteView or ByteViewMut; indices and counts are relative to the view.

parameters.label: start: int
parameters.documentation: Inclusive starting byte index, from 0 through length(bytes). Checked before end.

parameters.label: end: int
parameters.documentation: Exclusive ending byte index, from start through length(bytes).

std:bytes.documentation:
Creates an independent owned buffer containing bytes in the half-open range [start, end). Returns Ok(buffer); start equal to end produces an empty buffer, including at the source end. Bounds must satisfy 0 <= start <= end <= length(bytes). Negative indices never wrap and bounds are not clamped. Checks start first, then end; an invalid range returns range with the first offending coordinate as offset. A reversed range reports end. Failed reservation returns allocation with an undefined offset. The source remains unchanged on success and failure. Changing either buffer afterward cannot change the other. Coordinates count bytes, not Unicode characters. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable.

```tsrust
import {fromArray,copy,length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(fromArray([0,65,255])){Ok(bytes)=>{match(copy(bytes,1,3)){Ok(part)=>{console.log(length(part));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: 2.

Ownership: borrows the source readonly and returns a new independent owner. Copying is explicit and does not transfer the source.

std:bytes.name: fromUtf8

parameters.label: text: string
parameters.documentation: Valid UTF-8 text to encode. Borrowed unchanged; no implicit conversion from other types.

std:bytes.documentation:
Copies the UTF-8 encoding of a string into an independent owned byte buffer. Takes exactly one string and returns Ok(buffer), including an empty buffer for empty text. Text is already valid UTF-8; no normalization, BOM stripping or replacement occurs. NUL bytes and multibyte Unicode scalars are preserved. Length counts encoded bytes rather than characters. A length outside native storage returns length-range; failed reservation returns allocation. Both errors omit offset. No partial buffer escapes. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable.

```tsrust
import {fromUtf8,length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(fromUtf8("é😀")){Ok(bytes)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: 6.

Ownership: borrows the input and returns independent owned storage; no input is consumed or implicitly cloned.

std:bytes.name: toUtf8
std:bytes.signature: toUtf8(bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>): Result<string, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte buffer to decode strictly. Borrowed unchanged; invalid bytes are never replaced. Also accepts a ByteView or ByteViewMut; indices and counts are relative to the view.

std:bytes.documentation:
Decodes a byte buffer strictly into an independent owned UTF-8 string. Takes exactly one byte buffer and returns Ok(text), including an empty string for an empty buffer. Invalid, overlong, surrogate or truncated sequences return utf8 with message "Byte buffer contains invalid UTF-8." and offset equal to the first invalid sequence start in bytes. No replacement characters are inserted. NUL and a leading U+FEFF are preserved; no normalization or BOM stripping occurs. Valid text is checked once, then copied to reserved output storage. Failed reservation returns allocation with an undefined offset. The buffer is unchanged on success and failure. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable.

```tsrust
import {fromArray,toUtf8} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(fromArray([195,169,240,159,152,128])){Ok(bytes)=>{match(toUtf8(bytes)){Ok(text)=>{console.log(text);},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: é😀.

Ownership: borrows the input and returns independent owned storage; no input is consumed or implicitly cloned.

std:bytes.name: ByteView
ByteViewMut
view
std:bytes.signature: view(bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>, start: int, end: int): Result<ByteView, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte owner or view to look into without copying or mutation. A readonly ByteView forwards its byte owner lifetime; Bytes and ByteViewMut stay borrowed for the result lifetime.

parameters.label: start: int
parameters.documentation: Inclusive starting byte index, from 0 through length(bytes). Checked before end.

parameters.label: end: int
parameters.documentation: Exclusive ending byte index, from start through length(bytes).

std:bytes.documentation:
Returns a readonly window onto the bytes in the half-open range [start, end) without copying them. Returns Ok(view); start equal to end produces an empty view, including at the end of the bytes. Bounds must satisfy 0 <= start <= end <= length(bytes). Negative indices never wrap and bounds are not clamped. Checks start first, then end; an invalid range returns the error code range with the first offending coordinate as offset. A reversed range reports end. There is no allocation, so there is no allocation error. The view reads the owner's bytes: it has the same contents as the owner for as long as it exists. Coordinates count bytes, not Unicode characters; a range that splits a character makes toUtf8 of the view fail. A view of a view uses coordinates relative to that view. A readonly ByteView forwards the original byte owner lifetime, so the new view can outlive the intermediate view or its container. A ByteViewMut source remains borrowed for the result lifetime.

```tsrust
import { fromUtf8, view, toUtf8 } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromUtf8("hello")) { Ok(bytes) => { match (view(bytes, 1, 4)) { Ok(part) => { match (toUtf8(part)) { Ok(text) => { console.log(text); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }
```

Expected output: ell.

Ownership: borrows the bytes readonly. While the view is in scope the owner can be read and cannot be written, resized, moved or replaced. The view cannot be returned from the function that owns the bytes. Use copy for bytes that must outlive their owner.

examples.source:
import { fromUtf8, view, toUtf8 } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromUtf8("hello")) { Ok(bytes) => { match (view(bytes, 1, 4)) { Ok(part) => { match (toUtf8(part)) { Ok(text) => { console.log(text); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }

std:bytes.name: viewMut
std:bytes.signature: viewMut(bytes: Mutable<Bytes | ByteViewMut>, start: int, end: int): Result<ByteViewMut, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: Mutable<Bytes | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte owner or exclusive view to write into. Borrowed exclusively, without copying, for as long as the result is in scope.

parameters.label: start: int
parameters.documentation: Inclusive starting byte index, from 0 through length(bytes). Checked before end.

parameters.label: end: int
parameters.documentation: Exclusive ending byte index, from start through length(bytes).

std:bytes.documentation:
Returns an exclusive, writable window onto the bytes in the half-open range [start, end) without copying them. Returns Ok(view); start equal to end produces an empty view. Bounds must satisfy 0 <= start <= end <= length(bytes). Negative indices never wrap and bounds are not clamped. Checks start first, then end; an invalid range returns the error code range with the first offending coordinate as offset. A reversed range reports end. There is no allocation. set through the view changes the owner's bytes at start plus the view index. The view has a fixed length and cannot resize the owner. A readonly ByteView cannot supply an exclusive view.

```tsrust
import { fromUtf8, viewMut, set, toUtf8 } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromUtf8("hello")) { Ok(bytes) => { match (viewMut(bytes, 0, 1)) { Ok(part) => { match (set(part, 0, 72)) { Ok(_) => {}, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } match (toUtf8(bytes)) { Ok(text) => { console.log(text); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }
```

Expected output: Hello.

Ownership: borrows the bytes exclusively. While the view is in scope the owner cannot be read, written, resized, moved or replaced. The owner is usable again, with the written bytes, after the view's scope ends.

examples.source:
import { fromUtf8, viewMut, set, toUtf8 } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromUtf8("hello")) { Ok(bytes) => { match (viewMut(bytes, 0, 1)) { Ok(part) => { match (set(part, 0, 72)) { Ok(_) => {}, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } match (toUtf8(bytes)) { Ok(text) => { console.log(text); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }

OrderedSet.name: size
OrderedSet.documentation:
The number of distinct stored keys, including at most one NaN and one zero key. This read-only property takes no arguments, returns a nonnegative int, and does not change the set. Ownership: reading size borrows the receiver.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1.

OrderedSet.name: add
OrderedSet.documentation:
Insert value if no equal key is present. value must have the declared element type. A duplicate leaves size unchanged; signed zeros and NaNs follow the set equality rule. Returns void and may change the set. Ownership: an owned argument transfers even when it duplicates an existing key.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);values.add(2);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1.

OrderedSet.name: has
OrderedSet.documentation:
Test whether an equal key is stored. value must have the declared element type; an empty set returns false. Returns boolean without changing the set. Lookup follows the key order. Ownership: the receiver and argument are borrowed; string queries remain reusable and are not copied.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);console.log(values.has(2),values.has(9));}
```

Expected output: true false.

OrderedSet.name: delete
OrderedSet.documentation:
Remove the equal key if present. value must have the declared element type. Returns true after removal, or false when no key matched, including on an empty set. Ownership: the receiver is exclusively borrowed; the query argument is borrowed and remains reusable.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);console.log(values.delete(2),values.delete(2),values.size);}
```

Expected output: true false 0.

OrderedSet.name: clear
OrderedSet.documentation:
Remove all keys. Takes no arguments, returns void and leaves size zero. Clearing an empty set succeeds. Ownership: exclusively borrows the receiver and releases its stored keys.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);values.clear();console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 0.

Heap.name: size
Heap.documentation:
Returns the readonly number of stored values. Takes no arguments and leaves the heap unchanged. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

Heap.name: push
Heap.documentation:
Transfers one value of the declared element type into the heap. Returns void and increases size by one. Equal values are stored separately. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);values.push(9);console.log(values.pop()!);}
```

Expected output: 9.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

Heap.name: peek
Heap.documentation:
Returns the greatest value without removal, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. Scalar results copy; owned string results borrow from a stored receiver. Mutation is rejected while that borrow remains live. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);console.log(values.peek(),values.size);}
```

Expected output: 3 1.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

Heap.name: pop
Heap.documentation:
Removes and returns the greatest value, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. Removal transfers an owned value to the caller. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);console.log(values.pop(),values.size,values.pop());}
```

Expected output: 3 0 undefined.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

Heap.name: clear
Heap.documentation:
Releases every stored value and sets size to zero. Takes no arguments and returns void. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);values.clear();console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 0.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

OrderedMap.name: size
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns the number of distinct keys as int. Readonly property with no arguments; assignment is rejected. Empty maps have size 0. The receiver is unchanged.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 2

Ownership: Reading size borrows the receiver.

OrderedMap.name: set
OrderedMap.documentation:
Inserts key and value, or replaces the value of an equal key. Takes exactly two arguments matching Key and Value; returns void. Replacing a key leaves size unchanged. Traversal remains in ascending key order.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);values.set("a",3);console.log(values.size,values.get("a")!);}
```

Expected output: 2 3

Ownership: Owned arguments transfer into the map. Replacement releases the previous value; stored views retain their original owner loans.

OrderedMap.name: get
OrderedMap.documentation:
Reads the value for key, or returns undefined when absent. Takes one key argument. The receiver is unchanged for a stored map. No default value is inserted.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.get("a") ?? 0,values.get("missing") ?? 0);}
```

Expected output: 1 0

Ownership: The key is borrowed. Scalar results copy; owned results from a stored map borrow readonly. A consumed temporary transfers its selected owned value and releases the other entries.

OrderedMap.name: has
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns true when key is present and false otherwise. Takes one key argument and leaves the receiver unchanged.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.has("a"),values.has("missing"));}
```

Expected output: true false

Ownership: Receiver and owned query key are borrowed.

OrderedMap.name: delete
OrderedMap.documentation:
Removes key and its value, returning true if present or false if absent. Takes one key argument. Successful removal reduces size by one; deleting an absent key changes nothing.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.delete("a"),values.delete("a"),values.size);}
```

Expected output: true false 1

Ownership: The query key is borrowed. Removal releases the stored key and value. Retained entry borrows prevent mutation.

OrderedMap.name: clear
OrderedMap.documentation:
Removes every entry and returns void. Takes no arguments. Size becomes 0; clearing an empty map is valid.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);values.clear();console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 0

Ownership: Removed keys and values are released. Retained entry borrows prevent mutation.

OrderedMap.name: keys
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns an independent array of keys in ascending key order. Takes no arguments, leaves the receiver unchanged and returns an empty array for an empty map.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.keys().join(","));}
```

Expected output: a,b

Ownership: Keys are explicitly copied or cloned into independent array storage.

OrderedMap.name: values
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns an independent array of values in ascending key order. Takes no arguments and leaves the receiver unchanged. Empty maps produce an empty array. Values must support independent cloning; views and other non-cloneable values are rejected.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.values().join(","));}
```

Expected output: 1,2

Ownership: Values are explicitly deep-cloned into independent array storage.

OrderedMap.name: entries
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns an independent array of [key, value] tuples in ascending key order. Takes no arguments and leaves the receiver unchanged. Empty maps produce an empty array. Both payload types must support independent cloning.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);const pairs=values.entries();console.log(pairs[0][0],pairs[0][1]);}
```

Expected output: a 1

Ownership: Keys and values are explicitly deep-cloned. Use for...of for borrowed entry traversal.

OrderedMap.name: forEach
OrderedMap.signature: forEach(callback: (value: Value, key: Key, source: OrderedMap<Key, Value>) => Result): void
parameters: callback: (value: Value, key: Key, source: OrderedMap<Key, Value>) => Result
OrderedMap.documentation:
Calls callback once for each entry in ascending key order, supplying value, key and source. Takes one callback; the callback may omit trailing parameters. Returns void and ignores callback return values. An empty map makes no calls. The receiver is unchanged; callback failures propagate.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);let text="";values.forEach((value,key)=>{text+=key+String(value)+"|";});console.log(text);}
```

Expected output: a1|b2|

Ownership: Traversal borrows the receiver and owned payloads. Receiver mutation or transfer during traversal is rejected.

std:env.name: EnvError
std:env.signature: type EnvError = { code: string; message: string }
std:env.documentation:
Describes an environment or process-argument failure. code is InvalidName for an empty name or a name containing = or NUL, or NotUnicode when a value or process argument cannot be represented as Unicode. message explains the failure without including the environment value or argument. Missing variables are successful lookups, not errors. Fields are ordinary strings.

```tsrust
import {EnvError} from "std:env"; function describe(error:ReadOnly<EnvError>):string{return error.code + ": " + error.message;} function main(){}
```

Expected output: none. Ownership: an owned record; explicit clone creates independent storage.

examples.source: import {EnvError} from "std:env"; function describe(error:ReadOnly<EnvError>):string{return error.code + ": " + error.message;} function main(){}

std:env.name: get

parameters.label: name: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required nonempty variable name. Must not contain = or NUL. Uses the executable host’s case-sensitivity rules.

std:env.documentation:
Reads a variable from the running process environment. Returns Ok(value) with an independent UTF-8 string when present, Ok(undefined) when missing, or Err(EnvError). An empty value returns Ok(""). Empty names and names containing = or NUL fail with InvalidName. Non-Unicode values fail with NotUnicode; no lossy replacement occurs. Lookup uses host name matching rules and does not mutate the environment. Values are read at execution time.

```tsrust
import {get} from "std:env"; function main(){match(get("A=B")){Ok(_)=>{throw "unexpected success";},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);}}}
```

Expected output: InvalidName. Ownership: borrows name without consuming it; successful strings own their storage.

std:env.name: args
std:env.documentation:
Reads the program arguments, excluding the executable name. Takes no arguments. Returns Ok with a new owned array of strings in their original order; no arguments returns an empty array. Empty strings, spaces, Unicode and option-like strings are preserved. This function does not parse flags or mutate process arguments. If any argument is not valid Unicode, returns Err with code NotUnicode, without lossy replacement or a partial array; the error does not expose the argument.

Use `tsrust run main.tsr -- first "two words"` to forward arguments. Unlike Node process.argv, this result contains neither a runtime path nor a script path.

```tsrust
import {args} from "std:env"; function main(){const values=unwrap(args());console.log(values.length);}
```

Expected output when launched without arguments: 0. Ownership: every call returns independent owned strings and an owned array; mutations do not affect later calls.

std:time.name: monotonicNow
std:time.documentation:
Measures elapsed time using a process-local monotonic clock. Takes no arguments and has no defaults or argument errors. Returns a nonnegative number of milliseconds, including fractional milliseconds, relative to an origin established by the first call. Subtract two readings from the same process to measure a duration; readings are not calendar timestamps and must not be compared across processes. Consecutive readings may be equal because clock resolution varies. System-clock adjustments do not change the origin. Whether suspended time counts is platform dependent, and floating-point precision decreases over long runtimes. No receiver is mutated.

```tsrust
import { monotonicNow } from "std:time";
function main() { const start = monotonicNow(); const elapsed = monotonicNow() - start; console.log(elapsed >= 0); } // prints true
```

Ownership: returns an independent number; no handle, borrowing or explicit cleanup is required.

examples.source:
import { monotonicNow } from "std:time";
function main() { const start = monotonicNow(); const elapsed = monotonicNow() - start; console.log(elapsed >= 0); }

std:json.name: borrowRaw
std:json.signature: borrowRaw(text: string, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>): Result<JsonRaw, JsonError>

parameters.label: text: string
parameters.documentation: Named source string containing one strict JSON value, with optional surrounding whitespace. Validation does not modify or copy the source.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>
parameters.documentation: Nonnegative input limits: maxBytes defaults to 16777216, maxDepth to 64, maxEntries and maxNodes to 1000000. Depth cannot exceed 64. Whitespace and duplicate fields count toward their budgets.

std:json.documentation:
Validates one strict JSON value and returns a source-backed JsonRaw fragment. Optional limits default to maxBytes 16777216, maxDepth 64, maxEntries 1000000 and maxNodes 1000000. All limits must be nonnegative; depth cannot exceed 64. Whitespace and duplicate fields count toward budgets. Rejects comments, trailing data, malformed escapes and invalid resource limits with JsonError codes and zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets. No dynamic value tree is built. Validation can allocate temporary escape scratch; the returned fragment retains no copied source buffer. JSON.stringify and JSON.tryStringify preserve raw source text exactly, including whitespace, key order, escapes and number spelling. Raw fragments count toward the enclosing 64-container depth limit and output byte limit. JSONL writing preserves single-line raw text; literal CR or LF returns record-newline before writing any bytes of that record. Escaped newline sequences remain valid.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: { "count": 7e0 }.

Ownership: the fragment borrows text. Its source must remain alive and cannot be replaced or moved while the fragment is used. The fragment cannot be cloned or constructed directly. Errors carry no source loan.

std:json.name: JsonRaw
std:json.documentation:
A validated fragment borrowing its original JSON source. Create it with borrowRaw or select it as a field type in JSON.parse<T>/JSON.tryParse<T>; direct construction and clone are rejected. It is distinct from an owned JsonValue or a child JsonView. JSON.stringify and JSON.tryStringify preserve raw source text exactly, including whitespace, key order, escapes and number spelling. Raw fragments count toward the enclosing 64-container depth limit and output byte limit. JSONL writing preserves single-line raw text; literal CR or LF returns record-newline before writing any bytes of that record. Escaped newline sequences remain valid.

Typed decoding: Explicit JsonRaw fields preserve the selected value's source tokens without constructing a dynamic subtree. std:json.name: JsonBuildLimits
std:json.documentation:
Construction budgets with required int fields maxDepth, maxEntries and maxNodes. Omitted limits default to maxDepth 64, maxEntries 1000000 and maxNodes 1000000. All limits must be nonnegative integers; maxDepth cannot exceed 64. The root counts as one value and one container level. maxEntries applies to every nested collection; maxNodes counts the root and all descendant values. Zero entries permits an empty container; zero depth or nodes rejects any container. Errors use depth-limit, entry-limit, node-limit or invalid-limits with offset zero. Existing inputs are already allocated; these limits bound the resulting tree, not an input byte stream. No receiver is mutated. Ownership: ordinary owned record, borrowed by constructors.


Expected output: [42].

std:json.name: StringView
std:json.documentation:
A read-only borrowed UTF-8 string returned by asString. Borrows the text of a JSON string without copying it. Accepts a JsonValue owner or JsonView; other JSON kinds return Err with code expected-string and offset zero. Returns Ok(StringView). The source is unchanged.

The view supports length, startsWith, endsWith, includes, indexOf and lastIndexOf. Length and search coordinates use UTF-8 bytes; explicit positions must be scalar boundaries. typeof returns string, Boolean(view) is false only for empty text, and console output displays the text. String(view) makes an independent owned string. Other string operations require that explicit conversion.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: string 5 true hello.

Ownership: the view may be stored or returned only while its source owner remains alive. The owner cannot be moved or replaced while the view is retained. clone(view) is rejected; use String(view) to copy. An error carries no source loan.

std:json.name: asString

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Named JSON owner or view containing string text. Non-string kinds return expected-string.

std:json.documentation:

The view supports length, startsWith, endsWith, includes, indexOf and lastIndexOf. ```tsrust

std:json.name: JsonView
std:json.documentation:
