
Expected output: string. Ownership: the view retains the original owner lifetime. The owner cannot be moved or replaced while the view is retained. Views may be reborrowed; missing and error branches carry no child loan.

std:json.name: JsonValue
std:json.documentation:
An owned strict JSON value: null, boolean, number, string, array or object. Obtain values with parse; inspect their category with kind and encode with stringify. No public fields or direct record construction. Null is a JSON value; undefined is not. Object keys are sorted lexicographically and duplicate keys keep the last value. Signed 64-bit and unsigned 64-bit integers remain exact; other numeric values use finite floating point, including negative zero. Larger integer tokens may round as floating point. Cycles and shared object identity cannot be represented.

```tsrust
import {parse,kind} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parse("null")){Ok(value)=>{console.log(kind(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: null. Ownership: independent owned storage; explicit clone recursively copies the value. No input borrow survives parsing.

std:json.name: JsonError
std:json.signature: type JsonError = { code: string; message: string; offset: int }
std:json.documentation:
Describes a JSON failure without including input values or keys. code distinguishes invalid-json, unexpected-end, trailing-data, invalid-limits, byte-limit, depth-limit, entry-limit, node-limit, output-limit and unterminated-comment. message is fixed explanatory text. offset counts UTF-8 bytes from zero; unexpected-end points to input length. Resource failures point to the parser checkpoint, which may precede the next value. Output failures report bytes written before the rejected output chunk. Invalid limits and scalar extraction failures use zero. Scalar readers also report expected-boolean, expected-number, expected-string, integer-fractional, integer-range and number-precision. Child inspection also reports expected-object, expected-array and index-range. No mutation occurs.

```tsrust
import {parse} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parse("null secret")){Ok(_)=>{throw "unexpected success";},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code,error.offset);}}}
```

Expected output: trailing-data 5. Ownership: ordinary owned record; explicit clone copies it.

std:json.name: JsonLimits
std:json.signature: type JsonLimits = { maxBytes: int; maxDepth: int; maxEntries: int; maxNodes: int }
std:json.documentation:
Sets parse budgets. All four fields are required nonnegative integers. maxBytes bounds UTF-8 input bytes, maxDepth bounds nested containers and cannot exceed 64, maxEntries bounds each array/object including duplicate object entries, and maxNodes bounds total JSON values including containers but excluding object keys. Zero is allowed. Scalars have depth zero. When limits are omitted, defaults are 16777216 bytes, 64 levels, 1000000 entries per collection and 1000000 values. Invalid settings return invalid-limits.

```tsrust
import {parse,JsonLimits} from "std:json"; function main(){const limits:JsonLimits={maxBytes:20,maxDepth:2,maxEntries:1,maxNodes:10};match(parse("[1,2]",limits)){Ok(_)=>{throw "unexpected success";},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);}}}
```

Expected output: entry-limit. Ownership: parse reads this record without consuming or mutating it.

std:json.name: parse
std:json.signature: parse(text: ReadOnly<string>, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>): Result<JsonValue, JsonError>

parameters.label: text: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required strict JSON document. UTF-8 byte length is bounded by maxBytes.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>
parameters.documentation: Optional complete limits record. Omission uses the documented defaults; negative limits or maxDepth above 64 return invalid-limits.

std:json.documentation:
Parses one strict JSON document and returns Ok with an independent JsonValue or Err with a structured JsonError. text is UTF-8; leading and trailing JSON whitespace is allowed. Trailing non-whitespace, malformed syntax, invalid escapes, lone surrogates and nonfinite numbers reject. Duplicate object keys keep the last value and count toward maxEntries. Keys are sorted, integers within signed/unsigned 64-bit ranges remain exact, integer tokens outside those ranges reject with integer-range, and negative zero survives. Optional limits default to 16777216 bytes, 64 container levels, 1000000 entries per collection and 1000000 values. Budget failures have distinct codes; offset counts bytes, not characters. Neither argument changes.

```tsrust
import {parse,kind} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parse("null")){Ok(value)=>{console.log(kind(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: null. Ownership: borrows both arguments; the result owns all parsed storage and can outlive the input.

Integer tokens without a decimal point or exponent are preserved exactly within signed 64-bit or unsigned 64-bit JSON storage. Tokens outside that storage range are rejected instead of rounded; integer-range reports storage overflow, while invalid or nonfinite JSON can fail earlier. Extracting int still requires the signed 64-bit range. Decimal and exponent forms use floating-point JSON semantics.

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required JSON value to inspect without mutation.

Returns the JSON category: null, boolean, number, string, array or object. The value argument is required; there are no optional arguments or validation errors. Does not inspect, convert or mutate child values. JSON null reports "null".


std:json.name: stringify
std:json.signature: stringify(value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>, maxBytes?: int): Result<string, JsonError>

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required JSON value. Its contents are not mutated or consumed.

parameters.label: maxBytes?: int
parameters.documentation: Optional output byte limit, default 16777216. Zero rejects every JSON value; negative values return invalid-limits.

std:json.documentation:
Encodes a JsonValue or JsonView as compact strict JSON with sorted object keys and no extra whitespace. Returns Ok with a UTF-8 string or Err(output-limit) before writing beyond maxBytes. The optional nonnegative integer byte limit defaults to 16777216; a negative value returns invalid-limits. Escapes quotes, backslashes and control characters; other Unicode remains UTF-8. Exact integer values are retained and floating negative zero is emitted with its sign. JsonValue cannot contain undefined, nonfinite numbers, cycles or shared object identity. The value is unchanged.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: {"a":2,"z":1}. Ownership: borrows value; the output string owns independent storage. Public data records such as ValidationError, literal types and declared enums encode through their data fields or scalar values. Opaque resources and schema plans are not JSON data.

std:json.name: parseJsonc
std:json.signature: parseJsonc(text: ReadOnly<string>, allowTrailingComma?: boolean, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>): Result<JsonValue, JsonError>
std:json.typedSignature: parseJsonc<T>(text: ReadOnly<string>, allowTrailingComma?: boolean, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>): Result<T, JsonError>

parameters.label: text: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required UTF-8 JSONC document. Original input bytes, including comments, count against maxBytes.

parameters.label: allowTrailingComma?: boolean
parameters.documentation: Optional, default false. Set true to accept one comma after the final array element or object property.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>
parameters.documentation: Optional complete parse budgets, with the same defaults and ranges as parse.

std:json.documentation:
Parses JSON with // line comments and /* block comments */ wherever JSON permits whitespace. Comment delimiters inside strings remain literal. Line comments end at LF or CR; block comments end at the first */ and do not nest. Returns Ok with an owned JsonValue or Err with a JsonError. Unterminated block comments return unterminated-comment at the opening slash. All offsets address original UTF-8 input bytes. Trailing commas reject unless allowTrailingComma is true; empty collections with a comma and repeated commas always reject. Limits default to 16777216 input bytes, 64 container levels, 1000000 entries per collection and 1000000 values. Comment bytes count toward the input limit. Number, Unicode and duplicate-key rules match parse. Comments are discarded; stringify emits strict JSON. Neither argument changes.

```tsrust
import {parseJsonc,kind} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parseJsonc("/* note */ [1,]",true)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(kind(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: array. Ownership: borrows text and limits; allocates bounded scratch storage and an independent owned result.

With an explicit type argument, parseJsonc<T> returns Result<T, JsonError> and constructs the owned target directly. Supports scalars, named records, tuples, arrays and nullable records. Required fields must be present; missing optional fields become undefined; unknown fields are skipped but still count against limits. Every duplicate known field must match its type; the last valid occurrence wins. Shape mismatches report shape-mismatch. int conversion is checked; number rejects lossy integer conversion with number-precision. Unsupported targets fail during checking.

```tsrust
import {parseJsonc} from "std:json";type Item={name:string;};function main(){match(parseJsonc<Item>('/*note*/{"name":"hello"}')){Ok(item)=>{console.log(item.name);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: hello. Ownership: typed output owns its fields independently of the input and normalization buffer.

Integer tokens without a decimal point or exponent are preserved exactly within signed 64-bit or unsigned 64-bit JSON storage. Tokens outside that storage range are rejected instead of rounded; integer-range reports storage overflow, while invalid or nonfinite JSON can fail earlier. Typed decoding also accepts scalar singleton literal types and closed unions of literals from one scalar kind, with optional/null members. Each present value must match an exact declared literal; unknown alternatives produce shape-mismatch. For example, JSON.parse<'draft'|'published'>('"draft"') returns draft, while "other" rejects. Numeric literals retain the ordinary checked int/number precision rules; nullable and missing optional fields keep their existing behavior. Unions of unrelated shapes or mixed literal kinds remain unsupported. Decoding transfers successful owned string storage once.

std:json.name: JsonlReader
std:json.documentation:
A uniquely owned, bounded JSON Lines file reader. Open with openJsonl, pull one value with readJsonl and consume with closeJsonl. JSON null is distinct from EOF (undefined). std:json.name: JsonlError
std:json.signature: type JsonlError = { code: string; message: string; operation: string; line: int; offset: int; osCode?: int }
std:json.documentation:
A structured JSON Lines failure. code distinguishes JSON syntax/limit failures, capacity-range and file errors. message never includes record contents or paths. operation is open, read or close. Read line counts records from one and offset is the absolute zero-based UTF-8 byte offset. Open uses line 1 and offset 0; close uses 0 for both because it has no input location. osCode is present only when supplied by the operating system. A read failure is terminal and repeats without further I/O.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: capacity-range open.

Ownership: an independent owned record; explicit clone copies it. Raw fragments preserve their exact text. A literal CR or LF in encoded raw text returns record-newline before any bytes of that record are written and makes the writer terminal. Escaped newline sequences inside JSON strings remain valid; ordinary strings are escaped normally.

code.documentation: Stable failure category, including JSON syntax/limit errors, capacity-range and file errors. Does not contain input.

message.documentation: Fixed explanatory message. Never includes record contents or file paths.

operation.documentation: Operation that failed: open, read or close.

line.documentation: One-based JSON Lines record for read errors. Open errors use 1; close errors use 0 because no input location applies.

offset.documentation: Absolute zero-based UTF-8 input byte offset for read errors. Open and close errors use 0.

osCode.documentation: Optional native operating-system error code. Undefined when the failure has no OS code.

std:json.signature: openJsonl(path: ReadOnly<string>, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>, capacity?: int): Result<JsonlReader, JsonlError>

parameters.label: path: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required local file path, borrowed unchanged. Opened read-only; no whole-file load.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>
parameters.documentation: Per-record limits; defaults: maxBytes 16777216, maxDepth 64, maxEntries/maxNodes 1000000. Nonnegative; depth at most 64. LF is excluded; CR and other whitespace count.

parameters.label: capacity?: int

std:json.documentation:

Optional limits default to maxBytes 16777216, maxDepth 64, maxEntries/maxNodes 1000000 per record; values must be nonnegative and depth at most 64. parameters.label: reader: JsonlReader
parameters.documentation: Required owned reader, consumed even if close fails. Cannot be reused afterward. Also accepts JsonlReaderView, releasing its borrow without closing its owner.

std:json.documentation:

std:json.name: JsonlWriter
std:json.documentation:
An opaque owned JSON Lines output resource created by createJsonl. No public constructor or fields. Writes compact records through a bounded staging buffer and a buffered file. flushJsonl reports buffered output failures; closeJsonlWriter consumes the writer and reports cleanup errors. Scope exit closes remaining output but cannot report errors. Ownership: unique, nonclonable and nonconstructible; never shared implicitly.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: hello. The file contains {"name":"hello"} followed by LF.

std:json.name: createJsonl
std:json.signature: createJsonl(path: ReadOnly<string>, maxBytes?: int, capacity?: int): Result<JsonlWriter, JsonlError>

parameters.label: path: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Output path. Creates a file or truncates an existing file after validating options.

parameters.label: maxBytes?: int
parameters.documentation: Maximum encoded bytes per record, excluding LF; nonnegative, default 16777216. Zero permits creation but rejects every record.

parameters.label: capacity?: int
parameters.documentation: Output buffer capacity in bytes, from 1 through 1048576; default 8192. Supply maxBytes when specifying capacity.

std:json.documentation:
Creates or truncates a file for bounded synchronous JSON Lines output. Returns an owned writer or a structured error. Invalid maxBytes reports invalid-limits; invalid capacity reports capacity-range before opening or truncating the path. File errors preserve their stable code and optional OS code. Creation errors use operation create, line 1 and offset 0. Record limits exclude the trailing LF. No record is written by creation. Ownership: borrows path unchanged; returned writer owns its file and buffer.

std:json.name: writeJsonl
std:json.signature: writeJsonl<T>(writer: Mutable<JsonlWriter>, value: T): Result<void, JsonlError>

parameters.label: writer: Mutable<JsonlWriter>
parameters.documentation: Required writer, advanced on successful record output. Also accepts JsonlWriterView; the underlying owner remains open after adapter close.

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Required encodable scalar, record, tuple, array, JsonValue, JsonView or StringView; borrowed unchanged.

std:json.documentation:
Encodes one compact strict JSON record followed by LF. Returns Ok or a structured encoding/output error. Uses JSON.stringify typed rules: sorted keys, exact integers, omitted undefined object fields, undefined-value for root/array undefined, number-nonfinite for nonfinite numbers and depth-limit beyond 64 containers. Stages the entire record within the creation byte limit; output-limit or another encoding rejection writes none of that record. An I/O failure may leave a prefix and has no rollback guarantee. Any error makes subsequent writes/flushes repeat that terminal error without more output. Errors use operation write, the current one-based record and offset 0, which is not an output position. Ownership: mutably borrows writer and borrows value without mutation or implicit cloning.

parameters.documentation: Required writer; flushes buffered bytes without closing it. Also accepts JsonlWriterView; the underlying owner remains open after adapter close.

std:json.name: JsonlReaderView
std:json.documentation:
Borrows an existing BufferedReader for bounded JSON Lines reading from its current position. Does not reopen, seek or consume a record during construction. Uses the existing read-ahead buffer; no second file buffer is allocated. Optional limits default to maxBytes 16777216, maxDepth 64 and maxEntries/maxNodes 1000000 per record. Limits must be nonnegative and depth at most 64; invalid limits return invalid-limits without reading. LF is excluded from maxBytes; CR and other whitespace count. ```

Unions of unrelated shapes or mixed literal kinds remain unsupported. Decoding transfers successful owned string storage once.

import {open,bufferReader,close,writeFile} from "std:fs";import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";import {borrowJsonl,readJsonl,closeJsonl} from "std:json";
function main(){match(fromUtf8("7\n")){Ok(bytes)=>{writeFile("borrowed-jsonl-example.jsonl",bytes);},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(open("borrowed-jsonl-example.jsonl")){Ok(file)=>{match(bufferReader(file,8)){Ok(input)=>{{match(borrowJsonl(input)){Ok(reader)=>{match(readJsonl<int>(reader)){Ok(value)=>{if(value!==undefined){console.log(value);}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}closeJsonl(reader);},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}close(input);},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}

std:json.name: JsonlWriterView
std:json.documentation:
Borrows an existing BufferedWriter for bounded JSON Lines output at its current position. Does not create, reopen, truncate or seek a file. Uses the existing output buffer. Optional maxBytes defaults to 16777216 and must be nonnegative and fit the platform; it limits each encoded record excluding the final LF. Zero rejects every JSON value. Invalid limits return invalid-limits before writing or flushing. Returns a JsonlWriterView or JsonlError. Existing writeJsonl, flushJsonl and closeJsonlWriter accept the adapter. Typed writes borrow their input and stage a complete bounded record before writing; encoding errors emit no part of that record. I/O errors may leave a prefix. Errors make the adapter terminal. Error line starts at 1 for this adapter; offset is always zero, not a byte position. Closing or dropping the adapter flushes buffered output but leaves the owner open. Explicit close reports a flush error; otherwise it repeats any prior terminal error. Drop cannot report errors. No durability sync is performed.

```tsrust
import {create,bufferWriter,close} from "std:fs";import {borrowJsonlWriter,writeJsonl,closeJsonlWriter} from "std:json";
function main(){match(create("borrowed-jsonl-output.jsonl")){Ok(file)=>{match(bufferWriter(file,64)){Ok(output)=>{{match(borrowJsonlWriter(output,16)){Ok(writer)=>{match(writeJsonl(writer,7)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(closeJsonlWriter(writer)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}match(close(output)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Expected file contents: 7 followed by LF. No console output.

Ownership: exclusively borrows the buffered writer. The owner cannot be written, flushed, moved or closed while the adapter is live. The view cannot escape its owner, be cloned or be constructed directly. Close the owner explicitly after releasing the adapter.

std:schema.name: ValidationContext
std:schema.documentation:
Context supplied to a superRefine callback for reporting multiple validation issues. T is the validated input shape; addIssue paths are checked against it. The callback receives temporary mutable access. It cannot construct, clone, retain or transfer this context. Context lifetime ends when the callback returns.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.int().superRefine((value,ctx)=>{if(value<1){ctx.addIssue({message:'Must be positive'});}});const result=schema.safeParse(0);if(result.success){const value=result.data;throw 'Expected rejection';}else{const error=result.error;console.log(error.issues[0].message);}}
```

Expected output:
```text
Must be positive
```

Schema

std:schema.name: SchemaExportError
std:schema.documentation:
Thrown when a schema rule cannot be represented by JSON Schema export. Fields: code is unrepresentable; path is a JSON Pointer into the schema rule (empty for the root); reason explains the unsupported rule. Pointer segments escape ~ as ~0 and / as ~1. Export does not execute callbacks or default factories and never returns a partial document. Ownership: the error owns its path; catching it does not consume the source schema.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.string().refine(value=>value.length>0);try{schema.toJsonSchema();}catch(error){console.log(error.code);}}
```

Expected output:
```text
unrepresentable
```

std:schema.name: SchemaConstructionError
std:schema.signature: type SchemaConstructionError = { code: string; operation: string; limit: int | number }
std:schema.documentation:
Thrown when constructing invalid schema bounds. code is negative-length for string limits, nonfinite-limit for floating limits, or contradictory-bounds; operation identifies min, max, gt or lt; limit retains the supplied int or number without converting exact integers to floating point. Narrow the limit before arithmetic. This error concerns schema construction, not input validation through safeParse. Contains no input data.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){try{s.string().min(-1);}catch(error){console.log(error.code);}}
```

Expected output:
```text
negative-length
```

schemaBuilder.name: recursive

parameters.label: builder: (self: Schema<T>) => Schema<T>
parameters.documentation: Inline one-parameter builder evaluated once. Reuse self within its returned schema to refer to the completed definition. Output is inferred; an optional explicit type argument checks it against a named type.

schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs a reusable recursive schema. The builder runs once during construction, not once per validation or recursive node. Output is inferred from its returned schema; recursive input and output may differ when transforms change values. An optional explicit type argument checks the output against an existing named type.

Use self within arrays, object fields, record values or union branches. Map keys and Set elements still require scalar or enum types. Every definition needs a finite terminating value. Direct self, unguarded recursion and escaping or capturing self are rejected. Nullable recursive record links allocate uniquely owned storage; arrays supply their own indirection. Validation retains ordinary issue paths and validation limits. Callback exceptions propagate.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';const tree=s.recursive(self=>s.object({value:s.int(),children:s.array(self)}));function main(){const result=tree.safeParseJson('{"value":1,"children":[{"value":2,"children":[]}]}');if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value.children[0].value);}else{const error=result.error;throw 'unexpected';}}
```

Expected output: 2.

Ownership: the returned plan uniquely owns its child schemas. Validation borrows the reusable plan and consumes owned input. Recursion does not clone values or introduce shared ownership.

schemaBuilder.name: record
schemaBuilder.signature: record<Element>(element: Owned<Schema<Element>>, options?: { message?: string }): Schema<Map<string, Element>>

parameters.label: element: Owned<Schema<Element>>
parameters.documentation: Schema for each value or Set element. Child input and output types remain distinct through transforms.

parameters.label: options?: { message?: string }
parameters.documentation: Optional fallback validation message. The string is owned by the reusable plan and copied only into retained failures. A child custom message takes precedence. Unknown option fields and non-string messages are rejected.

schemaBuilder.documentation:
Validates every value of a JSON object against one child schema, returning an owned Map with arbitrary string keys. safeParse accepts matching owned Maps or JsonValue when the child accepts JSON; safeParseJson decodes directly from text. Keys are preserved and failures identify their property names. Empty objects produce empty Maps. Duplicate JSON keys use the last value before validation, after checking the entire document. Child callback exceptions propagate. Consuming transforms commit the enclosing union branch; later failure does not retry another branch. Construction consumes the child schemas. Validation borrows the reusable parent and consumes existing owned input on success or failure; clone explicitly to retain input.


An optional final { message: '...' } supplies fallback text for validation issues from this plan. Omission preserves the default issue message; child custom messages take precedence. This does not change validation rules or construction errors.

This constructor does not assign a JSON wire representation; use an explicit conversion when decoding JSON. Child callback exceptions propagate. schemaBuilder.name: literal
schemaBuilder.signature: literal(value: Owned<Literal>, options?: { message?: string }): Schema<Literal>

parameters.label: value: Owned<Literal>
parameters.documentation: One statically known string, integer, finite number, boolean or null value. The output keeps its literal type.

parameters.label: options?: { message?: string }
parameters.documentation: Optional fallback validation message. The string is owned by the reusable plan and copied only into retained failures. A child custom message takes precedence. Unknown option fields and non-string messages are rejected.

schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs a reusable schema for exactly one statically known string, integer, finite number, boolean or null value. Accepts a literal expression or a value already carrying a literal type; arbitrary broad scalar values cannot determine a singleton output type. Successful validation preserves that exact type. Different values report literal-mismatch; JSON with a different kind reports type-mismatch. Integer literals retain the full signed 64-bit range. Number validation rejects nonfinite values and checked integer conversion rejects precision loss. Positive and negative zero compare equal. Use s.null() for an equivalent null schema.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.literal('ready');const result=schema.safeParse('waiting');if(result.success){const value=result.data;console.log(value);}else{const error=result.error;console.log(error.issues[0].code);}}
```

schemaBuilder.name: enum
schemaBuilder.signature: enum(values: Owned<EnumValues> | EnumDeclaration, options?: { message?: string }): Schema<EnumValue>

parameters.label: values: Owned<EnumValues> | EnumDeclaration
parameters.documentation: A nonempty array literal of distinct known strings, or a nonempty declared enum with string or finite numeric values. A list infers its literal union; a declaration preserves its nominal enum type.

parameters.label: options?: { message?: string }
parameters.documentation: Optional fallback validation message. The string is owned by the reusable plan and copied only into retained failures. A child custom message takes precedence. Unknown option fields and non-string messages are rejected.

schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs a reusable schema accepting one of a fixed set of enum values. Pass a declared enum, or one nonempty array literal of distinct string literals or values already carrying string literal types. Empty lists, duplicate alternatives, non-string values and broad runtime arrays are rejected by the checker. Output is the exact union of the alternatives; a singleton list keeps its single literal type. String-list validation accepts owned strings or JsonValue. A declared enum returns its nominal enum type and accepts its own members, matching underlying strings or numbers, or JsonValue. Numeric enum schemas also accept exact integer conversion; number-precision rejects loss and number-nonfinite rejects nonfinite input. Empty declarations and declarations with nonfinite values are rejected. Equal-valued aliases select the first declared member and retain ordinary enum equality. A different string reports literal-mismatch; another JSON kind reports type-mismatch. Optional, nullable, defaults, object and array composition preserve the alternatives.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: literal-mismatch.

Ownership: evaluates list elements once in source order and consumes owned alternatives into an immutable plan. Validation borrows the plan and consumes input on every outcome; string-list output moves successful string storage without cloning. Declared enum output is a Copy value; raw string input is consumed and released.

An optional final { message: '...' } supplies fallback text for validation issues from this plan. Omission preserves the default issue message; child custom messages take precedence. This does not change validation rules or construction errors.

schemaBuilder.name: union

parameters.label: branches: Owned<Schema<Alternatives>[]>
parameters.documentation: Nonempty array literal of schemas. Branch order is significant; repeated output types and overlapping constraints are allowed.

parameters.label: options?: { message?: string }
parameters.documentation: Optional fallback validation message. The string is owned by the reusable plan and copied only into retained failures. A child custom message takes precedence. Unknown option fields and non-string messages are rejected.

schemaBuilder.documentation:
Accepts the first matching branch in declaration order. The output is the union of branch output types. Branch preparation borrows input; a rejected branch leaves its storage available to the next branch. Missing-field defaults are evaluated once per attempted branch and cached for the selected branch. Factory exceptions propagate without trying another branch. If every branch fails, safeParse returns bounded validation issues in branch order. Successful alternatives discard speculative errors from earlier branches. Optional, nullable, array and object composition preserve branch plans.

Ownership: consumes branch schemas into one uniquely owned reusable plan. Validation consumes input on every outcome and moves selected output storage without implicit cloning.

parameters.documentation: Literal name of a required discriminator field declared by every object branch.

parameters.label: branches: Owned<Schema<Alternatives>[]>
parameters.documentation: Nonempty array literal of object schemas. Discriminators must have nonoverlapping literal or closed enum values.

SchemaArray.name: safeParse

parameters.label: input: Owned<Input>
parameters.documentation: A matching owned array or dynamic JSON value. Both transfer on success and failure. JSON arrays are checked recursively without coercing strings, booleans or null. Number schemas also accept int arrays with matching nesting; every integer must convert exactly.

Channel.name: sender
Channel.documentation:
Creates an independently owned sender for this channel. Takes no arguments. Each sender can move into a worker. The last sender closing or leaving scope closes admission; buffered values remain readable. Calling after closure returns a closed sender. Does not copy queued messages.

Ownership: borrows the receiving owner and returns a transferable sender.

```tsrust
import {Channel} from 'std:threads';function main(){const inbox=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=inbox.sender();match(inbox.tryReceive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}unwrap(sender.send(7));match(sender.trySend(9)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);console.log(error.value);}}inbox.close();console.log(unwrap(inbox.receive()));match(inbox.receive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}sender.close();}
```
Expected output: empty, full, 9, 7, closed on separate lines.

Channel.name: receive
Channel.documentation:
Waits for and removes the oldest queued value. Takes no arguments. Returns closed after the buffer drains and admission closes, or when no senders exist; cancelled when the current worker is cancelled. Cancellation wakes the wait and does not remove a queued value. May wait indefinitely if a sender remains open without sending.

Ownership: borrows the receiving endpoint; success transfers one owned payload.

```tsrust
import {Channel} from 'std:threads';function main(){const inbox=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=inbox.sender();match(inbox.tryReceive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}unwrap(sender.send(7));match(sender.trySend(9)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);console.log(error.value);}}inbox.close();console.log(unwrap(inbox.receive()));match(inbox.receive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}sender.close();}
```
Expected output: empty, full, 9, 7, closed on separate lines.

Channel.name: tryReceive
Channel.documentation:
Removes the oldest queued value without waiting. Takes no arguments. Returns empty if the buffer is empty with open senders, closed if no future values can arrive, or cancelled for the current worker. Closure still permits draining queued values.

Ownership: borrows the receiver and transfers one owned payload on success.

```tsrust
import {Channel} from 'std:threads';function main(){const inbox=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=inbox.sender();match(inbox.tryReceive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}unwrap(sender.send(7));match(sender.trySend(9)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);console.log(error.value);}}inbox.close();console.log(unwrap(inbox.receive()));match(inbox.receive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}sender.close();}
```
Expected output: empty, full, 9, 7, closed on separate lines.

Channel.name: close
Channel.documentation:
Stops all new sends and wakes blocked senders and receivers. Takes no arguments. Existing queued values remain readable; receiving then reports closed. Repeated close is harmless. Dropping the receiving owner also closes admission and disposes unread values.

Ownership: borrows the receiver; no message copies.

```tsrust
import {Channel} from 'std:threads';function main(){const inbox=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=inbox.sender();match(inbox.tryReceive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}unwrap(sender.send(7));match(sender.trySend(9)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);console.log(error.value);}}inbox.close();console.log(unwrap(inbox.receive()));match(inbox.receive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}sender.close();}
```
Expected output: empty, full, 9, 7, closed on separate lines.

Sender.name: send

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Owned transferable message without channel endpoints; no default. Failure returns this same owned value.

Sender.documentation:
Waits for buffer capacity, then transfers value into the channel. Returns closed if this sender or the receiver is closed, cancelled if the current worker is cancelled. Cancellation wakes a blocked send. Every failure returns the original unsent value in error.value. Successful sends preserve queue order for this sender; concurrent senders may interleave.

Ownership: borrows the sender and consumes value; no cloning or serialization.

```tsrust

```
Expected output: empty, full, 9, 7, closed on separate lines.

Sender.name: trySend

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Owned transferable message without channel endpoints; no default. Failure returns this same owned value.

Sender.documentation:
Transfers value into the channel only if capacity is immediately available; never waits. Returns closed if this sender or the receiver is closed, cancelled if the current worker is cancelled, or full if capacity is exhausted. Every failure returns the original unsent value in error.value. Successful sends preserve queue order for this sender; concurrent senders may interleave.

Ownership: borrows the sender and consumes value; no cloning or serialization.

```tsrust
import {Channel} from 'std:threads';function main(){const inbox=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=inbox.sender();match(inbox.tryReceive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}unwrap(sender.send(7));match(sender.trySend(9)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);console.log(error.value);}}inbox.close();console.log(unwrap(inbox.receive()));match(inbox.receive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}sender.close();}
```
Expected output: empty, full, 9, 7, closed on separate lines.

Sender.name: close
Sender.documentation:
Closes this sender and wakes channel waits. Takes no arguments. Other senders remain usable. Closing the last sender closes admission; buffered values remain readable. Repeated calls are harmless. Scope exit closes this sender automatically.

Ownership: mutably borrows this sender; does not consume messages.

```tsrust
import {Channel} from 'std:threads';function main(){const inbox=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=inbox.sender();match(inbox.tryReceive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}unwrap(sender.send(7));match(sender.trySend(9)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);console.log(error.value);}}inbox.close();console.log(unwrap(inbox.receive()));match(inbox.receive()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}sender.close();}
```
Expected output: empty, full, 9, 7, closed on separate lines.

TaskContext.name: cancellationRequested
TaskContext.documentation:
Returns whether cancellation was requested for this particular worker. Takes no arguments and does not change state. A request is cooperative; returning or throwing finishes the callback. Blocking channel operations observe this same cancellation state automatically.

Ownership: borrows the context. Contexts cannot transfer to another worker.

```tsrust
import {spawn} from 'std:threads';function main(){const worker=unwrap(spawn((task):boolean=>task.cancellationRequested()));console.log(unwrap(worker.join()));}
```
Expected output: false.

Thread.name: join
Thread.documentation:
Waits for this worker and returns its value or typed error. Takes no arguments. Error codes are worker, panic and cancelled. Cancellation does not imply completion until join returns.

Ownership: consumes this handle exactly once.

```tsrust
import {spawn} from 'std:threads';function main(){const worker=unwrap(spawn((task):boolean=>task.cancellationRequested()));console.log(unwrap(worker.join()));}
```
Expected output: false.

Thread.name: cancel
Thread.documentation:
Requests cancellation of this worker only. Takes no arguments. Returns true for the first request before completion, false for repeated requests or published completion. Wakes supported channel waits; cannot forcibly interrupt arbitrary native code.

Ownership: borrows the handle; join or scope cleanup still waits.

```tsrust
import {spawn} from 'std:threads';function main(){const worker=unwrap(spawn((task):void=>{while(!task.cancellationRequested()) {}}));worker.cancel();match(worker.join()){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>console.log(error.code)}}
```
Expected output: cancelled.

Thread.name: detach
Thread.documentation:
Relinquishes automatic joining. Takes no arguments. Dedicated workers may outlive their caller; process exit need not wait. Pool shutdown still drains detached pool tasks.

Ownership: consumes the handle and discards eventual completion.

```tsrust
import {ThreadPool} from 'std:threads';function main(){const pool=new ThreadPool({workers:1,capacity:1});const worker=unwrap(pool.task(():void=>{}));worker.detach();unwrap(pool.shutdown());console.log('done');}
```
Expected output: done.

std:http.name: Router
std:http.signature: new Router<State = null, Variables = null>(state?: State): Router<State, Variables>

parameters.label: state?: State
parameters.documentation: Owned application state. Required when State is not null; omitted for a router without shared state. Immutable data and supported concurrent pools, clients, caches and senders are accepted.

std:http.inferredSignature: function new Router<State = null, Variables = null>(state?: State): Router<State, Variables>

std:http.name: Context
std:http.documentation:
A request-local context supplied by Router. req exposes the incoming request. header changes outgoing headers before or after downstream middleware; text, html and json construct responses. Context has no public constructor or clone operation.

```tsrust
function hello(c: Mutable<Context>): Response { return c.text('Hello'); }
```

Returns a UTF-8 response with status 200. Ownership: handlers exclusively borrow Context for the invocation; it cannot be retained in detached work.

State and Variables match the supplying Router. env exposes shared application state. set/get store checked request-local values, initially absent for each new request.

req.documentation: Incoming request for this context. Read headers and route parameters through c.req. The request remains owned by the context; it cannot be moved out of a mutable context loan.

env.documentation:
Read-only application state owned by Router. The same state serves all requests. Borrow fields for supported concurrent operations, or explicitly clone independently cloneable data. Moving or mutating state is rejected.

```tsrust
const greeting = clone(c.env.greeting);
```

Returns independent text when State declares greeting: string. The shared state itself stays owned by Router.

std:http.name: ContextNext
App
std:http.documentation:
Creates an empty Axum-backed router. No arguments. Register routes and middleware before listen consumes the app. Default missing-route and wrong-method responses are 404 and 405. No listener starts at construction.

```tsrust
const app = new App();
```

Ownership: unique, nonclonable router.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();console.log('ok');}

std:http.name: Client

parameters.label: options?: ClientOptions
parameters.documentation: Omit for default public CA roots. Supply { ca: pem } to trust only that nonempty PEM certificate bundle. Hostname, chain and validity checks remain enabled.

std:http.documentation:
Creates a reusable HTTP/HTTPS client with connection pooling and a 30-second request/body deadline. With no options, trusts default public CA roots. Optional { ca: string } supplies a nonempty PEM CA bundle that replaces those roots for this client only. Certificate chain, validity and URL hostname checks remain enabled. Invalid PEM throws HttpError code tls; construction failure throws code client. Redirects, proxies, automatic decompression and cookies are disabled.

```tsrust
const client = new Client(); // public HTTPS
const privateClient = new Client({ ca: caPem }); // private CA only
```

Ownership: borrows options during construction; retains independent trust settings. send borrows the client until its task completes or is disposed.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const client=new Client();console.log('ok');}

std:http.documentation:
Creates an unsent request. Invalid method or URI throws HttpError code method or url. Does not infer Content-Type, send data or mutate a receiver. Client.send validates the scheme and credentials.


parameters.label: body: Body
parameters.documentation: Owned streaming body; retains its remaining byte limit.

parameters.label: status: int = 200
parameters.documentation: HTTP status 200..599; defaults to 200.

std:http.documentation:
Creates a streaming response without collecting its body. Transport applies backpressure; disconnect disposes pending body work. Exceeding the cumulative body limit fails the stream rather than silently truncating it. Invalid status throws HttpError code status.

```tsrust
const response = stream(input.body());
```

std:http.name: Request
std:http.documentation:
An owned HTTP request. method(), url(), param(name) and header(name) inspect metadata. setHeader changes metadata. text() and body() consume the request; a body can be read once. Body reads enforce a cumulative 1048576-byte limit. Each handler receives a distinct request.

Ownership: unique, nonclonable capability; consuming operations transfer ownership.

```tsrust
import {Request} from 'std:http';function inspect(value:Request):void{}function main(){console.log('ok');}
```
Expected output: ok.

std:http.name: Response
std:http.documentation:
An owned HTTP response. status() and header(name) inspect metadata; setHeader changes metadata before transmission. text() or body() consumes the response. Client responses retain HTTP error statuses as data. Dropping the body releases its transport resources.

Ownership: unique, nonclonable capability; consuming operations transfer ownership.

```tsrust
import {Response} from 'std:http';function inspect(value:Response):void{}function main(){console.log('ok');}
```
Expected output: ok.

std:http.name: Body
std:http.documentation:
A single-owner HTTP byte stream. Await next() for Bytes or undefined at end; await text() to consume strict UTF-8. Reads apply backpressure and enforce a cumulative 1048576-byte limit. Dropping an unread body releases its resources.

Ownership: unique, nonclonable capability; consuming operations transfer ownership.

```tsrust
import {Body} from 'std:http';function inspect(value:Body):void{}function main(){console.log('ok');}
```
Expected output: ok.

std:http.name: Server
std:http.documentation:
An owned running HTTP listener. address() returns its IP and port. Await shutdown() to stop accepting and drain requests, with five seconds before cancelling remaining I/O. Dropping the handle requests cleanup; its async owner drains completion.

Ownership: unique, nonclonable capability; consuming operations transfer ownership.

```tsrust
import {Server} from 'std:http';function inspect(value:Server):void{}function main(){console.log('ok');}
```
Expected output: ok.

std:http.name: Next
std:http.documentation:
An owned middleware continuation. Await run(request) to invoke the remaining middleware and handler once. It consumes both the continuation and request. Returning without running it short-circuits the chain.

Ownership: unique, nonclonable capability; consuming operations transfer ownership.


std:http.name: HttpError
std:http.signature: type HttpError = { code: string; message: string; }
std:http.documentation:
A checked HTTP failure with code and message strings. Codes describe invalid method, route, address, status, header, URL, body, encoding, limit, listener, client, request or timeout. Catch at the failing operation; an uncaught handler failure becomes a generic 500 without exposing this message.

Ownership: ordinary owned error data.


std:http.name: TlsOptions
std:http.signature: type TlsOptions = { cert: string; key: string }
std:http.documentation:
HTTPS listener credentials. Both PEM strings are required: cert is the certificate chain, leaf first; key is its matching unencrypted private key. Invalid or mismatched credentials throw HttpError code tls when listen is awaited. No client certificate authentication. The listener keeps independent settings after startup.

Ownership: owned record; listen consumes it when creating the task.

```tsrust
import {TlsOptions} from 'std:http';function main(){const options:TlsOptions={cert:"PEM",key:"PEM"};console.log(options.cert);}
```
Expected output: PEM.

cert.documentation: PEM certificate chain, leaf first. Required with key; app.listen validates it before binding. Example: { cert: certificatePem, key: privateKeyPem }. Ownership: moved into the listener task; reading does not mutate it.

key.documentation: Matching unencrypted PEM private key. Required with cert; invalid or mismatched keys throw HttpError code tls. Example: { cert: certificatePem, key: privateKeyPem }. Ownership: moved into the listener task; reading does not mutate it.

std:http.name: ClientOptions
std:http.documentation:
Private trust settings for new Client(options). ca is a required, nonempty PEM CA bundle. It replaces default public roots for this client only; chain, hostname and validity checks remain enabled. Omit constructor options to use default public roots. Invalid PEM throws HttpError code tls.

Ownership: reusable owned record; construction borrows its strings.

```tsrust
import {ClientOptions} from 'std:http';function main(){const options:ClientOptions={ca:"PEM"};console.log(options.ca);}
```
Expected output: PEM.

ca.documentation: Nonempty PEM CA bundle used instead of default public roots. Invalid PEM throws HttpError code tls. Example: new Client({ ca: caPem }) trusts only caPem. Ownership: borrowed during construction; reading does not mutate it.

std:http.name: getCookie
std:http.signature: getCookie(c: ReadOnly<Context<State, Variables>>, name: string): string | undefined

parameters.label: c: ReadOnly<Context<State, Variables>>
parameters.documentation: Context containing incoming Cookie headers.

parameters.label: name: string
parameters.documentation: Cookie name using HTTP token characters.

std:http.documentation:
Reads the first valid cookie with this name, or undefined. Decodes UTF-8 percent escapes; plus stays plus. Malformed escapes remain literal. Invalid cookie entries are skipped. Duplicate names use the first valid value; applications requiring stricter policy must validate the raw Cookie header.

```tsrust
const theme = getCookie(c, "theme");
```

Cookie theme=dark returns dark. Does not mutate Context. Ownership: borrows Context and returns independent owned text.

std:http.name: setCookie
std:http.signature: setCookie(c: Mutable<Context<State, Variables>>, name: string, value: string, options?: CookieOptions): void
std:http.inferredSignature: function setCookie(c: Mutable<Context<State, Variables>>, name: string, value: string, options?: CookieOptions): void

parameters.label: c: Mutable<Context<State, Variables>>
parameters.documentation: Request context receiving outgoing cookies.

parameters.label: name: string
parameters.documentation: Cookie name using HTTP token characters.

parameters.label: value: string
parameters.documentation: Value encoded as UTF-8 percent escapes.

parameters.label: options?: CookieOptions
parameters.documentation: Path defaults to /. Other attributes are omitted unless supplied.

std:http.documentation:
Appends a separate Set-Cookie response header before or after next(). Path defaults to /; maxAge is integer seconds from 0 through 34560000. Invalid names, paths, domains, ages or sameSite throw HttpError code cookie. __Secure- requires secure; __Host- also requires Path=/ without domain. Partitioned requires secure.

```tsrust
setCookie(c, "theme", "dark", {httpOnly: true, sameSite: "Lax"});
```

Adds theme=dark; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax. Signing, Expires and Priority are unsupported. Ownership: exclusively borrows Context; copies supplied text into response headers.

std:http.name: deleteCookie
std:http.signature: deleteCookie(c: Mutable<Context<State, Variables>>, name: string, options?: CookieOptions): void

Adds theme=; Path=/; Max-Age=0. Ownership: exclusively borrows Context.

std:http.documentation:
Cookie response attributes. path defaults to /; domain is omitted. maxAge is 0..34560000 integer seconds. secure, httpOnly and partitioned default false. sameSite accepts Strict, Lax or None, including lowercase. SameSite=None requires secure for browser acceptance. Expires, Priority and signed cookies are unsupported.

```tsrust
const options: CookieOptions = {secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: "Strict"};
```

Ownership: an ordinary owned record; helper calls borrow it.

path.documentation:
Absolute ASCII cookie path, default /. Semicolons and control characters reject.

Example: `{ path: '/account' }`. Helpers borrow options; values are copied into the outgoing header.

domain.documentation:
Optional ASCII cookie domain using letters, digits, dots and hyphens. Omitted for a host-only cookie.

Example: `{ domain: 'example.com' }`. Helpers borrow options; values are copied into the outgoing header.

maxAge.documentation:
Lifetime in integer seconds, 0 through 34560000. Zero requests deletion. Omitted for a session cookie.

Example: `{ maxAge: 3600 }`. Helpers borrow options; values are copied into the outgoing header.

secure.documentation:
Only send over HTTPS when true; defaults false. Required by __Secure- and __Host- prefixes.

Example: `{ secure: true }`. Helpers borrow options; values are copied into the outgoing header.

httpOnly.documentation:
Hide the cookie from browser script when true; defaults false.

Example: `{ httpOnly: true }`. Helpers borrow options; values are copied into the outgoing header.

sameSite.documentation:
Strict, Lax or None, including lowercase. Omitted by default. None requires secure for browser acceptance.

Example: `{ sameSite: 'Strict' }`. Helpers borrow options; values are copied into the outgoing header.

partitioned.documentation:
Request partitioned browser storage when true; requires secure. Defaults false.

Example: `{ partitioned: true }` with `secure: true`. Helpers borrow options; values are copied into the outgoing header.

HttpApp.name: listen

parameters.label: address: string
parameters.documentation: IP address and port, such as 127.0.0.1:3000; port 0 chooses a free port.

parameters.label: tls?: TlsOptions
parameters.documentation: Omit for cleartext HTTP. Supply { cert, key } PEM strings for HTTPS: certificate chain leaf first, matching unencrypted private key. Invalid configuration throws HttpError code tls before binding.

HttpApp.documentation:
Creates a lazy listener task. Awaiting binds the address, freezes registration and returns a running server. Omit tls for cleartext HTTP; supply { cert, key } for HTTPS with HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 negotiation. cert is a nonempty PEM certificate chain, leaf first. key is its matching unencrypted PKCS#1, PKCS#8 or SEC1 PEM private key. Invalid configuration throws HttpError code tls before binding; invalid address or bind failure throws code address or listen. Clients verify trust, hostname and certificate validity. At most 128 active connections, including handshakes; a TLS handshake has a five-second deadline and shutdown interrupts it. Body readers have a cumulative 1048576-byte limit.

```tsrust
const server = await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0", { cert: certificatePem, key: privateKeyPem });
```

Ownership: consumes app and TLS options immediately. The running server retains independent TLS settings. Dropping Server requests cleanup, which its async owner drains.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

HttpApp.name: configure

parameters.label: options: ReadOnly<ServerOptions>
parameters.documentation: Complete body, connection, handler, time and global request-rate limits; all fields required.

HttpApp.documentation:
Sets listener limits before listen consumes this app. All seven integer fields are required. bodyLimit is 1..67108864 bytes (default 1048576); maxConnections and maxRequests are 1..65536 (default 128 each). requestTimeoutMs is 1..3600000 (default 30000); shutdownTimeoutMs and handshakeTimeoutMs use the same range (default 5000). requestsPerSecond is 0..1000000 (default 0, disabled). Invalid fields throw HttpError code options without changing configuration.

Connections beyond capacity remain in the OS backlog. Concurrent handler overload returns 503. A global fixed one-second window counts arrivals and returns 429 with Retry-After: 1 when exhausted; it is not a per-user or distributed limiter. At most twice the configured rate can cross a window boundary. Handler deadlines return 504 and request cooperative cancellation; response streaming after handler completion is outside this deadline. TLS handshakes and shutdown draining have independent limits. Content-Length exceeding bodyLimit returns 413; streaming reads reject once their cumulative byte budget is exhausted.

```tsrust
app.configure({ bodyLimit: 65536, maxConnections: 64, maxRequests: 32, requestTimeoutMs: 5000, shutdownTimeoutMs: 5000, handshakeTimeoutMs: 3000, requestsPerSecond: 100 });
```

Ownership: mutates app configuration and only borrows options.

examples.source: import {App} from 'std:http'; function main(){const app=new App();app.configure({ bodyLimit: 65536, maxConnections: 64, maxRequests: 32, requestTimeoutMs: 5000, shutdownTimeoutMs: 5000, handshakeTimeoutMs: 3000, requestsPerSecond: 100 });}

At most 128 parts and the configured total request byte limit, including multipart framing. File names are untrusted metadata, never filesystem paths. Nested multipart and streaming upload-to-disk are unsupported by this collecting helper. Returns an owned MultipartPart[]; malformed content, encoding and size failures throw HttpError.

```tsrust

```

Ownership: consumes the request; returned fields own their data. The body cannot be read again.

Returns the first value for a decoded, case-sensitive query name, or undefined when absent. Bare keys and empty values return empty strings. Decodes + as space and valid percent-encoded UTF-8 once.
```tsrust
import {request} from "std:http";function main(){const input=request("GET","http://localhost/?tag=a+b&tag=c","");const value=input.query("tag");if(value!==undefined){console.log(value);}}
```

Expected output: a b.
