HttpResponse.name: body
HttpResponse.documentation:
Transfers the unread body into a streaming reader. No arguments. Reading is lazy; this call performs no I/O. The cumulative read limit is 1048576 bytes.

```tsrust
const body = response.body();
```

Ownership: consumes the response; body cannot be read twice.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const body=response.body();console.log('ok');}

HttpResponse.name: text
HttpResponse.documentation:
Creates a lazy task that collects the body and returns strict UTF-8 text. No arguments. Body, encoding or cumulative 1048576-byte limit failures throw HttpError codes body, encoding or limit. Suspension does not block a worker.

```tsrust
const value = await response.text(); // "hello"
```

Ownership: consumes the response immediately; disposing its task releases the body.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const value=await response.text();console.log('ok');}

HttpResponse.name: status
HttpResponse.documentation:
Returns the HTTP response status. No arguments or mutation.

```tsrust
const value = response.status();
```

Ownership: borrows the response.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const value=response.status();console.log('ok');}

HttpServer.name: address
HttpServer.documentation:
Returns the actual bound IP address and port, including the assigned port when listen used port 0. No arguments or mutation.

```tsrust
const address = server.address();
```

Ownership: borrows the server.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");const address=server.address();await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

HttpServer.name: shutdown
HttpServer.documentation:
Creates a lazy shutdown task. Awaiting stops acceptance, permits up to five seconds for active connections to finish, then cancels stalled connections and drains nested request tasks. No arguments. Cleanup may take longer if synchronous application work does not suspend.

```tsrust
await server.shutdown();
```

Ownership: consumes the server; its listener and requests cannot detach.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

HttpServer.name: wait
HttpServer.documentation:
Creates a lazy task that waits for the running listener to finish. Await this at the end of a standalone service to keep its scope alive. No arguments, defaults or receiver reuse. Cancelling or disposing the waiting task requests server shutdown and drains cleanup through its async owner. Source finally is not promised on cancellation.

```tsrust
await server.wait(); // serve until completion or cancellation
```

Ownership: consumes Server immediately; the returned task owns listener cleanup.

examples.source: import {App,Server} from 'std:http';async function keep(server:Server):Task<void>{await server.wait();}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen('127.0.0.1:0');const running=keep(server).start();running.cancel();try{await running;}catch(error){console.log(error.code);}}

HttpClient.name: send

parameters.label: input: Request
parameters.documentation: Owned request with an absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL and no embedded credentials.

HttpClient.documentation:
Creates a lazy HTTP request task. Awaiting returns response headers and an unread streaming body. HTTP 4xx/5xx are responses, not exceptions. URL, transport and 30-second deadline failures throw HttpError codes url, request or timeout. No redirects, implicit proxies, cookies or decompression. Use response.text() or body() to read once.

```tsrust
const response = await client.send(request("GET", url, ""));
```

Ownership: consumes the request and borrows the reusable client until completion/disposal.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");const client=new Client();const response=await client.send(request("GET","http://"+server.address()+"/",""));await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

HttpBody.name: next
HttpBody.documentation:
Creates a lazy read of the next data frame. Returns owned bytes, or undefined at end. No arguments. Frame boundaries are transport-dependent; trailers are skipped. Cumulative reads above 1048576 bytes throw HttpError code limit; transport failures throw body. No background read-ahead is added.

```tsrust
const chunk = await body.next();
```

Ownership: mutably borrows the body until completion/disposal; concurrent reads are rejected.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const body=response.body();const chunk=await body.next();console.log('ok');}

HttpBody.name: text
HttpBody.documentation:
Collects remaining body data as strict UTF-8 text when awaited. No arguments. The remaining cumulative byte budget still applies. Throws HttpError code body, encoding or limit.

```tsrust
const value = await body.text(); // "hello"
```

Ownership: consumes the body; previously read frames are not replayed.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const body=response.body();const value=await body.text();console.log('ok');}

HttpNext.name: run

parameters.label: input: Request
parameters.documentation: Owned request forwarded downstream.

HttpNext.documentation:
Creates a lazy call to remaining middleware and the selected handler. Awaiting returns the downstream response for header changes. Does not restart earlier middleware. No receiver reuse, cloning or second invocation is permitted.

```tsrust
const response = await next.run(input);
```

Ownership: consumes Next and the request immediately, enforcing at-most-once delegation.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();app.use((input:Request,next:Next):Task<Response>=>next.run(input));const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");const client=new Client();const response=await client.send(request("GET","http://"+server.address()+"/",""));await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

std:numeric.name: toInt

parameters.label: value: int | number
parameters.documentation: Original int or number; no implicit conversion before validation.

std:numeric.documentation:
Returns the same int, or converts a finite, whole number within [-2^63, 2^63) to int. Rejects NonFinite, Fraction or Range. Integer inputs retain all 64 bits. A number already rounded before this call cannot be recovered. Negative zero becomes integer zero. No receiver is mutated. All arguments are required.

```tsrust
import {toInt as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert(42.0)));}
```

Expected output: 42. Ownership: scalar values copy; parseInt borrows its string. Results own their data.

std:numeric.name: toNumber

parameters.label: value: int
parameters.documentation: Signed 64-bit integer to convert exactly.

std:numeric.documentation:
Converts an int to number only when binary64 represents it exactly. Returns Precision otherwise, including 9007199254740993 and the maximum int. Exact integers beyond the safe-integer interval are permitted. No receiver is mutated. All arguments are required.

```tsrust
import {toNumber as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert(42)));}
```

Expected output: 42. Ownership: scalar values copy; parseInt borrows its string. Results own their data.

examples.source: import {toNumber as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert(42)));}

std:numeric.name: toFloat32

parameters.label: value: int | number
parameters.documentation: Original integer or finite floating value; must be exactly representable in binary32.

std:numeric.documentation:
Checks exact representability in binary32 and returns that value as number. Rejects NonFinite, Range for floating overflow, or Precision for rounding and nonzero underflow. Integer inputs are checked before any binary64 conversion. Negative floating zero is preserved. No rounding mode is offered. No receiver is mutated. All arguments are required.

```tsrust
import {toFloat32 as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert(1.5)));}
```

Expected output: 1.5. Ownership: scalar values copy; parseInt borrows its string. Results own their data.

std:numeric.name: checkSigned
std:numeric.signature: checkSigned(value: int, bits: int): Result<int, NumericError>

parameters.label: value: int
parameters.documentation: Signed 64-bit integer to range-check.

parameters.label: bits: int
parameters.documentation: Required width: 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits. No default.

std:numeric.documentation:
Checks the signed range for bits equal to 8, 16, 32 or 64, then returns the unchanged int. Returns Width for another width or Range for an out-of-range value. This validates a boundary; it does not introduce a narrower language type. No receiver is mutated. All arguments are required.

```tsrust
import {checkSigned as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert(127, 8)));}
```

Expected output: 127. Ownership: scalar values copy; parseInt borrows its string. Results own their data.

examples.source: import {checkSigned as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert(127, 8)));}

std:numeric.name: checkUnsigned
std:numeric.signature: checkUnsigned(value: int, bits: int): Result<int, NumericError>

parameters.label: value: int
parameters.documentation: Nonnegative int to range-check; full unsigned 64-bit values are not representable.

parameters.label: bits: int
parameters.documentation: Required width: 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits. No default.

std:numeric.documentation:
Checks the unsigned range for bits equal to 8, 16, 32 or 64, then returns the unchanged int. Returns Width for another width or Range for a negative or out-of-range value. The input and result remain signed 64-bit int: values above 2^63-1 are unsupported even with bits=64. No receiver is mutated. All arguments are required.

```tsrust
import {checkUnsigned as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert(255, 8)));}
```

Expected output: 255. Ownership: scalar values copy; parseInt borrows its string. Results own their data.

examples.source: import {checkUnsigned as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert(255, 8)));}

std:numeric.name: parseInt

parameters.label: text: string
parameters.documentation: Entire decimal string; optional leading sign, then at least one ASCII digit.

std:numeric.documentation:
Parses the entire string as an exact signed 64-bit decimal integer. An optional + or - sign and leading zeroes are accepted. Whitespace, fractions, exponents, separators, radix prefixes and trailing characters return Syntax. Overflow returns Range. Unlike the global parseInt, this returns Result<int, NumericError> and never accepts a numeric prefix. No receiver is mutated. All arguments are required.

```tsrust
import {parseInt as convert} from "std:numeric"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(convert("9223372036854775807")));}
```

Expected output: 9223372036854775807. Ownership: scalar values copy; parseInt borrows its string. Results own their data.

std:numeric.name: NumericError
std:numeric.documentation:
Describes a rejected exact numeric conversion. code is Syntax, Width, NonFinite, Fraction, Range or Precision; message explains the failure. Conversion functions return Err with this record and never round to claim success.

```tsrust
import {NumericError} from "std:numeric"; function describe(error:ReadOnly<NumericError>):string{return error.code+": "+error.message;} function main(){}
```

Expected output: none. Ownership: independent record with string fields; no resource cleanup.

examples.source: import {NumericError} from "std:numeric"; function describe(error:ReadOnly<NumericError>):string{return error.code+": "+error.message;} function main(){}

std:decimal.name: parseDecimal

parameters.label: text: string
parameters.documentation: Complete plain decimal text, at most 128 bytes. No whitespace or exponent syntax.

std:decimal.documentation:
Validates a complete plain decimal string and returns its exact value. Accepts optional + or -, decimal digits and an optional dot followed by digits. Leading/trailing zeroes are accepted and normalized; negative zero becomes zero. Whitespace, exponents, separators and missing digits return Syntax. Input is limited to 128 UTF-8 bytes; excess length or value bounds return Range. Values allow at most 38 significant digits, 38 integer digits and 28 fractional places after removing trailing zeroes.  All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){const value=unwrap(parseDecimal("19.990")); console.log(format(value));}
```

Expected output: 19.99. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

examples.source: import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){const value=unwrap(parseDecimal("19.990")); console.log(format(value));}

std:decimal.name: fromInt

parameters.label: value: int
parameters.documentation: Exact signed 64-bit value; never widened through number.

std:decimal.documentation:
Constructs an exact decimal from a signed 64-bit int. Every int fits; this operation has no conversion error. Values allow at most 38 significant digits, 38 integer digits and 28 fractional places after removing trailing zeroes.  All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(format(fromInt(42)));}
```

Expected output: 42. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: format

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Decimal value to format; borrowed and unchanged.

std:decimal.documentation:
Returns canonical plain decimal text without exponent notation or unnecessary trailing zeroes. Zero formats as 0. Formatting preserves the exact value but does not preserve the input spelling or scale. All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(format(unwrap(parseDecimal("1.2300"))));}
```

Expected output: 1.23. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: formatFixed
std:decimal.signature: formatFixed(value: ReadOnly<Decimal>, scale: int): Result<string, DecimalError>

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Decimal to format without rounding.

parameters.label: scale: int
parameters.documentation: Required fractional places, 0..28; no default.

std:decimal.documentation:
Returns plain decimal text with exactly scale fractional places, padding zeroes when needed. scale must be 0..28; otherwise returns Scale. If removing places would change the value, returns Precision. Never rounds money silently. All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(formatFixed(unwrap(parseDecimal("1.2")),2)));}
```

Expected output: 1.20. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: add
std:decimal.signature: add(left: ReadOnly<Decimal>, right: ReadOnly<Decimal>): Result<Decimal, DecimalError>

parameters.label: left: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Left operand, borrowed.

parameters.label: right: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Right operand, borrowed.

std:decimal.documentation:
Returns the exact sum. Returns Range when the normalized result exceeds decimal bounds; neither operand changes. Values allow at most 38 significant digits, 38 integer digits and 28 fractional places after removing trailing zeroes.  All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(format(unwrap(add(unwrap(parseDecimal("0.1")),unwrap(parseDecimal("0.2"))))));}
```

Expected output: 0.3. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: subtract
std:decimal.signature: subtract(left: ReadOnly<Decimal>, right: ReadOnly<Decimal>): Result<Decimal, DecimalError>

parameters.label: left: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Left operand, borrowed.

parameters.label: right: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Value subtracted from left, borrowed.

std:decimal.documentation:
Returns left minus right exactly. Returns Range when the normalized result exceeds decimal bounds; neither operand changes. Values allow at most 38 significant digits, 38 integer digits and 28 fractional places after removing trailing zeroes.  All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(format(unwrap(subtract(unwrap(parseDecimal("1.2")),unwrap(parseDecimal("0.3"))))));}
```

Expected output: 0.9. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: multiply
std:decimal.signature: multiply(left: ReadOnly<Decimal>, right: ReadOnly<Decimal>): Result<Decimal, DecimalError>

parameters.label: left: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: First factor, borrowed.

parameters.label: right: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Second factor, borrowed.

std:decimal.documentation:
Returns the exact product. Returns Range when the normalized result exceeds decimal bounds, including fractional precision; never rounds to fit. Values allow at most 38 significant digits, 38 integer digits and 28 fractional places after removing trailing zeroes.  All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(formatFixed(unwrap(multiply(unwrap(parseDecimal("19.99")),fromInt(3))),2)));}
```

Expected output: 59.97. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: divideExact
std:decimal.signature: divideExact(left: ReadOnly<Decimal>, right: ReadOnly<Decimal>): Result<Decimal, DecimalError>

parameters.label: left: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Dividend, borrowed.

parameters.label: right: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Nonzero divisor, borrowed.

std:decimal.documentation:
Returns an exact terminating decimal quotient within the decimal bounds. Zero divisor returns DivideByZero. Inexact division, including 1/3, returns Precision. An exact quotient outside the bounds returns Range. No rounding or implicit scale policy is applied. Values allow at most 38 significant digits, 38 integer digits and 28 fractional places after removing trailing zeroes.  All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(format(unwrap(divideExact(fromInt(1),fromInt(8)))));}
```

Expected output: 0.125. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: compare

parameters.label: left: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Left value, borrowed.

parameters.label: right: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Right value, borrowed.

std:decimal.documentation:
Compares exact decimal values and returns -1 when left is smaller, 0 when equal, or 1 when larger. Input spelling and trailing zeroes do not affect equality. Use this function for value ordering; decimal objects are not collection keys. All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(compare(unwrap(parseDecimal("1.0")),fromInt(1)));}
```

Expected output: 0. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: toInt

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Whole decimal within signed 64-bit range.

std:decimal.documentation:
Converts a whole decimal to signed 64-bit int exactly. A nonzero fractional part returns Precision; a whole value outside the int range returns Range. No truncation or rounding occurs. All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(toInt(unwrap(parseDecimal("9223372036854775807")))));}
```

Expected output: 9223372036854775807. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: toNumber

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<Decimal>
parameters.documentation: Decimal that must retain its exact mathematical value in binary64.

std:decimal.documentation:
Converts only values exactly representable as finite binary64 number. Returns Precision for values such as 0.1 or 9007199254740993. Returns Range if no finite result is available. Use decimal text for exact serialization when this conversion fails. All arguments are required. No receiver or input is mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDecimal,fromInt,format,formatFixed,add,subtract,multiply,divideExact,compare,toInt,toNumber} from "std:decimal"; function main(){console.log(unwrap(toNumber(unwrap(parseDecimal("1.25")))));}
```

Expected output: 1.25. Ownership: inputs are borrowed or scalar copies; returned values own independent storage. Clone Decimal explicitly when retaining another owner.

std:decimal.name: Decimal
std:decimal.documentation:
Opaque exact decimal value. Values allow at most 38 significant digits, 38 integer digits and 28 fractional places after removing trailing zeroes. Parse text or use fromInt; direct object construction, field access, implicit JSON/SQL conversion and collection keys are unsupported. Use format for explicit text serialization and parseDecimal to validate incoming text. Values can live in records, arrays and nullable unions, and can cross worker boundaries. Explicit clone owns independent storage.

```tsrust
import {Decimal} from "std:decimal"; function main(){}
```

Expected output: none. Ownership: owned value; ordinary scope cleanup releases storage.

std:decimal.name: DecimalError
std:decimal.documentation:
Owned conversion/arithmetic error with code and message strings. Codes are Syntax, Range, Scale, Precision and DivideByZero. Operations return this error as Result data; inspecting it does not mutate it.

```tsrust
import {DecimalError} from "std:decimal"; function main(){}
```

Expected output: none. Ownership: owned value; ordinary scope cleanup releases storage.

std:date.name: parseDate

parameters.label: text: string
parameters.documentation: Complete YYYY-MM-DD text; exactly ten ASCII bytes.

std:date.documentation:
Validates a complete YYYY-MM-DD Gregorian calendar date in years 0001..9999. Exactly four year digits and two month/day digits are required. Syntax rejects alternate layouts, whitespace and timestamps; Range rejects invalid days and out-of-range years. No rollover, local time or time zone is inferred. All arguments are required. Inputs are not mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDate,formatDate,format,addDays,addMonths,differenceInCalendarDays,compareAsc,isLeapYear,getYear,getMonth,getDate,startOfMonth,endOfMonth} from "std:date"; function main(){const date=unwrap(parseDate("2024-02-29"));console.log(formatDate(unwrap(parseDate('2024-02-29'))));}
```

Expected output: 2024-02-29. Ownership: date and string inputs are borrowed; returned Date values own independent storage. Clone explicitly to retain another owner.

std:date.name: formatDate

parameters.label: value: Date
parameters.documentation: Validated calendar date; borrowed and unchanged.

std:date.documentation:
Returns exactly YYYY-MM-DD with zero-padded Gregorian year, month and day. The value has no time of day or time zone. All arguments are required. Inputs are not mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDate,formatDate,format,addDays,addMonths,differenceInCalendarDays,compareAsc,isLeapYear,getYear,getMonth,getDate,startOfMonth,endOfMonth} from "std:date"; function main(){const date=unwrap(parseDate("2024-02-29"));console.log(formatDate(date));}
```

Expected output: 2024-02-29. Ownership: date and string inputs are borrowed; returned Date values own independent storage. Clone explicitly to retain another owner.

std:date.name: format
std:date.signature: format(value: Date, pattern: string): Result<string, DateError>

parameters.label: value: Date
parameters.documentation: Validated calendar date; borrowed and unchanged.

parameters.label: pattern: string
parameters.documentation: Formatting pattern of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; supported tokens and quoting are listed above.

std:date.documentation:
Formats a calendar date using yyyy, yy, MMMM, MMM, MM, M, dd, d, EEEE and EEE tokens. Month and weekday names are English. Quote literal letters with single quotes; doubled single quotes emit one quote. Other characters are literal. Format rejects unknown alphabetic tokens, unclosed quotes and patterns over 256 UTF-8 bytes. In particular YYYY and DD are not supported. No locale, time or zone tokens are available. All arguments are required. Inputs are not mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDate,formatDate,format,addDays,addMonths,differenceInCalendarDays,compareAsc,isLeapYear,getYear,getMonth,getDate,startOfMonth,endOfMonth} from "std:date"; function main(){const date=unwrap(parseDate("2024-02-29"));console.log(unwrap(format(date,'EEEE, MMMM d, yyyy')));}
```

Expected output: Thursday, February 29, 2024. Ownership: date and string inputs are borrowed; returned Date values own independent storage. Clone explicitly to retain another owner.

examples.source: import {parseDate,formatDate,format,addDays,addMonths,differenceInCalendarDays,compareAsc,isLeapYear,getYear,getMonth,getDate,startOfMonth,endOfMonth} from "std:date"; function main(){const date=unwrap(parseDate("2024-02-29"));console.log(unwrap(format(date,'EEEE, MMMM d, yyyy')));}

std:date.name: addDays
std:date.signature: addDays(value: Date, amount: int): Result<Date, DateError>

parameters.label: value: Date
parameters.documentation: Validated calendar date; borrowed and unchanged.

parameters.label: amount: int
parameters.documentation: Signed integer count; negative values subtract, zero retains the date.

std:date.documentation:
Returns a new date shifted by amount calendar days. amount is a signed 64-bit integer; negative values subtract days and zero returns an independent equal value. Range rejects arithmetic overflow or a result outside years 0001..9999. Calendar days do not represent elapsed 24-hour periods. All arguments are required. Inputs are not mutated.

```tsrust
import {parseDate,formatDate,format,addDays,addMonths,differenceInCalendarDays,compareAsc,isLeapYear,getYear,getMonth,getDate,startOfMonth,endOfMonth} from "std:date"; function main(){const date=unwrap(parseDate("2024-02-29"));console.log(formatDate(unwrap(addDays(date,1))));}
```

Expected output: 2024-03-01. Ownership: date and string inputs are borrowed; returned Date values own independent storage. Clone explicitly to retain another owner.

std:date.name: addMonths
std:date.signature: addMonths(value: Date, amount: int): Result<Date, DateError>

parameters.label: value: Date

std:cache.name: LruCache
std:cache.signature: new LruCache<K, V>(capacity: int): LruCache<K, V>
std:cache.documentation:
Creates an empty local least-recently-used cache. capacity is a positive int item limit; zero or negative capacity raises RangeError. There is no default TTL or background cleanup. This bounds entries, not payload bytes. Keys use one string, int, number, boolean or enum type; NaN keys compare equal and negative zero normalizes to positive zero. Object and mixed-union keys are unsupported. Values must own their storage; borrowed views, callbacks and task handles cannot be retained.

Non-copy values borrow read-only storage and retain an exclusive cache-owner loan until last use; no further cache operation or owner transfer is allowed during that loan. Copy scalars are independent snapshots. Last-use release applies to acyclic local bodies; loops, deferred callbacks, named capture plans and exception regions retain the lexical boundary, so use an inner block there. Use explicit clone(value) when supported, or remove to transfer ownership.

parameters.label: capacity: int
parameters.documentation: Positive maximum number of retained entries; invalid values raise RangeError.

std:cache.documentation:

std:cache.name: SharedLruCache
std:cache.signature: new SharedLruCache<K, V>(capacity: int): SharedLruCache<K, V>
std:cache.documentation:
Creates a shared LRU cache bounded by entry count. Capacity is a positive int; zero or negative capacity throws RangeError. Keys use one numeric, boolean, string or enum type. Values must be transferable owned data supporting independent cloning; resources, endpoints, tasks and callbacks are rejected. There is no byte-size bound or background expiration. Concurrent operations serialize; individual calls are atomic, but a get followed by set is not a transaction or single-flight loader. Methods accept read access to the handle while synchronizing entry changes; ReadOnly does not freeze shared entries.

```tsrust

```

parameters.label: capacity: int
parameters.documentation: Maximum number of entries; must be positive.

LruCache.name: get
LruCache.documentation:

Copy scalars are independent snapshots. Last-use release applies to acyclic local bodies; loops, deferred callbacks, named capture plans and exception regions retain the lexical boundary, so use an inner block there. Use explicit clone(value) when supported, or remove to transfer ownership.

parameters.label: key: ReadOnly<K>

LruCache.name: peek

LruCache.name: set
LruCache.signature: set(key: K, value: V, ttlMs?: int): Result<CacheEntry<K, V> | undefined, CacheInsertError<K, V>>
LruCache.documentation:
Inserts an owned entry as most recent. ttlMs, when supplied, must be a positive int number of monotonic milliseconds from insertion. Omission removes any previous deadline. Ok returns the replaced entry or the live least-recent entry evicted at capacity; otherwise undefined. Expired entries are disposed before capacity eviction. Err.code is "ttl" for a nonpositive TTL or "deadline" for clock overflow and returns the original key/value. Validation occurs before cleanup, replacement or eviction, so failure leaves the cache unchanged.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: one.

parameters.documentation: Owned key to store.

parameters.label: value: V

parameters.label: ttlMs?: int

HttpRouter.name: listen

parameters.label: address: string
parameters.documentation: IP address and port, such as 127.0.0.1:3000; port 0 chooses a free port.

parameters.label: tls?: TlsOptions
parameters.documentation: Omit for cleartext HTTP. Supply { cert, key } PEM strings for HTTPS: certificate chain leaf first, matching unencrypted private key. Invalid configuration throws HttpError code tls before binding.

HttpRouter.documentation:
Creates a lazy listener task. Awaiting binds the address, freezes registration and returns a running server. Omit tls for cleartext HTTP; supply { cert, key } for HTTPS with HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 negotiation. cert is a nonempty PEM certificate chain, leaf first. key is its matching unencrypted PKCS#1, PKCS#8 or SEC1 PEM private key. Invalid configuration throws HttpError code tls before binding; invalid address or bind failure throws code address or listen. Clients verify trust, hostname and certificate validity. At most 128 active connections, including handshakes; a TLS handshake has a five-second deadline and shutdown interrupts it. Body readers have a cumulative 1048576-byte limit.

```tsrust
const server = await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0", { cert: certificatePem, key: privateKeyPem });
```

Ownership: consumes app and TLS options immediately. The running server retains independent TLS settings. Dropping Server requests cleanup, which its async owner drains.

HttpRouter.name: configure

parameters.label: options: ReadOnly<ServerOptions>
parameters.documentation: Complete body, connection, handler, time and global request-rate limits; all fields required.

HttpRouter.documentation:
Sets listener limits before listen consumes this app. All seven integer fields are required. bodyLimit is 1..67108864 bytes (default 1048576); maxConnections and maxRequests are 1..65536 (default 128 each). requestTimeoutMs is 1..3600000 (default 30000); shutdownTimeoutMs and handshakeTimeoutMs use the same range (default 5000). requestsPerSecond is 0..1000000 (default 0, disabled). Invalid fields throw HttpError code options without changing configuration.

Connections beyond capacity remain in the OS backlog. Concurrent handler overload returns 503. A global fixed one-second window counts arrivals and returns 429 with Retry-After: 1 when exhausted; it is not a per-user or distributed limiter. At most twice the configured rate can cross a window boundary. Handler deadlines return 504 and request cooperative cancellation; response streaming after handler completion is outside this deadline. TLS handshakes and shutdown draining have independent limits. Content-Length exceeding bodyLimit returns 413; streaming reads reject once their cumulative byte budget is exhausted.

```tsrust
app.configure({ bodyLimit: 65536, maxConnections: 64, maxRequests: 32, requestTimeoutMs: 5000, shutdownTimeoutMs: 5000, handshakeTimeoutMs: 3000, requestsPerSecond: 100 });
```

Ownership: mutates app configuration and only borrows options.

SqlCursor.name: next
SqlCursor.documentation:
Reads the next owned row, or undefined at end of results. Takes no arguments. The lazy task does not advance the cursor until awaited. Rows remain valid after the cursor closes. EOF releases the connection; further next() calls return undefined. Database failures and duplicate result-column names throw SqlError, release the stream and leave the cursor at EOF. Alias duplicate columns explicitly. Canceling a pending next task does not consume the cursor; close or drop it to abandon the query.

```tsrust
const row = await cursor.next();
if (row !== undefined) { console.log(unwrap(row.int('value'))); } // 1
```

Ownership: exclusively borrows the cursor until the task completes or is dropped; returns an independently owned row.

SqlCursor.name: close
SqlCursor.documentation:
Disposes a cursor without reading remaining rows. Takes no arguments, returns no value and consumes the cursor. Connection cleanup follows the database driver; pool operations can reuse it once cleanup finishes. Calling close after EOF is allowed; calling any method on the consumed cursor is rejected. Dropping the cursor performs the same cleanup.

```tsrust
const cursor = await db.cursor('SELECT 1 AS value');
cursor.close(); // abandon before reading
```

Ownership: consumes the cursor and releases its pool loan. A pending next() loan must finish or be dropped first.

std:ui.name: Route

parameters.label: props: RouteProps
parameters.documentation: path is an absolute local path. exact defaults to true. render is an owned zero-argument factory returning Node, called once on first match.

std:ui.documentation: Lazily constructs a retained route subtree on web and native. Create the single location() owner first. path uses local navigation rules, normalizes trailing slashes and rejects queries, escapes, traversal and fragments. exact defaults to true; false also matches descendant path segments, so /docs matches /docs/api but not /docs-other. Location fragments do not change the route. render runs once at the first match; later visits preserve the same Nodes, fields, component state and scroll positions. Inactive content leaves layout, input and accessibility. Returns a transparent Node without an extra layout/focus element. Factory errors propagate without an automatic retry. This defers construction, not executable download. Example: <Route path="/docs" render={() => <Text>Documentation</Text>}/> initially renders nothing at / and renders Documentation after navigate("/docs"). Ownership: consumes the factory, drops its captures after construction, retains visited content until parent disposal, and never retains or replaces the location owner. An unvisited factory releases when its parent disposes.

examples.source: import {View,Text,Route,location,Node,document} from 'std:ui';function App():Node{const path=location();return <View><Route path="/" render={()=> <Text>Home</Text>}/><Route path="/docs" render={()=> <Text>Documentation</Text>}/></View>;}function main(){const app=App();console.log(document(app,'Route').includes('Home'));}

std:ui.name: RouteProps
std:ui.documentation: Properties for retained, lazy route content. Supply path and render; exact defaults to true. Only a matching route calls its factory. For example, <Route path="/docs" exact={false} render={() => <Text>Docs</Text>}/> matches /docs and /docs/api. Ownership: transfers the factory once; constructed content remains owned by its route.

path.documentation: Required absolute local route path. Trailing slashes normalize. Queries, escapes, traversal and heading fragments throw. Example: path="/docs" matches /docs, including /docs#heading. Read at construction; changing an ordinary prop record does not update the path. Ownership: copies the checked path into the route.

exact.documentation: Optional boolean, default true. false matches the path and its descendants at slash boundaries. Example: path="/docs" exact={false} matches /docs/api and rejects /docs-other. / with exact=false matches all local paths. Fragments do not affect matching. Ownership: copies one boolean at construction.

render.documentation: Required owned zero-argument function returning Node. Runs once on the first match. Example: render={() => <Text>Hello</Text>} constructs Hello only after its route becomes active. Revisits keep the same subtree and state. Errors propagate; no automatic retry. Ownership: consumes the factory and releases captures after its call; uncalled factories and visited subtrees release with the parent.

std:ui.name: Link

parameters.label: props: LinkProps
parameters.documentation: href is an absolute application path or HTTPS URL without credentials. children contains owned phrasing content; className defaults to empty. Element identity and naming are forwarded.

std:ui.documentation: Creates a link with browser anchor semantics and native accessibility Link role. Local href values such as /docs and /docs#heading navigate without reloading; construct interactive local links after the application location owner. Local queries, percent escapes, backslashes, whitespace and traversal throw. HTTPS URLs require a host and reject credentials, raw controls, whitespace and backslashes. Browser HTTPS links follow the anchor, including modified clicks; native activation opens the default browser and leaves local history unchanged. Native launch failure throws a readable error. Other schemes, including javascript:, file:, http: and protocol-relative URLs, are rejected. Example: <Link href="https://github.com/Forever-Frameworks-LLC/tsrust/releases">Releases</Link> opens GitHub Releases. document() emits an escaped anchor without launching anything. Ownership: consumes children and strings; local links hold only a non-retaining location binding, and HTTPS links need no location owner.

std:ui.name: location
std:ui.documentation: Creates the single application location owner. No arguments. Starts at the browser pathname plus fragment, or / on native. get() returns an owned path snapshot; set(path) checks and normalizes a local path, pushes history and updates the binding. A repeated current path adds no entry. Browser back/forward updates the same signal. Native history starts at /. A second live owner or invalid initial path throws. Example: const path = location(); returning <Text>{path.get()}</Text> shows / initially on native. Create it directly in a root component const declaration so its state is retained automatically. Ownership: one component owns the location; callbacks and history listeners use non-retaining bindings.

std:ui.name: navigate

parameters.label: path: string
parameters.documentation: Absolute application path with an optional nonempty heading fragment. The local path restrictions of Link apply; HTTPS links cannot be passed to navigate.

std:ui.documentation: Pushes an application location and updates shared route bindings without reloading the browser. Returns void; does not mutate the argument. The current path is a no-op. A missing/disposed location owner or invalid path throws. Example: navigate("/docs"); makes location().get() /docs on the existing owner; do not create another location owner to read it. Ownership: borrows the path and retains no state owner.

std:ui.name: back
std:ui.documentation: Visits the previous application history entry. No arguments; returns void. Browser behavior follows browser history, including leaving the site when appropriate. Native history stops at its initial entry. A missing/disposed location owner throws. Example: navigate("/docs"); back(); restores / on a new native application. Ownership: retains no location or route subtree.

std:ui.name: forward
std:ui.documentation: Visits the next application history entry after back(). No arguments; returns void. Browser traversal is asynchronous; native traversal updates the location immediately. Native history with no next entry is unchanged. A missing/disposed location owner throws. Example: navigate("/docs"); back(); forward(); restores /docs on native. Ownership: retains no location or route subtree.

std:ui.name: CopyButton

parameters.label: props: CopyButtonProps
parameters.documentation: value is the exact text to copy, including Unicode, CRLF and trailing whitespace. className defaults to empty; normal element identity and accessible naming props apply.

std:ui.documentation: Creates a platform clipboard button labeled Copy. Activating it writes value; the button is disabled while the browser operation is pending. Copied appears only after success. Failure shows Copy failed. Try again. and exposes the platform message as its description/title without removing the application. Browser copying requires a secure context and may require user activation or permission. Native uses the OS clipboard. An empty string clears text contents. Example: <CopyButton value="café\r\n" className="rounded px-3 py-2"/> copies those exact characters. No promise or lifetime handle is exposed. Ownership: consumes props, owns a text snapshot, and completion callbacks never retain a disposed subtree.

std:ui.name: CopyButtonProps
std:ui.documentation: Clipboard button properties. value is required; className and inherited ElementProps are optional. Ownership: consumes the value and other supplied strings.

value.documentation: Required string copied exactly, including Unicode, newlines and whitespace. No trimming or numeric conversion. <CopyButton value="hello"/> copies hello on activation. Empty text is supported. Ownership: stores an independent snapshot.

className.documentation: Optional checked shared button utilities, default empty. <CopyButton value="hello" className="rounded border px-3 py-2"/> styles the control on both targets. Unknown utilities throw. Shared aspect utilities set a preferred width/height ratio: aspect-square (1), aspect-video (16/9), aspect-[W/H], aspect-[R], or aspect-auto. Ratios must be finite, positive and within f32 native layout range; both targets use the normalized f32 ratio. With default spacing, <View className="w-64 aspect-video"/> is 256 by 144 logical pixels. Explicit width and height and min/max bounds take precedence. Children can overflow without clipping. relative keeps normal flow; absolute/sticky offsets remain unsupported. Ownership: consumes the string.

std:ui.name: Text

parameters.label: props: TextProps
parameters.documentation: Optional children is an ordered Child array: scalar text/bindings and inline Text or Link nodes. Null/undefined are omitted. className defaults to empty.

std:ui.documentation: Creates text from literal and reactive children in their supplied order. Strings and numeric snapshots are joined without a separator; signals display int, number, boolean or string values and update after handlers. Number text uses ordinary language formatting, including NaN/infinities and -0 as 0. Example: <Text>Count: {count}</Text> shows Count: 0 for a zero-valued signal. JSX scalar expressions reading local component state also refresh: <Text>{count.get()+1}</Text> displays 2 for count 1. Declared scalar helper results participate; unknown/inferred helper results and arbitrary prop-record reads remain snapshots. Expressions must be pure. Bare boolean literals remain unsupported; explicit boolean bindings display true/false. Only changed bound text is updated; the component is not rerun. Empty children are valid. Null and undefined children are omitted; <Text>A{null}B{undefined}</Text> displays AB. Invalid utilities or a disposed signal throw a readable error.  Optional as selects span (default), div, p, h1–h6, code, kbd, strong, em or del; headings expose the same level in native accessibility. Semantic props accept id, aria-label, aria-hidden, data-slot and the supported noninteractive roles. Example: <Text as="h2">Profile</Text> produces a level-two heading. Invalid tag/role combinations throw; blocks, arbitrary HTML and editable controls are not accepted. Nested Text and local Link share wrapping and preserve semantic identity. <Text as="p">Read <Text as="strong">carefully</Text> then <Link href="/docs">open docs</Link>.</Text> renders one paragraph. Inline descendants accept typography and text colors; box/layout styles throw. Native links keep separate keyboard and accessibility targets at their shaped text ranges. Browser text selection and native paragraph selection cross styled runs. On native, drag to select, Shift+arrows to extend, and use the platform select-all/copy shortcuts; selection stays within one paragraph. Ownership: consumes props; state bindings do not keep component state alive.

std:ui.name: View

parameters.label: props: ViewProps
parameters.documentation: Optional children is an ordered Child array: text strings/numbers, Signal/TextBinding values, owned Nodes, null or undefined. Omission defaults to empty. className defaults to empty.

std:ui.documentation: Creates a container from ordered strings/numbers, Signal/TextBinding values and owned Node children. JSX scalar expressions reading directly declared local state refresh after handlers without replacing nodes. Adjacent text/bindings share one text run; explicit nodes keep their place. Null, undefined, empty strings and omitted children produce no anonymous text node. Unknown utilities or depth over 128 fail. as selects div (default), section, span or label; all are native layout containers. Example: <View>Hello <Text as="code">world</Text></View> preserves Hello then world without cloning the child. Font size, color and text alignment inherit. Exact semantic attributes, roles and naming rules apply. Grid/flex display, equal grid tracks (1–12), bounded grid placement, per-side padding/gaps, preferred/min/max dimensions, alignment, wrapping and grow/shrink use the same logical-pixel model on both targets. p/px/py and size expand to independent properties; later classes win per property/state. Spacing 2/4/6 uses sm/md/lg, 1 uses sm/2, 3 averages sm/md; other numeric sizes use spacing.md/4 per unit. Percentage heights need a definite parent height. Example: <View className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 p-4" /> creates two equal tracks with default 16px gaps/padding. Viewport sm/md/lg/xl/2xl variants use 640/768/1024/1280/1536 logical pixels; dark matches the enclosing theme. Arbitrary CSS, container queries, named grid lines and subgrid remain unsupported.  A conditional JSX ternary whose condition reads directly declared component state mounts only its selected branch. Nested branches work. Unchanged selection preserves child state; removal releases it once, and later selection constructs fresh state. Transparent slots add no layout or accessibility element. Empty/absent derived text in containers also contributes no anonymous layout item; explicit Text components keep their own node. For example, <View>{visible.get()?<Text>Ready</Text>:null}</View> shows/hides Ready. Prebuilt owned Nodes cannot be consumed repeatedly from captures; ordinary callback ownership errors apply. Invalid interactive/label/hidden ancestry is checked again after replacement. Use as="kbd" or as="code" for composed noninteractive phrasing containers; these tags do not register keyboard handlers. View.hidden excludes a retained subtree from layout, input and accessibility until shown; unlike conditional removal, it preserves child state. overflow-auto scrolls a bounded container on both targets; screen dimensions use logical window/browser viewport size. View.tabIndex=0 adds a source-order Tab stop; -1 permits programmatic/accessibility focus. View.windowDragRegion marks noninteractive custom-header drag surfaces. Semantic as also supports nav/main/header/footer/aside/article, blockquote, ul/ol/li and table/thead/tbody/tr/th/td. These keep their browser/native landmark, list and table roles; use explicit layout classes. Example: <View as="table"><View as="tr"><View as="td"><Text>Value</Text></View></View></View> exposes a table cell. Ownership: consumes props and child nodes, including on failure; bindings never retain state owners.

std:ui.name: Button

parameters.label: props: ButtonProps
parameters.documentation: Optional children accepts strings/numbers, Signal/TextBinding values and owned phrasing Nodes, null or undefined. disabled defaults to false and also accepts compiler-derived ReactiveBoolean conditions. onPress is optional. className defaults to empty.

std:ui.documentation: Creates a semantic, focusable button from text, reactive bindings and owned phrasing children. JSX scalar text expressions reading local state refresh after handlers. Text/inline spans, code and kbd are supported; flow elements, nested controls and nonpresentational child roles fail instead of losing semantics. Null/undefined children are omitted without splitting adjacent text. Children are centered within padding; text alignment inherits into each line. rounded also rounds the native focus outline. onPress is optional: a button with no handler activates without changing state. Pointer click, Enter and Space invoke a supplied handler once. Disabled buttons never invoke it or take native focus. State-dependent disabled={count.get()<5} reevaluates after handlers, including for buttons with no handler. Handler/predicate failure stops the mounted tree with cleanup. Example: <Button onPress={()=>{count.set(count.get()+1);}}>Count: {count}</Button> displays a live count. aria-label overrides the accessible name; hidden descendant text does not contribute to it. Semantic construction failures throw readable strings.  A conditional JSX ternary whose condition reads directly declared component state mounts only its selected branch. Nested branches work. Unchanged selection preserves child state; removal releases it once, and later selection constructs fresh state. Transparent slots add no layout or accessibility element. Empty/absent derived text in containers also contributes no anonymous layout item; explicit Text components keep their own node. For example, <View>{visible.get()?<Text>Ready</Text>:null}</View> shows/hides Ready. Prebuilt owned Nodes cannot be consumed repeatedly from captures; ordinary callback ownership errors apply. Invalid interactive/label/hidden ancestry is checked again after replacement. Ownership: consumes children and the optional handler; callbacks/bindings release with the subtree and never keep component state alive.

std:ui.name: document

parameters.label: node: ReadOnly<Node>
parameters.documentation: Tree to render, borrowed without modification.

parameters.label: title: string
parameters.documentation: Document title; HTML metacharacters are escaped.

std:ui.documentation: Produces a complete semantic HTML document with the shared utility styles. Escapes text and title, preserving Unicode. Does not launch a browser, execute handlers or mutate nodes. Example: document(<Text>Hello</Text>, "Demo") returns HTML containing an escaped title and a span labelled Hello. Ownership: borrows the tree and title; returns an independent owned string.

std:ui.name: run
std:ui.signature: run(node: Node, title: string, options?: WindowOptions): Result<void, UiError>

parameters.label: node: Node
parameters.documentation: Owned tree displayed until window closure; consumed even if startup fails.

parameters.label: title: string
parameters.documentation: Native window title, borrowed during setup.

parameters.label: options?: WindowOptions
parameters.documentation: Optional creation-time dimensions and native/custom titlebar. Defaults to 640×480 logical pixels, minimum 240×160, native titlebar. Invalid dimensions return Err. Browsers validate options but keep their host window.

std:ui.documentation: Opens a GPU-rendered native window and waits for closure on the main thread. Returns Ok after window resources are released, or Err with code UiError and a readable message if initialization or rendering fails. Resize and DPI changes update layout. Content larger than the native window scrolls with wheel or trackpad input. PageUp/PageDown, Home/End and arrow keys scroll when a text field is not handling them; Tab reveals the focused control. Scroll offsets also update pointer targets, accessibility bounds and text-input positions. Optional WindowOptions selects initial/minimum dimensions and titlebar at creation. Custom titlebars currently require macOS, preserve real traffic-light controls and use View.windowDragRegion for dragging. Other desktop platforms return Err for custom. Reserve header space; live titlebar switching is unsupported. Browser mounts validate options but cannot change their host window. Invalid options return Err before a window opens. No CPU fallback is selected. Example: unwrap(run(<Text>Hello</Text>, "Demo")) displays Hello until the window closes. Requires a graphical desktop and supported GPU. Ownership: consumes the subtree; renderer resources belong to the event loop and release on exit.

std:ui.name: signal
std:ui.documentation: Creates independent component state from an int, number, boolean or string. initial is required; infer T from the value or write signal<string>("ready"). Arrays, records, nullable values, resources and callbacks are rejected. Declare state with const inside a component. Example: const name = signal("Ada"); <Text>{name}</Text> displays Ada; name.set("Grace") changes subsequent reads and bound text. int retains the full signed 64-bit range. number retains IEEE-754 values, including NaN, infinities and signed zero; text displays ordinary number strings, with -0 displayed as 0. Constructor aliases and creation inside anonymous callbacks are unsupported. Ownership: strings are independent snapshots; returning the component tree retains the single owner automatically. Bindings and callback captures never extend its lifetime.

parameters.label: initial: T
parameters.documentation: Required initial int, number, boolean or string. Strings are copied into state; there is no default value.

std:ui.name: Node
std:ui.documentation: An owned UI subtree produced by components. Moving it transfers children and retained handlers. A component return retains its local signal owners automatically. Nodes cannot be constructed as records, cloned or sent to workers. Example: const node = <Text>Hello</Text>; owns one text node. A conditional JSX ternary whose condition reads directly declared component state mounts only its selected branch. Nested branches work. Unchanged selection preserves child state; removal releases it once, and later selection constructs fresh state. Transparent slots add no layout or accessibility element. Empty/absent derived text in containers also contributes no anonymous layout item; explicit Text components keep their own node. For example, <View>{visible.get()?<Text>Ready</Text>:null}</View> shows/hides Ready. Prebuilt owned Nodes cannot be consumed repeatedly from captures; ordinary callback ownership errors apply. Invalid interactive/label/hidden ancestry is checked again after replacement.

std:ui.name: Signal
std:ui.documentation: Component state holding int, number, boolean or string. T defaults to int when a type argument is omitted; signal(initial) still requires an initial value. Use state directly in Text children and callback bodies. Example: const active = signal(false); active.set(true); active.get(); returns true. String reads are independent snapshots. Ownership: the returned component tree retains one owner; text bindings and captures are non-retaining. Disposed references throw UiError. Signals cannot be cloned or sent to workers.

std:ui.name: UiError
std:ui.documentation: A UI failure with string code and message fields. run returns Err for renderer or handler failures and releases its owned subtree. Example: const result = run(node, "Demo"); returns Result<void, UiError>. Errors own their message; no renderer resource is retained.

std:ui.name: WindowOptions
std:ui.documentation: Optional creation-time settings for run. Dimensions use finite logical pixels, not physical display pixels. Omitted fields use documented defaults. Minima cannot exceed initial dimensions. For example, run(node, "Docs", {width: 1040, height: 760, minWidth: 480, titlebar: "custom"}) creates a macOS window whose own content supplies the header while retaining OS window controls. Options are serialized and validated before opening; invalid values or unsupported custom titlebars return Err. Browser hosts retain their dimensions and chrome. Ownership: options are consumed as ordinary config data; no public window resource is exposed.

width.documentation: Initial content width, 240–16384 logical pixels; defaults to 640. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

height.documentation: Initial content height, 160–16384 logical pixels; defaults to 480. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

minWidth.documentation: Minimum content width, 240–initial width; defaults to 240. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

minHeight.documentation: Minimum content height, 160–initial height; defaults to 160. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

titlebar.documentation: Native (default) or custom. Custom currently requires macOS and preserves traffic-light controls. Reserve header space and mark View drag regions. Other desktop platforms return Err; browser hosts keep their own chrome. Creation-time only, not a live mode. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

std:ui.name: withTheme
std:ui.signature: withTheme<T>(node: Node, value: ReadOnly<T>, mode?: string | Signal<string>): Node

parameters.label: node: Node
parameters.documentation: The owned subtree receiving this theme scope.

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Serializable project theme data checked against the theme schema, normally read from tsrust.config.json ui.theme. Borrowed only during this call.

parameters.label: mode?: string | Signal<string>
parameters.documentation: Light or dark, default light. A string Signal switches mode after handlers while preserving child state, fields and identities. Invalid strings throw. This binding retains no state owner.

std:ui.documentation: Scopes project colors, spacing, radius and typography to an owned subtree. Requires every light/dark token. Colors accept #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, checked in-gamut oklch() and @token aliases within the same mode. OKLCH uses lightness/alpha 0–1 or 0–100%, nonnegative unitless chroma and hue 0–360; unsupported syntax, ranges, gamut, unknown tokens, missing references and cycles throw. Resolved background must be opaque; transparent native windows are unsupported. Functional conversion uses renderer float precision; native paint has an 8-bit sRGB boundary, while stored theme strings remain unchanged. spacing.sm/md/lg accepts 0–512 logical pixels; radius accepts 0–256; typography.base/xl accepts 8–128. Unknown keys fail. Returns a Node without rerunning its children or changing their state. Example: import config from './tsrust.config.json'; withTheme(Page(), config.ui.theme, 'dark') uses the project dark palette. Separate trees keep independent themes. Pass a component-local string Signal to switch palettes after handlers without rerunning components, remounting children or losing field values. Nested explicit theme scopes stay independent; transparent conditional roots follow the enclosing scope. Invalid modes throw before replacing the checked palette. Example: const mode = signal("light"); return withTheme(<View><Button onPress={() => mode.set("dark")}>Dark</Button></View>, config.ui.theme, mode); switches after the button press. Theme tokens are read during construction; mutable token-record bindings remain unsupported. Ownership: consumes child nodes; reads and serializes theme data during construction. The resulting subtree owns its checked theme; live mode bindings hold a non-retaining reference to component state.

std:ui.name: ThemeConfig
std:ui.documentation: Project-owned UI token data. Required schemaVersion, light, dark, spacing, radius and typography fields have no implicit missing-token defaults. Pass an imported theme to withTheme(Page(), theme); the subtree uses these values on both backends. Invalid keys, values and aliases produce readable errors. Ownership: readonly data imports are borrowed; clone an import before editing its data.

schemaVersion.documentation: Theme schema identifier. Must be int 1; other values fail validation. Read with theme.schemaVersion; the bundled theme returns 1. Reading does not change the theme. Ownership: copies the scalar.

light.documentation: Semantic colors selected by light mode, the default mode of withTheme. Surface ThemeColors keys are required; syntaxKeyword/String/Number/Type have built-in defaults. For the bundled theme, theme.light.primary is the raw string #2563eb. Reading does not resolve aliases or mutate data. Ownership: borrows the color record.

dark.documentation: Semantic colors selected by withTheme(node, theme, "dark"). Surface ThemeColors keys are required; syntaxKeyword/String/Number/Type have built-in defaults. The bundled theme.dark.background is #0f172a. Reading does not mutate data. Ownership: borrows the color record.

spacing.documentation: Required sm/md/lg spacing scale, 0–512 finite logical pixels per value. p-2/4/6, px-, py- and gap- use these slots; 0 uses zero. theme.spacing.md is 16 in the bundled theme. Both adapters apply display scaling. Ownership: borrows the scale; reading does not mutate it.

radius.documentation: Required sm/md/lg corner scale, 0–256 finite logical pixels. rounded uses md; rounded-sm/lg use the other slots. The bundled theme.radius.md is 8, including rounded button focus geometry. Ownership: borrows the scale; reading does not mutate it. Optional xl selects extra-large corners; omitted falls back to lg.

typography.documentation: Required base/xl text sizes, 8–128 finite logical pixels. text-base/xl select these sizes. theme.typography.xl is 24 in the bundled theme. text-sm derives 14px/20px at base=16. Generic font-sans/serif/mono utilities select platform families; custom named font assets remain unsupported. Ownership: borrows the scale; reading does not mutate it.

std:ui.name: ThemeColors
std:ui.documentation: Required semantic color slots for one mode. Values are raw #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, checked in-gamut oklch() strings or @token aliases in that mode. Aliases accept camelCase or hyphenated semantic names. Both targets resolve the same colors; missing references, cycles, unknown keys, invalid ranges and unsupported gamut fail. Background must resolve opaque. Example: primary: "oklch(0.6 0.12 260 / 0.8)" works with bg-primary/50 at alpha 0.4. Functional conversion uses renderer float precision; native paint uses 8-bit sRGB. Other functional syntaxes, missing components and hue/chroma units are unsupported. Ownership: source strings stay unchanged; readonly imports are borrowed.

background.documentation: Required color for default surface. Accepts #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, in-gamut oklch(L C H / A) or @token in the same mode; no missing-value default. Functional conversion uses renderer float precision; native paint uses 8-bit sRGB. For example, background: "#123456" resolves to sRGB bytes 18, 52, 86. Background must resolve opaque; transparent native windows are unsupported. Reading returns the raw string without changing it; aliases resolve when a theme is applied. Ownership: borrows the string from readonly data.

"Ready" : "Waiting"}</Text></View>; shows Ready on first entry and retains it. Callbacks may update state; updates refresh after the callback without intercepting scrolling. Throwing stops the mounted tree with normal cleanup. Keep layout feedback stable: callbacks which repeatedly hide/show their own view can oscillate. Browser reports are asynchronous; native reports follow layout. Static document() serialization never invokes callbacks. Ownership: the View owns the callback; local component state captures are non-retaining and removed nodes receive no late notifications.

A conditional JSX ternary whose condition reads directly declared component state mounts only its selected branch. Nested branches work. Unchanged selection preserves child state; removal releases it once, and later selection constructs fresh state. Transparent slots add no layout or accessibility element. Empty/absent derived text in containers also contributes no anonymous layout item; explicit Text components keep their own node. For example, <View>{visible.get()?<Text>Ready</Text>:null}</View> shows/hides Ready. Prebuilt owned Nodes cannot be consumed repeatedly from captures; ordinary callback ownership errors apply. Invalid interactive/label/hidden ancestry is checked again after replacement. Pass content between tags or through children={values}; combining both is rejected. Explicit child arrays transfer once and remain subject to ordinary ownership checks.

Ownership: consumes strings and owned children once; bindings do not retain state owners and owning child arrays cannot be cloned.

className.documentation: Optional shared utility string, default empty. <View className="flex-row gap-4" /> uses a horizontal container and project spacing.md between children. Example: <View className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 p-4" /> creates two equal tracks with default 16px gaps/padding. Viewport sm/md/lg/xl/2xl variants use 640/768/1024/1280/1536 logical pixels. Empty means implicit association; missing IDs associate with nothing. No function arguments. Ownership: consumes the ID string.

hidden.documentation: Optional boolean or reactive boolean condition; defaults to false. <View hidden={showCode.get()}>Preview</View> excludes the subtree from layout, paint, pointer/keyboard input and accessibility when true, while retaining its state, callbacks and identities. It becomes visible with its prior values when false. Unlike a conditional JSX branch, hiding does not dispose the subtree. Hidden descendants defer reactive refresh until shown. Errors in the condition propagate. Ownership: retains child owners until the containing tree is released; the condition captures state without retaining its owner.

PageUp/PageDown, Home/End, arrows and Space scroll the focused pane; unused directional deltas bubble to ancestors. Buttons and fields keep their normal behavior. Focus reveals descendants through clipped ancestors. Does not install an activation handler. Focusable containers cannot appear inside Button or aria-hidden ancestry. Ownership: copies the index; retains no focus handle.

Text and empty space drag; buttons, disabled controls, fields and labels exclude dragging. Native titlebars and browser hosts keep their existing window behavior. std:ui.documentation: Accepted controlled field values. Integers preserve all 64 bits, numbers use ordinary number formatting and strings remain Unicode text. No function arguments. `value={9007199254740993}` displays exactly 9007199254740993. Editing returns strings without numeric parsing. Boolean, nullable and resource payloads are unsupported. Ownership: consumes scalar values or non-retaining bindings; application state remains owned by the returned component tree.

std:ui.name: ReactiveInputValue
std:ui.documentation: Compiler-generated value getter used by state-reading JSX value expressions. No public helper call is needed. `<Input value={name.get() + '!'}/>` displays the current name followed by ! after each handler. Input bindings require string, int or number; thrown getters stop and dispose the tree. Ownership: owns the getter callback with non-retaining state captures.

evaluate.documentation: Owned zero-argument getter returning string | int | number without mutating the binding. Compiler-generated `value={name.get()}` reads the current string. Input supports string/int/number results only; errors propagate to control construction/refresh and dispose the tree. Ownership: callback captures state non-retainingly.

std:ui.name: InputTarget
std:ui.documentation: Read-only control snapshot observed during onChange. No constructor or function arguments. `event.target.value` is the new normalized text, not parsed data or an element reference. Snapshot contains value, name and id; no DOM methods. Ownership: handler borrows the snapshot; explicit clones or Signal.set retain copied data.

value.documentation: Normalized committed Unicode field text. Input removes CR/LF; Textarea normalizes CRLF/CR to LF. `event.target.value` is Ada after typing Ada. No numeric parsing, arguments or receiver mutation. Ownership: borrowed snapshot string; copy before retaining.

name.documentation: The field name or empty string when omitted. For <Input name="profile"/>, event.target.name is profile. No arguments or mutation. Ownership: borrowed snapshot string.

id.documentation: The explicit document ID or empty string when omitted. For <Input id="name"/>, event.target.id is name. No arguments or mutation. Ownership: borrowed snapshot string.

std:ui.name: InputChangeEvent
std:ui.documentation: Committed text-change snapshot passed to onChange. No function arguments. `event.target.value` and `event.currentTarget.value` both contain the normalized new text. No DOM references, preventDefault or composition methods are available. A callback returns void and may throw; errors stop the mounted tree. Ownership: borrowed only during callback execution.

target.documentation: Read-only InputTarget snapshot with value, name and id. Direct handlers observe identical target/currentTarget values. `event.target.value` is Ada after a committed Ada edit. No function arguments or receiver mutation. Ownership: borrow lasts for the callback; copy strings to retain them.

currentTarget.documentation: Read-only InputTarget snapshot with value, name and id. Direct handlers observe identical target/currentTarget values. `event.currentTarget.value` is Ada after a committed Ada edit. No function arguments or receiver mutation. Ownership: borrow lasts for the callback; copy strings to retain them.

std:ui.name: TextChild
std:ui.signature: type TextChild = string | int | number | TextBinding | Signal<int> | Signal<number> | Signal<boolean> | Signal<string> | null | undefined
std:ui.documentation: One ordered text child for Text. Strings, exact ints, numbers, TextBinding and direct scalar Signal bindings display in order; null and undefined contribute no characters or placeholder. <Text>A{null}B{undefined}</Text> displays AB. Empty arrays are valid. Bare boolean values and Nodes are not text children. JSX scalar/nullable expressions reading directly declared component state refresh after handlers. Declared top-level or imported scalar helpers participate; unknown/inferred helpers and arbitrary prop-record reads remain snapshots. No function arguments or receiver mutation. Ownership: strings transfer once; Signal bindings do not retain their owner, and owning child arrays cannot be cloned.

std:ui.name: TextBinding
std:ui.documentation: An owned live scalar text expression stored by the existing Text/View/Button children. JSX creates it automatically for supported expressions reading directly declared component state; no helper import or separate component is needed. <Text>{count.get()+1}</Text> displays 2 for count 1, then 3 after count becomes 2. Strings, exact 64-bit ints, numbers and explicit boolean bindings use ordinary formatting; -0 displays 0. Null/undefined getter results contribute no characters. Getters run during construction/refresh and must be pure. A getter error stops the mounted tree and preserves its readable message. There is no public constructor, field or receiver method. Ownership: transfers once with its callback; component-state captures stay weak. It cannot be cloned, reflected or sent to workers.

UiSignal.name: get
UiSignal.documentation: Reads the current scalar value without changing state. Takes no arguments. Returns T; string results are independent snapshots. Example: const label = signal("first"); const old = label.get(); label.set("second"); old remains first. int preserves the full signed 64-bit range; number preserves IEEE-754 values and signed zero. Throws UiError when its component is disposed. Ownership: borrows state; the returned scalar or copied string does not retain state.

UiSignal.name: set

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Required replacement with the same scalar type T. Strings are copied; there is no default.

UiSignal.documentation: Replaces the current state value and returns void. value must have the same int, number, boolean or string type T; no coercion occurs. Reads see the new value immediately; text and disabled bindings refresh after the active handler returns. Example: const label = signal("first"); label.set("second"); label.get(); returns second. int accepts its full signed 64-bit range; checked arithmetic fails before set and leaves state unchanged. number preserves NaN, infinities and signed zero. Throws UiError when its component is disposed. Ownership: borrows state and copies string values; it never extends the owner lifetime.
